title: t18988: fix(approval): framework provenance labels from feedback redispatch no longer...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18988` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `bug` `priority:high`

## Outcome

fix(approval): framework provenance labels from feedback redispatch no longer stale signed issue approvals

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `approval continuity stale label origin:worker source:ci-feedback signed approval` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: no open issue or PR. Same pattern as merged GH#36746 (fix-the-fixer), GH#37762 (needs-maintainer-permissions), GH#37993 (persistent): a trusted framework label transition must not stale a signed approval.
- [x] File refs verified at `main` (`approval-helper-continuity.sh:142-191`, `:608-616`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. Trust-boundary allowlist change plus regression cases in an existing suite.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-14
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (productivity mission session)
- **Conversation context:** Mining pulse dispatch blocks found #37919 retried every cycle since 2026-11-13T01:58Z with `missing_worker_context signal=brief_scope_untrusted_author`, costing 35-67s per attempt. The maintainer had already signed an approval for it. The pulse's own CI feedback route then invalidated that approval.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `bash .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh verify 37919 marcusquinn/aidevops`

**Actual output:**

```text
APPROVAL_REASON: stale-or-unproven-continuity
STALE_APPROVAL
```

Post-approval timeline of #37919. Every mutation was made by the maintainer account (the pulse runner):

```text
20:38 labeled status:available, auto-dispatch, tier:standard; unlabeled needs-maintainer-review   (approval lifecycle, allowed)
23:47 status:queued -> status:in-progress -> status:in-review                                     (dispatch, allowed)
01:58 labeled origin:worker, labeled source:ci-feedback, unlabeled origin:interactive              (CI feedback route, REJECTED)
01:58 unassigned, status:in-review -> status:available                                            (allowed)
```

The three 01:58 provenance events come from `_transition_issue_for_redispatch` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-review.sh:605-642`). They are not in the continuity allowlists, so `_approval_verify_locked_issue_continuity` returns 1 and the approval becomes stale. The body edit (CI feedback section) by the same trusted account is already authenticated by `_approval_continuity_body_edits_authorized`.

## What

A signed issue approval stays valid when an authorized collaborator applies framework provenance labels after signing: `origin:worker`, `origin:interactive`, `origin:worker-takeover`, `source:ci-feedback`, `source:review-feedback`, `source:conflict-feedback`, `source:review-repair`. Any other label change, and any change by an unauthorized actor, still stales the approval.

## Why

Every approved external-contributor issue whose first worker PR fails CI, gets review feedback or conflicts loses its approval through the pulse's own redispatch transition. The issue then needs the maintainer to re-sign with `sudo aidevops approve`, but nothing tells them: the dispatch block reads as `missing_worker_context`. This turns a one-time maintainer decision into a silent permanent block, which costs human time the approval was meant to save.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Narrow allowlist extension following three merged precedents, with mirrored positive and negative regression cases.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh:14-22`: add a provenance label list constant beside `_APPROVAL_OBSERVABILITY_LABEL`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh:142-191`: allow those labels in `allowed_label` (add and remove) in `_approval_continuity_lifecycle_change_allowed`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh:608-616`: accept `labeled`/`unlabeled` events for those labels in the replay loop. The actor authorization below stays in force.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh`: in `test_locked_issue_tier_backfill_continuity` (pattern: the GH#36746 fix-the-fixer cases), replay the #37919 sequence with a trusted actor (VERIFIED) and an untrusted actor (STALE_APPROVAL), and add an unrelated label (`hold-for-review`) case that stays stale.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `approval-helper.sh verify` (`_approval_classify_digest_mismatch`), used by `pulse-dispatch-brief-scope.sh:_brief_scope_signed_approval_valid`, NMR approval gates and `ever-NMR` checks.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none; verification only.
- **Schemas/config:** none. The signed payload format is unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A. Existing stale approvals such as #37919 verify again once the fix is deployed.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Trust boundary:** provenance labels describe who routed work. They never widen the approved title/body, which keep their separate authenticated-edit checks. Every provenance mutation still requires a live admin/maintain/write actor in the ordered replay.
- **Mixed-version:** older runners keep reporting stale until updated. That fails closed.
- **Idempotency/retry:** n/a.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh
bash .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh verify 37919 marcusquinn/aidevops   # after deploy: VERIFIED
```

- **Surface mapping:** content-binding suite covers locked-issue continuity.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A trusted post-approval `origin:worker`/`source:ci-feedback` add and `origin:interactive` removal preserves a locked issue approval (VERIFIED).

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh"
  ```

- [ ] The same events by an untrusted actor stay STALE_APPROVAL.
- [ ] Negative: a trusted `hold-for-review` (non-provenance) label change still stales the approval.
- [ ] After deploy, `approval-helper.sh verify 37919 marcusquinn/aidevops` prints VERIFIED and the pulse dispatches #37919 without a new signature.

## Context & Decisions

- Related: GH#36746, GH#37762, GH#37993 (same allowlist pattern), GH#33097 (authenticated body edits), GH#37052 (signed approval authorizes worker-owned scope discovery).

title: t18989: perf(pulse): routine comment responder resolves runner login once per cycle and skips repos without routine-tracking issues
body:
## Task


1. `dispatch_routine_comment_responses` resolves the runner login once per cycle and passes it to every `scan`/`dispatch` child as `ROUTINE_COMMENT_SELF_LOGIN`.
2. `routine-comment-responder.sh scan` skips a repo for 1 hour (configurable, `ROUTINE_COMMENT_EMPTY_TTL_SECONDS`, default 3600) after a scan found no open `routine-tracking` issues.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `gh api user identity cache trust boundary collaborator permission cache quota` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: GH#38242 / PR #38247 (merged) cached `/user`, commit-by-SHA and per-process permission reads for `pulse-merge-routine.sh` only. GH#38273 covers moving reads to a GitHub App. GH#37888 covers unattributed same-login drain. None covers the routine comment responder.
- [x] File refs verified at `main` (`routine-comment-responder.sh:33-36,132-151`, `pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh:946-984`, `pulse-ancillary-dispatch-core.sh:203-210`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple`. Two files, a single-value env pass-through plus a negative-result stamp, with an existing test file to extend.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-14
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (productivity mission session)
- **Conversation context:** At 13:10Z the pulse cycle ended `outcome=blocked blocker=rest-core-quota dispatched=0 workers=0/20`. REST core had 0/5000 remaining. Attributing the exhausted hour showed the routine comment responder spending one identity read per pulse-enabled repo per cycle.

## Reproducer

```bash
awk -F'\t' '$5=="rest-core" && $9=="attempt" && $2=="routine-comment-responder.sh" {n[$25]++} END {for (x in n) print n[x], x}' ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log
```

**Actual (2026-11-14 09:53Z-13:11Z, 70 pulse-enabled repos):** 280 `GET user` calls, about 84 per hour, plus about 94 per hour logical `rest-core-selected` reads from the per-repo `gh issue list --label routine-tracking`. Together they use about 3.5% of the 5,000/h PAT budget every hour. Most repos have no open `routine-tracking` issues.

## What

1. `dispatch_routine_comment_responses` resolves the runner login once per cycle and passes it to every `scan`/`dispatch` child as `ROUTINE_COMMENT_SELF_LOGIN`.
2. `routine-comment-responder.sh scan` skips a repo for 1 hour (configurable, `ROUTINE_COMMENT_EMPTY_TTL_SECONDS`, default 3600) after a scan found no open `routine-tracking` issues.

## Why

Pulse cycles are stopping at REST core exhaustion with all 20 worker slots idle. Every repeated read that cannot change within a cycle delays worker dispatch for every repo.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** Env pass-through with a validated fallback, plus a stamp-file skip. No trust-boundary change: the login is the same credential's own identity, resolved by the same process tree in the same cycle.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/routine-comment-responder.sh:33-36`: `_get_self_login` returns `ROUTINE_COMMENT_SELF_LOGIN` when it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9-]{0,37}[A-Za-z0-9])?$`, otherwise it keeps the current `gh api user` call.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/routine-comment-responder.sh:143-151`: before `gh issue list`, skip the repo when `${STATE_DIR}/${slug//\//_}_empty.stamp` is younger than the TTL (use `_file_mtime_epoch` from `portable-stat.sh`, or `find -mmin`). Touch the stamp when the list is empty. Remove it when the list is non-empty. A failed list call writes no stamp.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh:946-977`: resolve the login once before the repo loop. Reuse `_DISPATCH_SELF_LOGIN` (exported at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:895`) when set, else `_foss_current_gh_login` (`pulse-ancillary-dispatch-core.sh:203`). Pass `ROUTINE_COMMENT_SELF_LOGIN="$login"` on the `bash "$responder" scan ...` and `dispatch ...` invocations.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-comment-responder-ops-filter.sh`: add cases using its existing gh stub: (a) with `ROUTINE_COMMENT_SELF_LOGIN` set, `scan` makes no `api user` call; (b) a second scan within the TTL after an empty list makes no `issue list` call.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/routine-comment-responder.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-comment-responder-ops-filter.sh`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh:715` calls `dispatch_routine_comment_responses || true`; unchanged.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** new `*_empty.stamp` files in the existing `ROUTINE_COMMENT_STATE_DIR`.
- **Schemas/config:** new optional env `ROUTINE_COMMENT_SELF_LOGIN`, `ROUTINE_COMMENT_EMPTY_TTL_SECONDS`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert; stale stamps only delay one scan by at most the TTL.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-routine-comment-responder-ops-filter.sh`, `test-routine-comment-responder-trust.sh`, `test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Trust boundary:** unchanged. The responder still compares comment authors against the runner's own login; an invalid env value falls back to the live read.
- **Latency:** a newly created `routine-tracking` issue in a previously empty repo is scanned at most one TTL later. Comments on routine issues are not latency-critical.
- **Bash 3.2:** no associative arrays.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-comment-responder-ops-filter.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-comment-responder-trust.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/routine-comment-responder.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** responder tests cover scan/dispatch; stage-wiring covers the pulse call site.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `ROUTINE_COMMENT_SELF_LOGIN` set to a valid login, `scan` performs no `gh api user` call.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-comment-responder-ops-filter.sh"
  ```

- [ ] A repo whose last scan found no open `routine-tracking` issues is not listed again within the TTL; a failed list never writes the stamp.
- [ ] After deploy, `routine-comment-responder.sh` `GET user` attempts in `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` drop from about 84/h to at most about 1 per pulse cycle.

## Context & Decisions

- Related: GH#38242 (merge-routine read caching), GH#38273 (App read routing), GH#37888 (unattributed drain).
- Cross-process caching of collaborator permissions stays out of scope (GH#38242 decision: it would delay revocation).

</details>

title: t18990: perf(pulse-merge): verify GH#38242 permission memo survives merge-routine sub...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18990` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `feat` `fix-the-fixer` `priority:medium`

## Outcome

perf(pulse-merge): verify GH#38242 permission memo survives merge-routine subshells; share it per run

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `collaborator permission memo per-process merge routine quota` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: GH#38242 / PR #38247 (merged 2026-11-14 09:47Z, released in v3.39.192 at 11:13Z) added the per-process memo in `_gh_collaborator_permission_lookup`. No issue covers verifying that it takes effect.
- [x] File refs verified at `main` (`shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh:306-357`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. Diagnosis first, then a narrow fix inside one trust-boundary helper.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-14
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (productivity mission session)
- **Conversation context:** Pulse cycle at 13:10Z ended `blocker=rest-core-quota dispatched=0`. Attributing that hour found `pulse-merge-routine.sh` still spending 131 `collaborators/:u/permission` reads (stage `collaborator-permission-rest`, which only `shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh:265` sets), after the GH#38242 memo was deployed.

## Reproducer

```bash
awk -F'\t' '$1>=1794650000 && $5=="rest-core" && $9=="attempt" && $2=="pulse-merge-routine.sh" && $25 ~ /permission$/ {b=int(($1-1794650000)/1800); n[b]++} END {for (x in n) print x, n[x]}' ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log | sort -n
```

**Actual (30-minute buckets from 09:53Z; v3.39.192 deployed around bucket 3):** 65, 77, 26 before; 72, 56, 75 after. There was no visible drop. The same buckets for `commits/:id` fell only from about 49 to about 28, and `/user` stayed at 8-23 per bucket.

Process tree observed during one run: `pulse-merge-routine.sh run` (pid A) → child subshell (pid B, alive for the whole run) → further nested subshells per PR. Memo writes made inside a `$(...)` substitution or a pipeline/loop subshell are discarded when that subshell exits.

## What

1. **Verify the premise first.** Add one summary log line per routine run, `collab_memo hits=N misses=M`, to `pulse-merge-routine.sh`'s runner log. Measure one run. If misses are mostly distinct `(repo, login)` pairs, the memo is working and the volume is real. In that case, close with the measurement and stop.
2. **If the memo is being lost in subshells,** back it with a per-run scratch file. Create it under the routine's existing temp area at run start, export its path, append successful lookups, and delete it in the routine's EXIT trap. Subshells then share hits within one run. The next run still observes revocation, which keeps the GH#38242 decision intact.

## Why

REST core quota is the current ceiling on unattended throughput: at 0 remaining the pulse dispatches no workers at all. A memo that does not survive the routine's own process structure gives no saving and hides the real cost.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The fix touches a `#aidevops:trust-boundary` helper. It must keep "only successful lookups, never across runs" semantics and needs mirrored hit/miss tests.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh:306-357`: count hits and misses. When `AIDEVOPS_GH_COLLAB_MEMO_FILE` is set and is a regular file owned by the current user, read and append memo entries there as well as the in-process variable. Keep failures, deferrals and fallback/retry routes unmemoized.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh` (run path around `_pmr_acquire_lock`, `:421-445`): create the memo file with `mktemp` after the lock is acquired. Export it, remove it in the existing EXIT trap, and log the hit/miss summary at run end.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-gh-collaborator-permission-cache.sh`: add (a) a lookup inside `$(...)` followed by a parent lookup for the same key makes one API call when the memo file is set; (b) a failed lookup is not written to the file; (c) without the env var, behaviour is unchanged.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-gh-collaborator-permission-cache.sh`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** every `_gh_collaborator_permission_lookup` / `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority` caller. Outside the merge routine the env var is unset, so behaviour is unchanged.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** one per-run temp file, mode 600, deleted on exit.
- **Schemas/config:** new internal env `AIDEVOPS_GH_COLLAB_MEMO_FILE`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** EXIT trap; revert the PR.
- **Existing verification/tests:** the GH#38242 tests added in PR #38247.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Trust boundary:** revocation is observed by the next run, the same as today. A run lasts minutes. Do not add any cross-run TTL cache (GH#38242 decision).
- **File safety:** refuse a memo path that is a symlink, is not owned by the current user, or is outside the temp root.
- **Bash 3.2:** no associative arrays.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-gh-collaborator-permission-cache.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh
```

title: t18991: perf(review-threads): route valid findings owned by another managed repo upstream instead of parking PRs for maintainer attention
body:
## Task


When a review-thread finding is valid but its fix belongs in a different repository that aidevops manages, the PR should not wait for a human. The finding should become a worker-ready issue in the owning repository, the thread should get an in-thread reply linking that issue and be resolved, and the PR should proceed through its normal merge gates.

1. New scanner subcommand: `pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh route-upstream <repo_slug> <pr_number> <thread_id> <owner_repo> <details_file>`.
- `owner_repo` must be an `initialized_repos[]` entry in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` with `pulse: true` and no `local_only: true`, and must differ from `repo_slug`. Compare case-insensitively. The registry is the trust source; worker text is not. Otherwise exit non-zero with a clear message, so the worker falls back to `mark-blocked`.
- `thread_id` must be one of the PR's currently assigned thread IDs.
- Create or reuse the issue in `owner_repo`. Use the framework issue wrapper so origin labels and the signature apply; never raw `gh issue create`. Labels: `auto-dispatch`, a tier label, `bug`. Dedupe with a body marker `<!-- aidevops:upstream-route:<repo_slug>#<pr_number>:<thread_id> -->`. The body carries the sanitized `details_file` (files, the defect, and the verification suggested by the worker) and a back-link to the PR thread. Print the issue URL on stdout.
- Log `route-upstream: <repo_slug>#<pr_number> thread=<id> -> <owner_repo>#<n>`.
2. Worker prompt (`:1141-1170`): add a classification bullet. "If the defect is real but the cited file is owned by another repository (synced/vendored core file, template-owned path), run `route-upstream` for that thread. Reply in-thread with the printed issue link and note that the fix will arrive via the owning repository's next sync. Then resolve the thread. If `route-upstream` refuses, use `mark-blocked decision`." Keep the existing rule that the scanner never resolves threads itself; the worker resolves after replying.
3. `cmd_mark_blocked`: as with `_prrts_is_capacity_reason` (GH#37926), refuse reasons matching `*upstream*`, `*belongs_in_*`, or `*starter*` when `blocked_by` is `decision` or `code`. Tell the worker to use `route-upstream`. A worker that tries to park for this reason is redirected instead of silently parking.
4. Bump `PRRTS_WORKER_CONTRACT_VERSION` to `12`. Per `pr-review-thread-response-scanner-state.sh:349-357`, existing same-fingerprint escalations (including #208 and #96 above) retry automatically under the new contract.

When a review-thread finding is valid but its fix belongs in a different repository that aidevops manages, the PR should not wait for a human. The finding should become a worker-ready issue in the owning repository, the thread should get an in-thread reply linking that issue and be resolved, and the PR should proceed through its normal merge gates.

The body carries the sanitized `details_file` (files, the defect, and the verification suggested by the worker) and a back-link to the PR thread. Print the issue URL on stdout.
   - Log `route-upstream: <repo_slug>#<pr_number> thread=<id> -> <owner_repo>#<n>`.
2. Worker prompt (`:1141-1170`): add a classification bullet. "If the defect is real but the cited file is owned by another repository (synced/vendored core file, template-owned path), run `route-upstream` for that thread. Reply in-thread with the printed issue link and note that the fix will arrive via the owning repository's next sync. Then resolve the thread. If `route-upstream` refuses, use `mark-blocked decision`." Keep the existing rule that the scanner never resolves threads itself; the worker resolves after replying.
3. `cmd_mark_blocked`: as with `_prrts_is_capacity_reason` (GH#37926), refuse reasons matching `*upstream*`, `*belongs_in_*`, or `*starter*` when `blocked_by` is `decision` or `code`. Tell the worker to use `route-upstream`. A worker that tries to park for this reason is redirected instead of silently parking.

Parking also has a measured cost. The merge pass re-ran every gate on these heads each cycle, using the pass deadline and REST quota, and the PRs stayed open for most of a day. The upstream defect also stays unfixed for every derived repository until someone files it.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Bounded to one scanner script, its prompt and one test file. The cross-repository write is limited to issue creation in registry-validated, pulse-managed repositories through the existing wrapper.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh`: add `cmd_route_upstream` and its dispatcher case (usage header `:6-16`). Add the prompt bullet (`:1141-1154`) and the terminal-state note (`:1163-1165`). Add the reason refusal next to `_prrts_is_capacity_reason` (`:856-862`) and call it from `cmd_mark_blocked` (`:893-913`). Bump `PRRTS_WORKER_CONTRACT_VERSION` (`:72`).

### Files Scope

### Hazards and Compatibility

title: t18992: fix(pulse-merge): finish interactive PRs left idle by a still-running session
body:
**Task ID:** `t18992` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug` `fix-the-fixer` `priority:high`

## Outcome

fix(pulse-merge): finish interactive PRs left idle by a still-running session — targeted review-thread guard, session-bus idle handover, takeover worktree

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `interactive PR idle handover review-thread worktree ownership` → 0 relevant hits
- [x] Discovery pass: no open issue covers this. GH#36647 (merged #36649) added the `origin:interactive` guard to the repo-wide scan only. t2189 added `_interactive_pr_is_stale`/`_interactive_pr_trigger_handover` for the CI/conflict fix-worker route only.
- [x] File refs verified at `main`: `pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:681-728` (`cmd_scan_pr`, the targeted path; no label guard), `:730-741` (`_prrts_labels_block_response`) and `:771-777` (scan-loop guard), `pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh:271-306` (`_prrts_apply_expected_worktree_owner`) and `:356-376` (reused-worktree path), `pulse-merge.sh:164-214` (`_pulse_merge_dispatch_review_thread_remediation` → `dispatch-pr`), `pulse-merge-conflict.sh:269-387` (`_interactive_pr_is_stale`, Gates 2 and 3 at `:370-380`), `pulse-merge-process.sh:1304-1320` (handover → fix-worker route), `release-lane-liveness.sh:69-86` (bounded `session-bus-helper.sh show --json` liveness read).
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking`. This changes the interactive-ownership boundary across the scanner, the handover detector and worker worktree selection.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-14
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (productivity mission session)
- **Conversation context:** While attributing slow merge passes (GH#38259), wpallstars/seoproanalytics#98 (`origin:interactive`) failed review-thread remediation with `review_worktree_ownership_unverified` 8 times between 07:39Z and 13:44Z, about every 30-80 minutes, and tripped the infrastructure circuit breaker once. It is one unresolved minor CodeRabbit thread (`README.md:577`) plus a `qlty check` ERROR away from merge. The interactive TUI session that claimed #97 (06:04Z) and opened #98 (06:08Z) is still running, with PID alive and claim stamp present. Its session-bus record shows `status=idle` and `last_activity_epoch` at about 06:47Z (7.6h idle), and it has moved on to a different objective. With the current gates, nothing will finish this PR until the user returns to that terminal.

## What

Interactive PRs left idle by a still-running session should reach merge without the user, while keeping GH#36647's rule that workers never write concurrently with an *active* interactive session.

1. **Targeted-path guard (certain defect).** In `cmd_scan_pr` (`dispatch-pr`), apply the same rule as the scan loop. For `origin:interactive` without `origin:worker-takeover`, log `dispatch-pr: <repo>#<n> skipped — interactive PR owned by its session (no worker-takeover)` and return the existing deferred outcome (10) before any worktree work. This stops the misclassified retryable-infrastructure loop. It also closes a latent GH#36647 gap: today, once the owner process exits, this path would launch a worker onto an interactive PR without any handover.
2. **Idle-session handover evidence.** `_interactive_pr_is_stale` treats `status:claimed|in-review` (Gate 2) and an existing claim stamp (Gate 3) as proof of an active human. A long-lived TUI therefore holds a PR indefinitely. Add one evidence path: resolve the stamp's owner session (the claim stamp has `pid` and `worktree_path`; the worktree registry row for that path has `owner_session`), then read it with a bounded `session-bus-helper.sh show <session> --json`, following `release-lane-liveness.sh:69-86`. Treat Gates 2 and 3 as satisfied only when all of these hold: the session's `status=idle`, `last_activity_epoch` is older than `AIDEVOPS_IDLE_SESSION_HANDOVER_SECONDS` (new, default 14400 = 4h), PR activity is older than the same threshold, and the session's current `issue`/`pr` is not this issue or PR. A busy session, recent activity, an unknown or timed-out bus, or a missing mapping keeps the current behaviour (not stale). `no-takeover` still opts out.
3. **Route review-thread blockers through handover.** When the merge pass finds review-thread blockers on an `origin:interactive` PR that item 2 reports as stale, call `_interactive_pr_trigger_handover` (as `pulse-merge-process.sh:1304-1320` already does for CI/conflict) before `dispatch-pr`. Then send one non-waking session-bus `send` notice to the owner session: PR, reason, idle duration, and that adding `no-takeover` reclaims it.
4. **Takeover worktree.** After `origin:worker-takeover`, never transfer or write the live idle owner's worktree. The scanner refuses it today (`:271-306`). Use a worker-owned worktree on the PR head instead. The branch is checked out in the owner's worktree, so verify how `_prrts_prepare_worker_worktree` (`:610`) creates worktrees and use a distinct local branch tracking `origin/<head_ref>` that pushes to `<head_ref>`. The owner's worktree is then stale relative to the remote, which is the normal, recoverable resume case.

## Why

The user launches interactive sessions to go faster. A session that opens a PR and moves on, leaving one minor thread, should not turn that PR into a standing request for user attention. In this case the system knew the session was idle, the PR was one quick fix from merge, and the only gate was a liveness proxy (PID plus claim stamp) that cannot tell "open in a terminal" from "being worked on". Each cycle also re-ran merge gates and the failing remediation for the PR.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** Changes the interactive-ownership trust boundary (GH#36647, t2189) and worktree ownership transfer rules across three scripts. Item 1 alone would be standard.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh`: add the interactive guard to `cmd_scan_pr` (`:681-728`), using the labels already fetched at `:702-708`, so no extra API call.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh`: add the idle-session evidence helper and use it in `_interactive_pr_is_stale` Gates 2 and 3 (`:370-380`). Add the owner notice in `_interactive_pr_trigger_handover` (`:407+`).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`: in `_pulse_merge_dispatch_review_thread_remediation` (`:164-214`), or its review-thread callers (`:216-246`), run stale check → handover before `dispatch-pr` for `origin:interactive` PRs.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh`: takeover-mode worktree selection when the existing worktree has a live owner and the PR carries `origin:worker-takeover`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-dispatch.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh`: add cases.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-dispatch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `pulse-merge.sh` review-thread remediation callers; `pulse-merge-process.sh:1304-1320` (existing handover route, unchanged behaviour); `pulse-merge-author-checks.sh:337-346` (also calls `_interactive_pr_is_stale`; confirm the new evidence path is acceptable there or gate it behind an argument).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `origin:worker-takeover` label plus the one-time handover comment (existing); one session-bus notice; a worker-owned worktree.
- **Schemas/config:** new env `AIDEVOPS_IDLE_SESSION_HANDOVER_SECONDS` (default 14400).
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none. The scanner's existing infrastructure-failure state for such PRs clears on the next deferred outcome.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert; `AIDEVOPS_INTERACTIVE_PR_HANDOVER_MODE=detect` logs would-handover decisions without acting.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-pr-context.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-origin-interactive-auto-merge.sh`, `test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-dispatch.sh`, `test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktrees.sh`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Fail closed:** any missing, unknown or timed-out liveness evidence keeps the PR with its session. A busy session, or one whose current issue/PR is this one, is never handed over.
- **Never write the owner's worktree:** no reset, stash, transfer or checkout in it.
- **Bounded bus call:** reuse the timeout pattern from `release-lane-liveness.sh:45-67`; the merge pass must not block on the bus.
- **Bash 3.2:** no associative arrays; `local var="$1"`; explicit returns.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-pr-context.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-origin-interactive-auto-merge.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-dispatch.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktrees.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** the handover suite covers stale gates; the scanner suites cover the guard and worktree selection.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `dispatch-pr` on an `origin:interactive` PR without `origin:worker-takeover` returns 10 with the skip log and performs no worktree or ownership work.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-dispatch.sh"
  ```

- [ ] `_interactive_pr_is_stale` returns stale for a live-PID claim only when bus evidence shows idle beyond the threshold, both PR and session are idle, and the session is not on this issue or PR. Busy, recent, unknown or mapping-missing cases return not-stale.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh"
  ```

- [ ] After handover, the review-thread worker uses a worker-owned worktree and pushes to the PR head without touching the owner's worktree.
- [ ] After deploy: wpallstars/seoproanalytics#98, or the next PR in the same situation, stops logging `review_worktree_ownership_unverified` every cycle. It is either handed over and merged, or shows an evidenced different blocker, and the owner session receives one notice.

## Context & Decisions

- GH#36647 keeps workers off interactive PRs to prevent head drift and surprise commits. This preserves that rule for active sessions and narrows "active" from "process exists" to "process exists and is not idle beyond the threshold".
- The 4h default (versus 12h for PR-age-only handover) is justified by the double signal: PR idle and session idle. `no-takeover` remains the explicit opt-out.
- Related: GH#38259 (merge-pass attribution that surfaced this), GH#38290 (upstream routing of review findings).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

title: fix(opencode-service): do not quote WorkingDirectory in Linux unit
body:
## Summary

Linux unit generation for `aidevops-opencode-server.service` quotes `WorkingDirectory` via `systemd_quote()`. systemd treats the quotes as part of the path, so the unit fails to load with:

`WorkingDirectory= path is not absolute: "<home>"`
`Unit configuration has fatal error, unit will not be started.`

## Evidence

- Observed on a Linux user systemd host on 2026-11-14.
- Generator `definition_bytes()` emitted `WorkingDirectory="<absolute-home>"`.
- `systemctl --user status` reported `Loaded: bad-setting` until the live unit was rewritten without quotes.
- `ExecStart=` and `Environment=` quoting is fine; only `WorkingDirectory=` must be an unquoted absolute path.

## Fix

### Files Scope
- `scripts/opencode_service_state.py`
- `scripts/tests/test_opencode_service.py`

In `definition_bytes()` for Linux use:

`WorkingDirectory={str(self.home)}`

not `systemd_quote(str(self.home))`.

Add a regression assert in `test_systemd_escaping_has_no_environment_dollar_expansion`:

- `WorkingDirectory=` + home path is present
- no `WorkingDirectory="` prefix

## Verification

- Generated unit contains unquoted absolute `WorkingDirectory=`
- `systemctl --user daemon-reload` yields `LoadState=loaded` (no bad-setting) when the unit is installed
- Do not enable the service as part of this fix unless an operator explicitly wants managed-server mode

## Local note

Workhorse already has a live unit + deployed generator mitigation. Upstream still needs the fix so the next aidevops update does not reintroduce the bad unit on install/reconcile.

title: fix(release): reconcile exits 8 silently when channel verification is pending after workflow success
body:
## Observed

During the v3.39.193 release (source PR #38302), `aidevops release reconcile 38302` exited `8` twice after the publish workflow (run 43617946234) had already concluded `success`. Both times the last release line was `WORKFLOW_STATUS=completed` / `WORKFLOW_URL=...`. Nothing said which gate was still pending.

Manual checks at the time showed:
- the GitHub release was published and not a draft
- npm `aidevops@3.39.193` existed, with `dist.attestations.provenance.predicateType = https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`
- the Homebrew formula URL and sha256 matched the tag tarball exactly
- `postflight.yml` run "Postflight Verification v3.39.193" had concluded `success`

A manual `npm audit signatures --json --include-attestations` then passed (0 invalid, 0 missing, 2 bundles). The next reconcile printed all channel lines and `release:published`. The most likely cause is a short delay before npm attestations became available. During that window, `_full_loop_release_verify_channels` returned non-zero and `_full_loop_release_unverified_channels_action` returned `8`, waiting out the 900 s success grace.

## Problem

`_full_loop_release_verify_channels` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:1038`) returns `1` at many points without printing anything: GitHub release, npm metadata, npm provenance/audit, Homebrew formula fetch, tarball sha and formula comparison. The operator can't tell which channel is pending, so they have to debug the channel checks by hand.

## Proposed fix

- In `_full_loop_release_verify_channels` and `_full_loop_release_verify_npm_provenance`, set or print a `CHANNEL_PENDING=<github-release|npm-metadata|npm-provenance|homebrew-formula|homebrew-sha>` line before each failing return.
- In `_full_loop_release_unverified_channels_action` (`:1137`), when returning `8` within the grace, print `RELEASE_WAIT=channel-propagation retry_after=<updated_at+900>`.
- Do not change exit codes or dispatch behaviour.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:912-1075, 1137-1162`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` (existing harness; assert the new line on an unverified-channel path)
- `.agents/workflows/release.md` Troubleshooting table: add a row for `CHANNEL_PENDING`

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/release.md`

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`

body:
**Task ID:** `t18997` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `feat`

## Outcome

feat(recovery): maintainer replies on held issues wake the AI supervisor; unexplained holds get a stated why

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Discovery pass: no wake path exists for a maintainer answer on a `hold-for-review` issue. Dispatch (`dispatch-dedup-assignment.sh` `_is_assigned_check_hold_for_review`), terminal-blocker recovery (`_TBR_OTHER_HOLDS_JQ`) and unclassified intake (GH#37978) all exclude the label; `_health_aged_hold_section` (GH#36788) only displays it.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking`. This changes a maintainer-trust boundary: which comments the recovery supervisor may carry out.

## What

Let a maintainer settle a held issue with a plain reply on that issue, and let pulse carry out the reply without an interactive session:

1. **Maintainer reply on a `hold-for-review` issue**: queue it for the runner-local AI recovery supervisor (new intake `answered_hold`), which carries out exactly what the reply decides and posts one receipt.
2. **`hold-for-review` with no stated reason** (no trusted comment around or after the label for a day): queue it for the runner that applied the label (intake `unexplained_hold`). That supervisor posts one decision packet, or a pointer to the issue that holds the decision. A blocked label is not an instruction, so it still needs a why.
3. **Maintainer reply after a recorded `human_decision`** (any terminal-blocker recovery intake): end the 24h decision suppression early so the owning supervisor re-assesses on its next pass instead of the next day.
4. **Supervisor dashboard**: show the ask from the newest trusted decision comment even when it does not use the exact words "Recommended path", and tell the maintainer that a reply on the issue is enough.

## Why

- `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md:34` stated it directly: "nothing lifts that label when the answer arrives". Today the only way to act on a hold is an interactive session. That spends the maintainer's scarcest resource twice: once to decide and once to have the decision carried out.
- Evidence from 2026-11-14, one supervisor runner and one managed repo: the dashboard reported 47 maintainer-decision holds older than 3 days. All 10 visible rows said "No decision comment yet", although the issues did carry decision comments (`**Owner/action:**`, `**Unblock evidence:**`, pointers to the deciding issue). Of 57 open holds, 53 had no comment containing "Recommended path", and 10 had no trusted comment at all. Every post-hold maintainer comment was an interactive-session note.
- On this runner, 46 of 75 terminal-blocker recovery decisions were `wake: human_decision`. Each one suppressed re-assessment for 24h, even after the maintainer answered.

## How

1. New sourced module `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-holds.sh`, stage `holds` run from `tbr_pending` after seed and before the unclassified stage, in the supervisor pass only, never `rearm`. For each pulse repo, at most every `BLOCKER_RECOVERY_HOLD_INTERVAL` (default 3600s): list open `hold-for-review` issues (GraphQL), skip trust-gate and claim labels, skip unchanged issues by an `updatedAt|due|handled` memo, then read label events and comments.
   - `answered_hold`: this runner's own OWNER/MEMBER login commented after the latest hold label, with no signature footer, automation marker, trusted `<!-- aidevops:hold-reply:<id> -->` receipt or handled memo.
   - `unexplained_hold`: this runner's login applied the label more than `BLOCKER_RECOVERY_HOLD_EXPLAIN_AGE` (default 86400s) ago and no trusted non-notice comment exists from one hour before the label onward.
   - The stage writes nothing to GitHub.
2. `_tbr_check_hold_entry`: retire when the hold or its intake no longer matches, or once a decision is recorded after queueing (then memo the reply id). Print the usual JSON line with `reply_comment_id` and no local excerpts.
3. `_tbr_decision_active`: a recorded `human_decision` is inactive when a plain OWNER/MEMBER (or self) comment is newer than `recorded_epoch`.
4. Supervisor prompt (`pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`) and `worker-discipline.md` "Maintainer replies on held issues": carry out exactly what the reply decides (revise/resume, retire, keep holding, answer once, or record a non-decision notice), post one receipt for public outcomes, record the decision; post a decision packet for `unexplained_hold`.
5. Dashboard: `_health_hold_recommendation` reads `Recommended path`, `Decision needed`, `Specific question`, `Owner/action`, `Owner/next action`, `Next action` and decision pointers; `_health_aged_hold_section` says a reply on the issue is enough.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-holds.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard-issue.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-discovery.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-health-dashboard-identity-aliases.sh`

## Acceptance

- An unsigned own-login OWNER/MEMBER reply after the hold label is queued as `answered_hold` with its comment id. Not queued: a signed or `origin:worker` comment, another login's comment, a collaborator-association own-login comment, a comment before the hold label, a reply with a trusted receipt, an issue with `status:claimed` or `needs-maintainer-review`.
- A hold this runner applied more than a day ago, with no trusted comment from an hour before the label onward, is queued as `unexplained_hold`; not when another login applied it or a comment explains it.
- `rearm` never lists, reads or queues holds. The stage performs no GitHub write.
- A recorded decision retires the entry; the same reply is not queued again; a newer reply is.
- A maintainer reply newer than a recorded `human_decision` makes `_tbr_decision_active` false; a signed or older comment does not.
- The dashboard row shows `Owner/action` text and `Decision on #N`; "Recommended path" extraction still works.
- ShellCheck is clean; the terminal-blocker and dashboard suites pass.

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-health-dashboard-identity-aliases.sh
```

Register NetBird's self-hosted management MCP (`https://<management>/api/mcp`) as an on-demand aidevops MCP named `netbird`:

1. `netbird-mcp-launcher.sh` bridges the endpoint to stdio with pinned `mcp-remote@0.16.6` (`--transport http-only`). It resolves the token secret from `NETBIRD_MCP_SECRET` or `aidevops secret default netbird`, and the URL from `NETBIRD_MCP_URL` or the credential-registry account name (hostname). `aidevops secret NAME --` injects the token; mcp-remote expands `${NAME}` in `--header` itself, so the value never reaches argv or config.
2. Registry entry: disabled by default, activation agent `netbird` from `services/networking/netbird.md`, exact `allowedTools` = the 33 read-only NetBird 0.83.1 tools (mirrors the Cloudron guide's `NB_MCP_TOOLS` set), so write tools are denied client-side even if the server exposes them.
3. Doc section in `netbird.md`: setup with an Auditor service-user token, secret/account/default commands, dry-run validation, overrides and the rights caveat.

## Why

NetBird 0.83 added an embedded MCP server. A secret-injecting launcher keeps self-hosted URLs and tokens out of shared config, and the read-only allowlist matches the best-practice "read first" guidance.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Follows two existing registry patterns exactly; no changes to shared plugin logic.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/netbird-mcp-launcher.sh`: model on `.agents/scripts/backblaze-b2-mcp-launcher.sh` (dry-run env, explicit returns, `exec aidevops secret … --`).
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs`: entry after `backblaze-b2`, `allowedTools` as in `mobile-mcp`.
- `EDIT: .agents/services/networking/netbird.md`: `mcp: [netbird]` frontmatter and "MCP Server (aidevops `netbird`)" section.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs`: registration/permission assertions.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/netbird-mcp-launcher.sh`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs`
- `.agents/services/networking/netbird.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18998-brief.md`
- `TODO.md`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `registerMcpServers`, `registerOnDemandMcpAgents`, `aidevops_mcp` name enum (derived from the registry).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none beyond generated OpenCode config.
- **Schemas/config:** none new; env overrides `NETBIRD_MCP_SECRET`, `NETBIRD_MCP_URL`, `NETBIRD_MCP_LAUNCHER_DRY_RUN`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts` and the plugin.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert; the entry is disabled until connected.
- **Existing verification/tests:** plugin `node --test` suite.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- `aidevops secret inventory` fails closed on non-conforming gopass names, so the launcher uses `resolve`/`check`/`describe` instead.
- `agent-mcp-tools.mjs` is intentionally not extended: its wildcard grant would widen the exact allowlist (same as `mobile-mcp`).

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/
shellcheck .agents/scripts/netbird-mcp-launcher.sh
NETBIRD_MCP_LAUNCHER_DRY_RUN=1 bash .agents/scripts/netbird-mcp-launcher.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** registry/permission assertions in `test-mcp-activation.mjs`; launcher validated by dry run and a live stdio probe.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `config.mcp.netbird` is a disabled local entry pointing at the launcher; `netbird_*` denied with the 33 read tools allowed on the `netbird` agent.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs"
  ```

- [x] Live stdio probe against a 0.83.1 server with an Auditor service-user token: `initialize` → `netbird-management`, `tools/list` → 33 tools, no write tools, `list_peers` succeeds.
- [x] ShellCheck clean.

## Context & Decisions

- Cloudron package guide: marcusquinn/cloudron-netbird-app `docs/MCP-SERVER.md` (v2.7.5).
- OAuth via mcp-remote is possible but sessions are lost on every app restart (in-memory store); a PAT is the stable unattended path. The Auditor role, not the tool list, is what blocks REST writes with that token.

title: t18999: fix(full-loop): merge helper should reconcile a release-provenance PR that native auto-merge lands mid-run
body:
## Task


`full-loop-helper.sh merge <release-PR>` fails closed with `PR #N is not open` when GitHub native auto-merge lands the protected release PR (`chore/release-vX.Y.Z-provenance`) while the helper is running. The helper should then take its existing already-merged path (`_merge_handle_already_merged_provenance`: verify the merge SHA, no merge write, reconcile the source lane) instead of failing.

GH#34839 added that path for a PR that was already merged **before** the helper started. This issue covers the remaining time-of-check race: the PR is open at that first check and merged before the readiness gate.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`full-loop-helper.sh merge <release-PR>` fails closed with `PR #N is not open` when GitHub native auto-merge lands the protected release PR (`chore/release-vX.Y.Z-provenance`) while the helper is running. The helper should then take its existing already-merged path (`_merge_handle_already_merged_provenance`: verify the merge SHA, no merge write, reconcile the source lane) instead of failing.

GH#34839 added that path for a PR that was already merged **before** the helper started. This issue covers the remaining time-of-check race: the PR is open at that first check and merged before the readiness gate.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-14 on release v3.39.194 (release PR #38314, source PR #38312):

- `wait-checks 38314` returned PASS when the last required check finished.
- `merge 38314` started at 18:38:38Z. `_merge_handle_already_merged_provenance` read the PR while it was still open and returned 2 (not applicable).
- Native auto-merge (armed by the release helper, method MERGE) merged at 18:38:55Z.
- The readiness gate (`_full_loop_verify_pr_readiness`, `full-loop-helper-readiness.sh:446`) then read `state=CLOSED` and the helper exited 1 at 18:38:59Z: `PR #38314 is not open` / `Merge blocked by the pre-merge safety gate`.
- The documented fallback `aidevops release reconcile 38312` worked, but `workflows/release.md` says the merge helper "also handles a PR already merged by native auto-merge without another merge write".

Auto-merge fires as soon as the last required check succeeds, which is exactly when `wait-checks` returns. So this race is likely the common case for every protected release, not a rare one. Each hit adds a failed command, a manual diagnosis and a fallback step to every release close-out.

## How

1. In `cmd_merge` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`, around the `_merge_handle_already_merged_provenance` call at ~line 1798), when the later pre-merge readiness/gate step fails, re-run `_merge_handle_already_merged_provenance "$pr_number" "$repo"` once. If it returns 0 or 1, return that status; if 2, keep the original failure. Keep the ordinary-PR behaviour fail-closed: the function already returns 2 for anything that is not a merged same-repo `chore/release-v*-provenance` PR into `main`.
2. Alternative with the same effect: have the readiness gate's `state != "OPEN"` branch call the already-merged handler for provenance heads only. Pick whichever keeps the trust-boundary checks (`#aidevops:trust-boundary` jq at ~line 1552) as the single authority.
3. Keep the reconcile idempotent: `_merge_reconcile_provenance_release` must not run twice in one invocation.
4. `full-loop-helper-readiness.sh` changes only under option 2. Extend the existing merge-helper test that covers `_merge_handle_already_merged_provenance` (find it with `rg -l '_merge_handle_already_merged_provenance' .agents/scripts/tests/`).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`

The merge suite exercises cmd_merge and the existing provenance handler; extend it to cover the mid-readiness race and fail-closed cases. Verify with bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh.

## Acceptance

- A provenance PR that is open at the first check and merged before the readiness gate ends in `LIFECYCLE_STATE=MERGED ... (already merged; no merge write)` and a single source-lane reconcile, exit 0.
- An ordinary PR that closes or merges mid-run still fails closed with `is not open`.
- A provenance PR closed without merging still fails closed.
- ShellCheck is clean; the existing merge-helper tests pass.

## Verification

```bash
rg -l '_merge_handle_already_merged_provenance' .agents/scripts/tests/
bash <that test file>
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh
```

title: secret-helper: one nested gopass state entry (aidevops/<tool>/<id>) aborts the whole inventory and breaks inventory-based MCP launchers
body:
## What

`aidevops secret inventory` aborts the whole inventory with `Invalid secret inventory name` when any gopass entry under `aidevops/` does not match `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$` (`secret-helper.sh` `inventory_add_name`, around line 1222). Nested state entries written by tools that share the prefix trigger it. Observed: `aidevops/netbird-sso/<sha256>`, written by marcusquinn/cloudron-netbird-app `scripts/cloudron-sso.py:218` (documented in that repo's `docs/SSO-SWITCH.md:77`).

Impact: every inventory consumer fails for that user, not just the odd entry. `quickfile-mcp-launcher.sh:65-68` exits with "Unable to read the names-only aidevops secret inventory", so QuickFile MCP cannot start. Any other launcher or audit built on inventory is affected the same way.

## Decide

The fail-closed test in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-secret-helper.sh` (around line 290-300) asserts the abort, so the current behaviour may be deliberate. Two compatible fixes:

1. In `inventory_add_name`, skip entries containing `/` (nested non-env state, which can never be injected as an env var anyway). Keep failing closed on top-level malformed names. Report a skipped count on stderr, with no names.
2. Separately (other repo, not this issue): move `cloudron-sso.py` state out of `aidevops/` to a non-secret prefix, with a read fallback for existing state.

Recommendation: 1, because it fixes every consumer at once and keeps the guard for names that could be injected.

## Files

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` (`inventory_add_name` and its caller)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-secret-helper.sh` (add a nested-entry case; keep the malformed top-level case failing)

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-secret-helper.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] With a gopass fixture holding `aidevops/GOOD_NAME` and `aidevops/tool-state/abc`, `inventory` exits 0 and lists only `GOOD_NAME`.
- [ ] A top-level `aidevops/bad-name` still fails closed with the existing error.

title: install-hooks-helper self-test fails on invalid-session-identity, skipping git hook installation
body:
## Description

`install-hooks-helper.sh install` aborts at its self-test on 3.39.194, so the
git hook installers that run after the self-test (`install_gh_wrapper_guard_hook`,
`install_pre_commit_hook`, `install_pre_push_quality_hook`,
`install_markdoc_validate_hook`) never run. A freshly initialized repo is left
without the pre-commit quality hook and without the gh-wrapper/quality pre-push
chain, while `aidevops init` reports success.

Reproduces from any cwd (`install-hooks-helper.sh test`):

```text
FAIL: should allow in linked worktree: git checkout -b linked-branch
FAIL: should allow in linked worktree: git checkout --orphan linked-pages
2 tests failed, 22 passed
```

Running the guard directly in the self-test fixture's linked worktree shows the
cause:

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "deny",
 "permissionDecisionReason": "BLOCKED: lifecycle owner admission unavailable (invalid-session-identity)"}}
```

The self-test fixture (`_test_hook_run`, `install-hooks-helper.sh:1735`) passes
no session identity, and lifecycle owner admission now denies branch creation
without one. The linked-worktree "allowed" cases therefore can never pass.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh` — `_test_hook_run` (~L1735),
  `_test_hook_run_linked_worktree_cases` (~L1829), `install_hook` (~L948: the
  `test_hook || return 1` gate placed before the git hook installers at ~L963-972).
- `.agents/hooks/git_safety_lifecycle.py` / `git_safety_guard.py` — admission
  path that returns `invalid-session-identity`.

## Suggested fix

1. Give the self-test fixture a valid synthetic session identity (or a test-only
   admission env that the lifecycle adapter honours only for the fixture's temp
   repos registry), so the linked-worktree allow cases exercise branch policy
   rather than admission.
2. Install the repository git hooks independently of the Claude PreToolUse
   self-test result (or report the self-test failure without skipping them), so
   a Claude settings problem cannot silently leave repos without git hooks.

## Secondary observation

`aidevops_hook_status` with `workdir` set to a linked worktree reported
`pre-commit: missing` and `pre-push` without markers, while the same call on the
canonical checkout (shared `.git/hooks`, `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`
resolves there, no `core.hooksPath`) reported both hooks with all markers.
The linked-worktree view appears to read a different location.

## Workaround used

Sourced the helper and called the three installers directly (the pattern in
`tests/test-hooks-path-coexistence.sh` `run_helper_pre_push`). Hooks then
installed and chained into the repo-verify pre-push dispatcher correctly.

## Verification

- `install-hooks-helper.sh test` reports all tests passing.
- After `aidevops init` in a new repo, `install-hooks-helper.sh install` leaves
  pre-commit (quality marker) and pre-push (gh-wrapper + quality markers) present.
- `aidevops_hook_status` reports the same markers from a linked worktree and from
  its canonical checkout.

title: t19000: gh-api-instrument: label normal-mode native REST attempts with method/class/family
body:
## Task


Native REST attempt rows written by the default (non-exact-capture) transport path carry `request_method`, `endpoint_class` and `endpoint_family` = `unknown` (log columns 23–25), so `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh api-budget` still reports a large `unknown` REST family. Derive these three labels statically from the `gh api` argv on that path, using the same allowlisted classes and families as `gh_quota_debug_request.py`, without an extra process fork per call.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Native REST attempt rows written by the default (non-exact-capture) transport path carry `request_method`, `endpoint_class` and `endpoint_family` = `unknown` (log columns 23–25), so `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh api-budget` still reports a large `unknown` REST family. Derive these three labels statically from the `gh api` argv on that path, using the same allowlisted classes and families as `gh_quota_debug_request.py`, without an extra process fork per call.

## Why

Deliverable 3 of #37888. In the last 40,000 local log rows, about 690 of about 6,600 REST attempt rows (~10%) are unlabeled. All of them share route `rest-core-selected` with no HTTP status and no remaining-quota field, the signature of `gh_run_transport_attempt` in normal mode (`gh-api-instrument.sh`, the final `gh_record_attempt` call). That call never passes the method/class/family arguments; only the exact-capture frame writers in `gh-quota-attribution-lib.sh` do. Affected callers include `pulse-merge-routine.sh`, `gh_api_rest`, `pulse-wrapper.sh`, `full-loop-helper.sh`, `interactive-session-helper.sh` and `stats-wrapper.sh`.

## How

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh

### Steps

1. Add a pure-Bash classifier (Bash 3.2 compatible, no forks) that reads the argv of one `gh api` invocation. It finds the endpoint positional (skipping value-taking flags such as `-X/--method`, `-H/--header`, `-f/--raw-field`, `-F/--field`, `--input`, `-q/--jq`, `-t/--template`, `--cache`, `--hostname`, `-p/--preview`, including `--flag=value` forms). It derives the method: an explicit `-X/--method`, otherwise POST when field or input flags are present, otherwise GET. It maps the endpoint through the `ROOT_CLASSES` / `REPO_CLASSES` allowlist and the family pattern in `gh_quota_debug_request.py`.
2. In `gh_run_transport_attempt` normal mode, pass the three labels to `gh_record_attempt` (positional arguments 20–22). Non-`api` subcommands and unparseable argv stay `unknown`; never record raw paths, owners, repositories, IDs or query strings.
3. Add focused cases to `test-gh-api-instrument.sh`: a repo issues read, an explicit-method write, a field-implied POST, a root class, and a non-api command that must remain `unknown`, plus an assertion that no private path text is recorded.

## Acceptance

- Normal-mode `gh api` attempt rows record method/class/family matching the exact-capture classifier for the same endpoint.
- Non-`api` commands and unrecognized endpoints remain `unknown`/`other`, and no raw request target is written.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh` passes; ShellCheck is clean.

## Related

Ref #37888 (the consolidated spec; its operational post-fix reset-window criteria stay open there).

title: dependabot-alert-monitor.sh creates duplicate issues for one package when its alerts have different patched versions
body:
## Observed

On 2026-11-14 (aidevops v3.39.192), Dependabot alerts were enabled on a managed private repo with 230 open alerts. The first pulse cycle's `dependabot_alert_monitor` stage created, seconds apart:

- two open issues titled `Remediate dependency alert: Pillow (pip)`
- two open issues titled `Remediate dependency alert: aiohttp (pip)`

All carry `auto-dispatch`, so workers can open competing PRs against the same lockfile.

## Cause (from reading the script)

File: `.agents/scripts/dependabot-alert-monitor.sh`

1. `_dam_fetch_alert_groups` (jq, about lines 143-165) groups by `[package, ecosystem, patched]`. One package with alerts fixed in different versions becomes several groups.
2. `_dam_issue_title` (about line 169) uses only package and ecosystem, so those groups share one title.
3. `_dam_issue_exists` (about line 181) dedupes with `gh issue list --search "\"<title>\" in:title"`. GitHub search indexing lags, so an issue created moments earlier in the same loop is not found and the next group creates a duplicate.

## Scale

In that repo, 230 alerts formed 64 groups (30 distinct packages). 165 of the alerts came from a single `uv.lock`. Every group becomes its own auto-dispatch issue, and many of them edit the same lockfile.

## Suggested fix

- Group by `[package, ecosystem]` and carry the highest `first_patched_version` across that package's alerts, so one upgrade covers all of them. Or keep an in-run set of titles already created and check it before `_dam_issue_exists`.
- Optional: when one manifest/lockfile has many alerts, file one issue per lockfile (or cap new issues per repo per cycle) to avoid many parallel PRs conflicting on the same lockfile.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/dependabot-alert-monitor.sh`: `_dam_fetch_alert_groups`, `_dam_create_issue_for_group`, `dependabot_alert_monitor_scan_repo`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependabot-alert-monitor.sh`: add a case with two alerts for one package that have different patched versions.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependabot-alert-monitor.sh`
- A dry run (`dependabot-alert-monitor.sh scan --dry-run --repos-json <fixture>`) over that fixture prints one `DRY_RUN` line for the package, not two.
- ShellCheck clean.

title: t19001: fix(headless-runtime): signal-less merged own-PR handoff ignores the post-mer...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19001` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `bug`

## Outcome

fix(headless-runtime): signal-less merged own-PR handoff ignores the post-merge cleanup-deferred marker

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Discovery pass: GH#37597 (merged) excluded the deferred-cleanup marker from the own-merged and PR-less completion proofs; GH#38059 (merged) did the same for reclaim. GH#38303 (merged) added the signal-less handoff path without that exclusion. No open issue covers it.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. Reuses an existing, tested cleanliness helper; no new trust boundary.

## What

Make the GH#38303 signal-less own-PR handoff path (`_run_result_reconcile_signal_less_handoff`) treat a worktree whose only untracked path is the post-merge `.agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred` marker as clean, so a worker that merged its own closing PR through `full-loop-helper.sh merge` but omitted the completion token is routed through the post-PR handoff gate instead of `premature_exit`.

## Why

Evidence (last 72h, runner-local metrics `~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`): 16 issue-worker `premature_exit` outcomes. In 8, the issue was already CLOSED/COMPLETED 1.5-4 minutes before the worker exited. Two inspected cases (a Cloudron app repo and a WordPress plugin repo) follow the same sequence:

1. The worker opened its PR with `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue N` (exact `Resolves #N`, branch `feature/auto-*-ghN`).
2. `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR>` merged it; the linked issue closed within 2 seconds; the runner stayed sole assignee.
3. The cleanup receipt was written as `FINALIZATION_PENDING` / `release_status: pending` (no worker release authority), so `_hrw_own_merged_terminal_complete` correctly declines (it requires a finalized receipt, GH#35629).
4. The final answer reported the merge but emitted no `FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE`, so `output_has_completion_signal` failed.
5. `_run_result_classify_incomplete_issue_exit` calls `_run_result_reconcile_signal_less_handoff`, which accepts `merged` handoff state, but its cleanliness test was raw `git status --porcelain`. After a helper merge the worktree always contains the untracked `.agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred` marker (`_merge_record_deferred_cleanup_owner`); in both surviving worker worktrees it was the only entry. The path returned 1, so the run became `premature_exit` (exit 77), mapped to `overwhelmed` for escalation (`_hrw_run_finish_crash_type`) and skipping `status:done` label normalization.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh` `_run_result_reconcile_signal_less_handoff`: use `_hrw_task_worktree_status "$work_dir"` (the shared task-worktree status the own-merged and PR-less proofs use), guarded with `declare -F` so an unavailable helper still fails closed. Every other guard is unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh`: `merged_marker` (marker only → `post_pr_handoff`) and `merged_marker_dirty` (marker plus another untracked file → `premature_exit`) scenarios in the GH#38303 fixture.

## Acceptance

## Task


Simplify the pulse dispatch path so a worker launch costs about what an interactive `/full-loop` start costs (claim + worktree + start, about 20s), and free worker slots refill within minutes, not at the end of a 26-45 minute maintenance cycle. This plan has measurable phases. Each child is a separate issue.

## Children

- #38333
- #38352
- #38413

Phase coverage: phase 1 = #38333; phase 3 = #38352; phase 2 = #38413 plus existing early dispatch (GH#28880/GH#37986). Phase 4 (REST budget priority) has no child yet, so the close contract stays `needs-decomposition`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Simplify the pulse dispatch path so a worker launch costs about what an interactive `/full-loop` start costs (claim + worktree + start, about 20s), and free worker slots refill within minutes, not at the end of a 26-45 minute maintenance cycle. This plan has measurable phases. Each child is a separate issue.

## Why (evidence, one runner, 2026-11-07..14)

Throughput, managed repos, last 7 days (GitHub search `issueCount`):

| Lane | Merged PRs / 7d | Median issue→merge | Median PR open→merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interactive sessions (`origin:interactive`, maintainer-authored) | 806 (≈115/day) | 0.8h | 15 min |
| This runner's workers (`origin:worker`, maintainer-authored) | 240 (≈34/day) | 3.1h | 24 min |

The worker lane's extra ~2.3h happens before a PR exists. The runner is not capacity-bound:

- `max_concurrent_workers=20`; worker metrics show 450 runs and 106 worker-hours in 168h, so **mean concurrency ≈0.6 of 20**. `pulse-health.json` at 19:42Z showed 0/20 active, last dispatch progress 18:11Z.
- The ready queue is not empty. 121 open `auto-dispatch` issues are unassigned, not blocked, unheld and non-parent. The oldest dates from 2026-06-10.
- Cycles take 26-45 min (`pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`) and dispatch 0-6 workers each. In one 44-minute window, maintenance stages took about 3,870 stage-seconds (`pulse-stage-timings.log`). The largest were post_dispatch_housekeeping 636s, dashboard_freshness_check 499s, preflight_label_maintenance 488s, preflight_ownership_reconcile 328s and normalize_active_issue_assignments 261s. preflight_early_dispatch ran in 0s and dispatched nothing.
- Per-launch dispatcher ceremony (`dispatch-stages.tsv`, 24h, 67 launches) took median 295s, p90 532s. In the same window, 408 `dedup.dedup_check` runs (median 46s) consumed 441 minutes, about 6.6 min of rejected-candidate checking per successful launch. claim_lock median was 56s and precreate_worktree median 43s.
- Rejections are knowable cheaply from the candidate snapshot. Over 41h of `pulse.log`: dedup_active_claim* 242, draft-checkpoint blocked/stale 236, dedup_pr_evidence 108, runner_capability_unmet 45, terminal_blocker_circuit 34. `_filter_dispatchable_issue_candidates_json` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-repo-meta.sh:575`) admits assigned, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review` and `status:claimed` issues by design (comment at `:641-654`). `_dispatch_recheck_zero_worker_active_claims` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:695`) re-opens active-claim rejections whenever the pool is empty, which is this runner's normal state.
- Two cycles in the window were blocked on `rest-core-quota`, with zero dispatch, while maintenance continued to draw on the same REST budget.
- About a dozen recent symptom-level perf fixes (#37874, #38022, #38033, #38055, #38210, #38226, #38237, #38261, #38274, #37811) did not move launches above about 2.8/hour.

## How (phases → child issues)

1. **Fresh-first candidate lane.** Rank unclaimed candidates first: no assignee and no `status:in-progress`/`status:in-review`/`status:claimed`. Recovery candidates (assigned, in-review or claimed) get a small per-round evaluation cap. Nothing becomes undispatchable; stale-claim recovery keeps a bounded share. Target: under 2 dedup checks per launch.
2. **Dispatch never waits on maintenance.** When at least half the slots are free, dispatch/refill runs before label maintenance, dashboard freshness, ownership reconcile and housekeeping, and again between them. Maintenance stages yield to a pending refill instead of holding the cycle.
3. **Interactive-equivalent launch ceremony.** Target median under 60s of dispatcher time per launch. Move worktree precreate and post-launch hooks onto the worker's own startup path, and launch candidates in parallel once claims are verified.
4. **REST budget priority.** Maintenance defers when REST-core falls below the dispatch reserve, so a `rest-core-quota` cycle still dispatches.

## Acceptance (measured on a 20-slot runner, 24h after deploy)

- Launches per day on this runner at least 3x the 67/day baseline, with no rise in duplicate PRs or duplicate claims (`dispatch-stages.tsv`, metrics jsonl).
- Mean worker concurrency at least 5 while the ready queue is non-empty.
- Median issue→merge for worker PRs at or below 1.5h (GitHub search, same method as above).

title: worker-lifecycle: treat ESRCH (ProcessLookupError) from exited /proc tasks as vanished, not observation failure
body:
## What

`require_idle_proc` in `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_proc.py` treats a `/proc` task that exits mid-scan as an observation failure. Retirement then refuses spuriously, and the Worker Lifecycle Linux contract flakes in CI.

## Evidence

Complexity Analysis → "Verify Worker Lifecycle Linux contract", run 43633794824 (job 132566656522), on PR #38326, which does not touch worker-lifecycle:

```
ERROR: test_codex_config_retirement_preserves_bytes_without_restoring_config (test_retirement.RetirementContract)
  legacy_proc.py line 70, in require_idle_proc -> inspect_proc_task(path, task, proc)
  legacy_proc.py line 122, in inspect_proc_task -> live_owned_proc_task(task)
  legacy_proc.py line 77, in live_owned_proc_task -> (task / "status").read_text(...)
ProcessLookupError: [Errno 3] No such process
```

Reading `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/status` for a task that has just exited raises ESRCH (`ProcessLookupError`), not ENOENT. `inspect_proc_task` (line 125) only treats `FileNotFoundError` as "task vanished". `ProcessLookupError` is an `OSError`, so the outer handler in `require_idle_proc` (line 71) converts it to `ValueError("proc-observation-unavailable")`.

## Reproducer

Intermittent: a same-UID task exits between `(process / "task").iterdir()` and `(task / "status").read_text()`. Deterministic simulation: patch `Path.read_text` to raise `ProcessLookupError(3, "No such process")` and `Path.exists` to return False for one task. `require_idle_proc` then raises `ValueError("proc-observation-unavailable")` instead of skipping the vanished task.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_proc.py`

## How

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_proc.py`:
  - `inspect_proc_task`: catch `(FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError)` and keep the existing `task.exists()` re-check, so a still-present task still fails closed.
  - `require_idle_proc`: apply the same pair to the `(process / "task").iterdir()` listing.
  - Check `require_predating_daemon` and `inspect_proc_references` for the same race. Only a disappeared task may be skipped; permission errors and still-existing tasks must keep failing closed.
- Reference pattern: the existing `FileNotFoundError` + `exists()` re-check in the same file.

## Verification

- `PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle python3 -m unittest discover -s .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests -v` on Linux, the same suite as the CI step "Verify Worker Lifecycle Linux contract".
- Optional focused case: patch `Path.read_text` to raise `ProcessLookupError` while `Path.exists` returns False, and assert the scan continues. With `exists` True it must still raise `proc-observation-unavailable`.
