**Task ID:** `t19004` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `feat`

## Outcome

feat(github-auth): one-command GitHub App setup (manifest create + bulk bind) so Pulse reads stop exhausting the shared PAT

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Discovery pass: no manifest-flow or bulk-bind command exists (`rg app-manifests|bind` in `github_auth*.py`); related merged work GH#38150 (actions:read) and GH#38273 (advisory) left setup manual.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. Additive CLI over existing signing, exchange, profile and route validation.

## What

Add a near-zero-attention setup path for Pulse GitHub App read routing:

1. `aidevops github auth app create --owner OWNER [--name NAME]` — GitHub App Manifest flow. A loopback-only page (127.0.0.1, random port, one-time `state`) auto-posts a read-only manifest to GitHub; the operator clicks **Create GitHub App**; the CLI exchanges the one-time code (`POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions`), writes the PEM to `~/.config/aidevops/keys/<slug>.pem` (0600, O_EXCL, never printed), creates the named profile with the existing profile code, and prints the install URL.
2. `aidevops github auth app bind --profile NAME [--owner OWNER] [--dry-run]` — discovers the App's installations with a JWT, lists each installation's covered repositories, and binds only covered, pulse-enabled, non-local registry entries (read → github-app, write → inherit) in one locked registry write. Uncovered repos keep inherited auth.

## Why

Evidence from one runner, 24h to 2026-11-14T20:30Z:

- `aidevops github auth advise --since 24h`: 80,868 routable REST attempts; `routable_known_quota_cost` 63,338 of 77,093 (82%); `rest_core_min_remaining` 0; all 5 pulse owners lack App read routing; 0 of 70 pulse repos bound.
- `pulse.log`: 13 deferrals of `dispatch_max` at `rest=emergency:0/5000`; 8 of 33 cycles ended `blocked/rest-core-quota` with zero dispatch while 121 ready `auto-dispatch` issues waited (parent GH#38332 phase 4).
- The binding machinery exists (GH#38150, GH#38273) but setup is manual: create App in the web UI, choose 7 permissions, generate and move a PEM, copy App ID and installation ID, then `aidevops github auth set` once per repository (70 here). That is the barrier, not the routing.

## How

- New modules: `.agents/scripts/github_auth_setup.py` (parser, create orchestration), `.agents/scripts/github_auth_app_manifest.py` (loopback Manifest flow, conversion, key save), `.agents/scripts/github_auth_app_bind.py` (installation discovery, planner, locked bind). Split to stay under qlty file-complexity and parameter/return smells. Wire `app create|bind` into `.agents/scripts/github_auth_cli.py` (`repo_free_action`).
- Reuse: `github_app_auth.jwt/exchange/api/atomic_json/private_read`, `DEFAULT_PULSE_READ_PERMISSIONS`, `github_auth_profiles.manage_profile`, `github_auth_config.registry/registry_lock/settings`, `github_auth_policy.validate_routes`.
- Manifest: `public: false`, no webhook (`hook_attributes.active: false`), `default_permissions` = read for `DEFAULT_PULSE_READ_PERMISSIONS`, no events, `redirect_url` = loopback callback. Org owners post to `https://github.com/organizations/<org>/settings/apps/new`, users to `https://github.com/settings/apps/new`.
- Bind skips: legacy `pulse_auth` entries (needs `migrate`), `local_only`, non-pulse, owners without an installation, repos outside a `selected` installation, suspended installations. Report each skip reason.
- Docs: add a "Fast path" section to `.agents/reference/github-auth.md`.

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/github_auth_setup.py
- .agents/scripts/github_auth_app_manifest.py
- .agents/scripts/github_auth_app_bind.py
- .agents/scripts/github_auth_cli.py
- .agents/reference/github-auth.md
- TODO.md

## Acceptance

- `app bind --dry-run` with a valid profile lists per-repo decisions and writes nothing.
- `app bind` writes routes only for covered repos; `aidevops github auth check OWNER/REPO --consumer pulse` reports `read_check: passed` for a bound repo.
- Negative: bind refuses an unknown profile; never overwrites a legacy `pulse_auth` entry; never binds a repo absent from a `selected` installation; PEM is never echoed and an existing key file is never overwritten.
- `app create` refuses a mismatched or missing `state` and binds only to 127.0.0.1.

## Verification

- `python3 -m py_compile .agents/scripts/github_auth_setup.py .agents/scripts/github_auth_app_manifest.py .agents/scripts/github_auth_app_bind.py .agents/scripts/github_auth_cli.py`
- `qlty smells --no-snippets` on the three new modules reports no smells.

title: Planning PR fallback fails on new repos: allow-auto-merge label is never provisioned
body:
## Problem

On a newly initialised managed repository whose default branch requires pull requests, the first planning publication fails. `planning-commit-helper.sh complete <task> --pr <N>` (and plain `planning-commit-helper.sh "<msg>"`) falls back to a planning PR, and `shared-todo-commit.sh` `_todo_open_planning_pr` (line ~707) passes `--label "allow-auto-merge"` to `gh_create_pr`. Nothing provisions that label, so `gh` rejects the call:

```text
could not add label: 'allow-auto-merge' not found
[todo_commit_push] Planning publication stopped after pushed; ...
AIDEVOPS_PLANNING_RECOVERY_PR_STATE=missing
[plan] Task completion publication failed; no successful direct push or planning PR was created
```

Observed 2026-11-14 on a private repository created the same day with `aidevops init` (lean profile), the four managed workflow callers, and classic branch protection (PR required, 0 approvals). Older repositories have the label, apparently created by hand or by earlier framework versions.

## Evidence

- `rg -n 'allow-auto-merge' ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/managed-label-provisioning-lib.sh ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/repo-onboarding-audit-lib.sh` → no matches; the only creator-side reference is the `--label` in `shared-todo-commit.sh`.
- After `gh label create allow-auto-merge` (same colour and description as an older repo: `0E8A16`, "Allow approved automation to merge after required checks pass"), re-running `planning-commit-helper.sh` reused the pushed branch and opened the planning PR. Recovery works; the first attempt does not.
- The same new repository also lacked `complexity-bump-ok`, `conflict-feedback-routed`, `fix-the-fixer`, `infrastructure`, `source:auto-decomposer` and `source:conflict-feedback` compared with an older repository. Check whether any script adds these with `--label` without creating them.

## Suggested fix

1. Add `allow-auto-merge` to a provisioning set in `managed-label-provisioning-lib.sh` and ensure it before `gh_create_pr` in `_todo_open_planning_pr`, or let `gh_create_pr` create missing managed labels.
2. Have `aidevops init` / the onboarding audit (`repo-onboarding-audit-lib.sh`) provision every label that framework scripts pass with `--label`/`--add-label`.

## Verification

- On a fresh repository with protected `main` and no `allow-auto-merge` label, `planning-commit-helper.sh complete <task> --pr <merged-pr>` opens a planning PR on the first attempt.
- `rg -n -- "--(add-)?label \"[a-z:-]+\"" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts --glob '*.sh'`: every literal label found is created by a provisioning path.

title: gpt_image_generate: OAuth route hardcodes rejected gpt-6-sol router model; add OpenRouter image route
body:
## What happened

`gpt_image_generate` failed on its default ChatGPT OAuth route during an interactive image task (2026-11-14):

```
OpenAI oauth image request failed (400): model_not_found: The 'gpt-6-sol' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.
```

The OAuth route sends the hardcoded router model `CODEX_FALLBACK_MODEL = "gpt-6-sol"` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/openai-codex-model-fallback.mjs:6`, used by `gpt-image-request.mjs:97`). There is no way to choose another router model from the tool arguments (`model` is API-only).

## Evidence gathered

- `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models?client_version=1.0.0` for the pooled OAuth account returned only `gpt-reserve`, `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-5.6-luna`, `codex-auto-review`. `gpt-6.1-sol` was also rejected with `model_not_found`.

title: Phase 3 of #38051: One decision function `remove | archive | refuse(reason)`, stage 1 removals only, each decision journaled as a Reclaim authorization event keyed by (path, evidence fingerprint) with a commit-time CAS recheck.
body:
<!-- aidevops:generator=phase-autofile parent=38051 phase=3 -->

## What

Implement Phase 3 of parent-task #38051: one decision function classifies every
reclaim candidate as `remove | archive | refuse(reason)`. Stage 1 removes only
`remove`; `archive` candidates are skipped (queued for Phase 5), not refused.
Each applied decision is journaled as a Reclaim event keyed by
(path, evidence fingerprint), and removal re-computes the fingerprint and
refuses on mismatch (CAS).

## Why

Today `reclaim/evidence.py` returns a single `authorized` boolean, so finished
work with uncommitted changes or unpushed commits is refused alongside genuinely
unsafe trees, and nothing durable records why a tree was removed. The
2026-11-13 maintainer decisions on #38051 ("delete first, archive second" and
"remove the manual retirement authorization") require a three-way decision and
an evidence-backed authorization event that later phases (6, 7) can read in
place of `enrolled_only_authorized`.

## How

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/decision.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/evidence.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/sweep.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/journal.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reclaim.py`

### Per-file changes

- `decision.py`: `classify(verdict)`, `fingerprint(path)`, deterministic `uuid5` event IDs, journal helper.
- `evidence.py`: finished work whose only blocker is `uncommitted-changes` / `unpushed-commits-N` is reported so `classify` returns `archive`.
- `sweep.py`: consume `classify`; receipt gains `decision` per result and an `archive_queued` count; when `--apply`, journal `reclaim-authorized` before removal and `reclaim-removed` after; CAS recheck before removal.
- `journal.py`: archive-first compaction of reclaim event types older than retention.
- `test_reclaim.py`: classification, fingerprint CAS and journal idempotency cases.

### Reference pattern

- Journal writes: `LifecycleRegistry.connection(write=True)` + `append_event` (`journal.py:20`); event IDs must be UUID strings (`storage.identifier`).
- Owner checks stay in `reclaim/owners.py`; dry runs issue no writes.

## Acceptance

- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests` passes.
- A dry run reports `decision` for every result and writes nothing to the registry.
- An applied removal leaves exactly one `reclaim-authorized` and one `reclaim-removed` event; a repeat pass is idempotent.
- A tree whose HEAD or status changes between judgement and removal is refused with `evidence-changed`.

## Session Origin

Filed interactively for parent #38051. For #38051.

body:
## What

Let Pulse progress a phased parent on its own instead of holding it for a
human when the next declared phase is ready to file.

## Why

Parent #38051 stalled for a day. Two defects combined:

1. `_update_parent_phases_section` (`.agents/scripts/shared-phase-filing.sh`)
   only rewrites bullet phase lines (`- Phase N ...`). `_parse_phases_section`
   also accepts numbered lines (`N. desc`) and bold lines (`**Phase N — desc**`).
   For #38051 (numbered form) the bootstrap filed #38062 for Phase 1 but never
   wrote `#38062` back, so Phase 1 stayed "unfiled".
2. When every filed child is closed and phases remain unfiled,
   `_hold_parent_for_incomplete_close_contract`
   (`.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions-parent.sh`) posts the
   unfiled-phases nudge and adds `hold-for-review`. The bootstrap filer only
   runs for parents with zero children, so after Phase 1 nothing ever files
   Phase 2+. A plan with no `requires-decision` marker needs no human decision.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-phase-filing.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions-parent.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-phase-filing.sh`

  is `requires-decision`, and honour an existing `hold-for-review`.

- An idle parent (all filed children closed) with an unfiled non-decision
  phase gets that phase filed, with no nudge or `hold-for-review`.

body:
## Task


Trusted worker release comments posted after a maintainer approval must not stale that approval when they are exact writer output. Today six writer outputs are rejected:

| Writer output | Reader verdict |
|---|---|
| `missing_files_scope`, `files_scope_excluded`, `target_code_blocker`, `external_trigger_pending`, `permission_required`, `unknown` | canonical |
| `source_access_blocked owner=access-owner` | **not canonical** (class missing) |
| `push_policy_timeout`, `network_policy_timeout`, `runner_capability_unmet` (`owner=runner-recovery`) | **not canonical** (classes missing) |
| `input_required` with a sanitized question | **not canonical** (new Next action text and the `Input requested:` line) |
| `input_required` without a question | **not canonical** (fallback Next action text) |
| `unknown` with a `CHECKPOINT_UNKNOWN_TRIAGE pending_work ...` line | **not canonical** (extra line) |

## Done when

- [ ] Positive: a trusted, post-cutoff release comment generated by the current writer for every class in the table, including `input_required` with and without a question and `unknown` with a triage line, verifies as `VERIFIED`.
- [ ] Negative: the same comment with extra prose, an unlisted owner, an `Input requested:` line containing `<`, `@` or a newline, or a non-trusted author still verifies as `STALE_APPROVAL`.
- [ ] Negative: the existing approval binding tests pass unchanged apart from the replaced stale fixture.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh:138` — extend `canonical_terminal_blocker_release`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh:662-700` — build the release fixtures from the real writer and cover every class.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `canonical_terminal_blocker_release` is used only at `approval-snapshot-v2.sh:194`, in the trusted-author, post-cutoff comment exclusion.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` `terminal_blocker_observation_fragment` (line 705) and `_terminal_blocker_recovery` (line 999) produce the text; the release wrapper adds the `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked ...` line and the worker footer. No writer change is needed.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh` (canonical release cases around lines 662-700) and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` (writer text, question sanitizer around lines 560-600).
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because the public release comment format written by `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` is unchanged; only its reader is corrected.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`; no generated output.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because approvals are verified on read; already-stale approvals become `VERIFIED` again on the next read with no backfill.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR in `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh`; no state is written.

### Implementation Steps

1. In the reason alternatives add `source_access_blocked owner=access-owner` and `(?:push_policy_timeout|network_policy_timeout|runner_capability_unmet) owner=runner-recovery`.
2. In the Next action alternatives add the exact current strings from `_terminal_blocker_recovery` for those classes and the two current `input_required` strings (with question: "Supply the requested input in the issue brief; ..."; without: "no sanitized question recorded; the originating runner's recovery supervisor must publish one. No maintainer action is possible until then."). Keep the legacy `input_required` string so comments posted by older runners still verify.
3. After `Raw evidence remains in protected worker telemetry\\.\\n`, admit at most one optional line: either `Input requested: ` followed by 1-500 characters excluding control characters and `` <>`@ `` (the sanitizer contract in `_terminal_blocker_public_question`, lines 960-997), or `CHECKPOINT_UNKNOWN_TRIAGE pending_work brief=[a-f0-9]{64} head=[a-f0-9]{40,64}`. Keep the `^`/`$` anchors, so any other extra prose stays content-bound.
4. In the test, generate each release body by sourcing `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` in a subshell and calling `terminal_blocker_observation_fragment`, rather than copying strings, so future writer changes fail this test instead of silently staling approvals. Replace the stale fixture at line 685.
5. Run the tests and `shellcheck`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A because verification is a pure read of comment history; no locks or writes are involved.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; the reader is evaluated on every verification.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** keep every existing alternative, including the legacy `input_required` action, so comments from older runners still verify.
- **Idempotency/retry:** verification is deterministic for the same comment history.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** N/A because a regex mismatch fails closed to `STALE_APPROVAL`, today's behaviour.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** `test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh` proves each writer class verifies as canonical (acceptance 1) and that extra prose, an unlisted owner and an external author stay content-bound (acceptance 2). `test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` proves the writer text is unchanged. `shellcheck` covers both touched files.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required. One reader regex and its test.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not widen trusted associations, the cutoff or the anchors. Admit only exact writer output; free text is limited to the sanitized `Input requested:` line. Keep the `#aidevops:trust-boundary` comment.

The writer changed (GH#36760 `aed371e4ed`, plus the runner-recovery and source-access classes) and the reader did not.
- [x] Reproduced on 2026-11-14 by feeding real writer output for every class through the reader's own jq definition (method under Verification Before Dispatch).

## Origin

- Created: 2026-11-14, interactive productivity-mission session (OpenCode), author ai-interactive, while preparing t19007.

## What

Trusted worker release comments posted after a maintainer approval must not stale that approval when they are exact writer output. Today six writer outputs are rejected:

| Writer output | Reader verdict |
|---|---|
| `missing_files_scope`, `files_scope_excluded`, `target_code_blocker`, `external_trigger_pending`, `permission_required`, `unknown` | canonical |
| `source_access_blocked owner=access-owner` | **not canonical** (class missing) |

| `input_required` without a question | **not canonical** (fallback Next action text) |
| `unknown` with a `CHECKPOINT_UNKNOWN_TRIAGE pending_work ...` line | **not canonical** (extra line) |

## Why

A non-canonical trusted comment after the approval cutoff is treated as content drift, so the approval verifies as `STALE_APPROVAL` and a needs-maintainer-review issue returns to the maintainer for re-approval. A runner-capability release (for example, a runner lacking a declared secret) can therefore stale an approved issue even though it changed nothing the maintainer approved. ## Context & Decisions

body:
**Task ID:** `t19006` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-14
**Tags:** `feat` `auto-dispatch`

## Outcome

perf(dispatch): halve launch ceremony and dedup verdict time (For #38332 phase 3)

## Done when

- [ ] Positive: over a 12h window after deployment, `dispatch-stages.tsv` shows median `dedup.ceremony_total` of 175s or less and average `dedup.dedup_check` of 35s or less. The PR reports before and after numbers.
- [ ] Positive: `[dispatch-claim] stage=assignment_guard` averages under 5s, or the stage is removed with the reuse rationale documented. The post-consensus `final_assignment_guard` still performs a fresh read.
- [ ] Positive: a draft-checkpoint verdict whose PR head, labels and issue comments are unchanged is answered from the negative cache, `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` averages under 30s, and a skipped cache record is logged with its reason.
- [ ] Negative: no cross-runner double dispatch. The consensus window, claim lock, NMR gate and draft-checkpoint redispatch hold behave as before, and the existing tests above pass unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh:760-830` — `assignment_guard` / `final_assignment_guard`: reuse layer-6 evidence or call a cheaper check; keep the post-consensus guard fresh.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-runtime.sh:54-72` — share the validated per-launch snapshot (`_dch_snapshot_valid`) with the assignment check.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:1390-1460` — `is-assigned` / `is-assigned-read-only`: profile and cut redundant network reads.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh:326-390` — layer 4: consult the negative cache before the checkpoint continuation helpers.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh:693-730` — layer 6: export its verdict and fingerprint for the claim step.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:459-515` — `_dispatch_negative_cache_record`: log silent record skips once per issue with their reason.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh` — bound `verify.reconcile` / `reconcile_scan` for a freshly created worker worktree.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:1937-2036` — `_dispatch_launch_worker`: attribute `worker_launch_total` beyond precreate (the `_ds_record` stage calls) if the targets are not met. Precreate itself is `_dlw_precreate_worktree` at `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:885-986`.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` (`dispatch_with_dedup`) calls the dedup layers. `dispatch-claim-helper.sh` is invoked from `pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh` (claim step around line 787) and `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`. `worktree-helper-add.sh` is called by `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` precreate. Negative-cache readers are `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason` callers in `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** claim comments (`claim_post`) and handoff leases in `dispatch-claim-helper.sh`; negative-cache files under `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-negative-cache/` written by `_dispatch_negative_cache_record`; stage rows appended to `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv` by `dispatch-stage-instrument.sh`. No GitHub write paths are added.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-claim-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`. Production evidence: `dispatch-stages.tsv` and `[dispatch-claim] stage=` lines in `pulse.log`.
- **Schemas/config:** the negative-cache record format is the tab-separated line in `_dispatch_negative_cache_record` (line 504). Keep the field order; add no fields unless every reader is updated in the same PR. `DISPATCH_CLAIM_WINDOW` stays at its default.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`. There is no generated output; deployment follows the normal release.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A. Existing negative-cache files stay readable because the format is unchanged; old records expire through their existing TTL and boundary.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR. Cached verdicts in `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-negative-cache/` self-invalidate on fingerprint change, and no persistent state outside that directory is introduced.

### Implementation Steps

1. Read `[dispatch-claim] stage=` lines and `dispatch-stages.tsv` for the latest 12h to confirm the baseline (commands under Verification Before Dispatch).
2. Profile one `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned` call (e.g. `bash -x` or its existing stage output) and list its network reads. Decide between making it cheap (one issue read and one comments read, shared through the validated claim snapshot) and reusing the layer-6 verdict for `assignment_guard` when issue `updated_at` and the comment count are unchanged. The final post-consensus guard must stay a fresh read.
3. In `worktree-helper-add.sh`, skip or bound `verify.reconcile` / `reconcile_scan` when the worktree was created by this call and its generation marker was just written. Keep the full check for reused or recovered worktrees.
4. In layer 4, check `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason` for `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` / `stale_draft_checkpoint` before invoking the continuation helper. In `_dispatch_negative_cache_record`, log `negative_cache_record_skipped reason=<boundary|fingerprint> issue=#N` when `_dispatch_draft_hint_boundary` or `_dispatch_negative_pr_fingerprint` fails, and fix the failing input found on a real skipped issue.
5. If the targets are still missed, attribute `worker_launch_total` stages in `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` and cut the next largest step.
6. Run ShellCheck and the existing tests, commit a WIP checkpoint, then measure again after deployment.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** cross-runner double dispatch is the main risk. The consensus window, claim lock and fresh post-consensus assignment guard stay. Only the pre-consensus duplicate check may reuse evidence, and only when the issue revision is unchanged.
- **Migration/rollback:** no data migration. Rollback is a revert; caches self-invalidate on fingerprint change.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** other runners on older versions still post the same claim comments and read the same negative-cache format. Claim comment formats must not change.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a reused verdict is a hint; any mismatch falls through to the full check. Retrying a dispatch after a cache miss behaves as today.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a failed cache read or write falls through to the authoritative ceremony, as today. A precreate verification skipped on a fresh worktree must leave the full check in place for any reused path.

### Complexity Impact

`_dedup_layer6_assignee_and_stale` and the claim functions are near the 100-line function gate. Extract helpers before adding logic; keep each changed function under 80 lines.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
awk -F'\t' '$6=="complete" && $4 ~ /^dedup\.(ceremony_total|dedup_check)$/ {n[$4]++; s[$4]+=$5} END{for(k in n) printf "%s n=%d avg=%.0fms\n", k, n[k], s[k]/n[k]}' ~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv
rg -o '\[dispatch-claim\] stage=[a-z_]+ elapsed_s=[0-9]+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-claim-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh .agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-runtime.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** the `awk` command proves both timing targets (acceptance 1). The `rg` command proves the assignment-guard reduction (acceptance 2). `test-dispatch-claim-helper.sh` covers claim consensus and the final guard (concurrency hazard, acceptance 4). `test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh` and `test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh` cover negative-cache reuse and draft-checkpoint holds (acceptance 3 and 4). `shellcheck` covers every touched script.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required. The changes are confined to dispatch helpers with focused tests.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: the three test scripts above
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: t19006 dispatch ceremony`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required — confined to dispatch helpers

### Scope Boundaries

title: Draft checkpoint strips auto-dispatch and 48h fleet window stalls single-runner queues; kept branch re-triggers checkpoint
body:
## Observed

On a private managed repo, five day-one issues stalled the same way:

1. A worker opens a draft PR on its issue branch, then exits partial. `_escalate_worker_pr_checkpoint` (`headless-runtime-worker-output.sh` ~line 286) sets the issue `status:in-review` and removes `auto-dispatch`, so stale recovery can continue the exact PR.
2. Stale recovery for that draft (`pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh dispatch-stalled`) reports `stale_draft_checkpoint` with tier `fleet_window_pending` (172800 s window). So nothing continues the PR for up to 48 h, and nothing else dispatches the issue because `auto-dispatch` is gone.
3. The maintainer closes the draft (keeping the branch) and re-adds `auto-dispatch`. The next worker finds the kept branch, reopens a draft from it, and checkpoints again. That strips `auto-dispatch` a second time (seen within 3 minutes of dispatch).

The only reliable workaround was closing the draft and deleting the branch so the worker starts clean.

## Expected

A checkpointed draft should be continued within one pulse cycle, or the issue should keep a dispatchable state. Re-adding `auto-dispatch` after closing the draft should not be undone by a worker reusing the old branch.

## Suggested direction

- Shorten or remove the 48 h `fleet_window_pending` for single-runner fleets (only one runner ever dispatches).
- Or: when the checkpointed PR is closed by a maintainer, treat the checkpoint as void. Restore `auto-dispatch` and do not reuse the PR's head branch.
- Add test coverage in `tests/test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh` for "maintainer closed the checkpoint PR → next dispatch starts from default branch".

## Related lesson

A scripted rewrite of `repos.json` (python `json.dump`) left the file mode 664. `github_app_auth.py` `private_read` then rejected it ("Unsafe ownership or permissions on auth input"). Candidate enumeration failed for every repo until `chmod 600`. Consider having repos.json writers preserve mode 0600. Also consider a pulse-health warning naming the file, instead of a per-repo enumeration failure.

## What

When a Pulse exact-head continuation of a stall-released worker draft fails to launch, the runtime releases the claim as `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_not_launched`. `_pcc_stall_release_evidence` then finds no current stall release, `blocked-attention` posts `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION ... reason=worker_not_launched`, and the draft is held until a maintainer acts. Nothing re-arms it.

After this fix, a `worker_not_launched` release keeps the draft on the bounded automatic continuation path:

1. A never-launched continuation episode of the PR's own session (claim and prelaunch leases, no ready lease, no `Dispatching worker`) that is closed by its own `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_not_launched` stays transparent, as GH#38103 already does for episodes closed only by a terminal lease. The earlier stall release stays current evidence. The first failed launch is retried at once; the second reaches the existing per-head attention and re-arm windows.
2. A `worker_not_launched` release whose episode did post a ready lease (runtime never confirmed, `_hrff_verified_release_reason`) is a stall-class release under `_PCC_STALL_RELEASE_PATTERN`. It is bounded by the existing per-head stall count, re-arm windows, per-PR fuse and the GH#37779 terminal action, never by a human-only attention record.

## Why

Sample on 2026-11-14 of 38 open issues carrying `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` across the managed fleet: 10 (26%) were held only because the newest release was `worker_not_launched`. They had been idle 2-23 hours, with no re-arm path. Examples:

- This repo: #38282 (draft #38284). Stall release `worker_draft_checkpoint` at 13:41Z. Continuation claim at 13:44Z, prelaunch lease, then `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_not_launched` at 13:45Z in session `pr-checkpoint-continuation-marcusquinn-aidevops-38284`, and `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION ... reason=worker_not_launched` at 13:47Z. Nothing since.
- One managed product repo, local runner logs: `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_REARMED ... mode=untried_runner`, then `headless-prelaunch.log` `prelaunch_abort ... stage=post_attempt_observers_start cause=worker_runtime_not_invoked`, then on every later cycle `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED: ... has no current stall release` and `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`.

A launch failure records no worker decision and leaves the head unchanged. GH#36597 already treats `worker_noop_zero_output` and `worker_incomplete_exit` the same way. Sending it to a human contradicts the release fragment that the runtime itself posts ("bounded retries").

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Two small edits to an existing jq classification, following GH#36597 (pattern addition) and GH#38103 (transparent never-launched episode). Recovery bounds are unchanged.

- Reuses the existing bounds instead of adding a new retry counter, so the recovery machinery does not grow.
- The python approval validator (`STALL_RELEASE_REASONS`) is left alone. GH#37669 already covers approval reuse after `worker_not_launched`. Making the release itself approvable is a separate contract.
- The cause of `worker_runtime_not_invoked` at `post_attempt_observers_start` is a separate launch-reliability question. This fix removes the human dependency whatever the cause.

title: Cloudron commit-mode standing release policy rejects full-SHA pins and upstreamLicense URL bumps
body:
## What

The commit-mode standing release policy (GH#37697, `upstream_mode: "commits"`) cannot authorize a real routine upstream bump of a commit-tracked Cloudron package, because the predicate rejects two changes that every such bump makes.

Observed on a managed Cloudron package repo (public: `marcusquinn/cloudron-opendesk-app`, PR #106, bump `7a47f44` -> `08b28ba`, package 0.2.23 -> 0.2.24):

1. **Full-SHA build pin.** `Dockerfile` pins `ARG OPENDESK_COMMIT=<40-char sha>` while `CloudronManifest.json` `upstreamVersion` is the 7-char prefix. `substitute_versions()` (`.agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py:109`) only replaces whole tokens bounded by `(?![A-Za-z0-9_])`, so the short prefix never matches inside the full SHA and the pinned-file rule fails: `Dockerfile: pinned file changes beyond version substitution`.
2. **SHA-bearing manifest field.** `upstreamLicense.url` is `https://github.com/<upstream>/blob/<full sha>/LICENSE` and changes with every bump. `check()` (`cloudron_routine_bump.py:237-239`) only excludes `version`/`upstreamVersion`, so it fails: `manifest changes beyond version and upstreamVersion`.

Additionally, that repo's signed policy (issue #107) was generated in default `semver` mode, so `release_policy_authorizes()` (`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh:384-388`) silently returns 1 on the `semver:upstream-commit-*` mismatch without printing a "does not apply" reason. `process` only reports `approval NO_APPROVAL; no merge`, which hides why the signed policy is inert.

Result: every routine bump of a commit-tracked package needs a per-release `sudo aidevops approve`, defeating the standing policy.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py`: in `commits` mode, extend the substitution mapping with the proven full SHAs (`upstream_proof.base` -> `upstream_proof.head`) for pinned files, and allow `upstreamLicense.url` to differ only by that same full-SHA substitution (keep every other manifest field exact).
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh` `release_policy_authorizes()`: print `standing policy #N does not apply (policy mode semver vs commit finding)` to stderr on the mode/fingerprint mismatch instead of a silent `return 1`.
- Optionally have `policy-request` / package init pick `commits` mode automatically when the monitor tracks upstream commits.

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh` and `test-cloudron-release-evidence.py` pass; add a fixture for a full-SHA Dockerfile pin plus SHA-bearing `upstreamLicense.url` that returns `ROUTINE_BUMP` in commits mode, and still returns `NOT_ROUTINE` when the full SHA does not match the proven upstream head.
- `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --repo <repo>` prints the mode-mismatch reason for a semver policy against a commit finding.

title: status:blocked must carry a needs-* label naming what unblocks it; heal false blocks
body:
## What

Make `status:blocked` always explain itself. An open issue may carry `status:blocked` only together with at least one `needs-*` label that names what unblocks it. Otherwise it is a false block, and the framework must route it back to solving.

The owner rule (14 November 2026): "status:blocked is meaningless. We only use status:blocked when there's an accompanying needs* label to explain what is needed to unblock." This patch must prevent false blocking and must never leave an issue without guidance on how to get it solved.

## Why (observed evidence)

In one managed private project repo, 5 of 12 open issues carried `status:blocked`, and the maintainer could not see why they were not being solved:

- Two had a `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` / `Terminal blocker: reason=input_required` comment. The real need (third-party test API keys, i.e. credentials) was buried in a recovery comment, and no `needs-credentials` label was present.
- One waited on an open dependency in another repo that a worker was already solving. Nothing on the issue said "waits on X".
- One was a scheduled monitoring task that an interactive session actively owned. Nothing external blocked it, so `status:blocked` was simply wrong.
- One was an owner-gated go-live step. The owner input was described only in the body.

Labels catalogued today (`.agents/scripts/label-sync-helper.sh` lines ~138-170): `needs-credentials`, `needs-maintainer-permissions`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `needs-review`, `needs-consolidation`, `needs-simplification`, `needs-review-fixes`. No label covers "owner decision or input" or "waits on a linked issue".

## How

1. **Catalogue two labels** in `.agents/scripts/label-sync-helper.sh` (system labels, attention colour) and in the `ensure` list in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh` (~line 471):
   - `needs-maintainer-input`: "Blocked: owner decision or input that AI cannot supply; the issue names the exact ask"
   - `needs-dependency`: "Blocked: waits on a linked open issue; solve that first, unblocks when it closes"
2. **Every writer of `status:blocked` adds the matching `needs-*` label in the same edit.** Today's writers (non-test):
   - `pulse-dep-graph.sh:702` (dependency): add `needs-dependency`. Remove it with `status:blocked` at `:713` / `:826`, and in `dependency-event-reconciler.sh:517`.
   - `headless-runtime-failure.sh:662` and `:1165`, plus the terminal-blocker projection in `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` `_terminal_blocker_recovery` (~line 998). Map by reason:
     - `input_required` → `needs-maintainer-input`
     - `permission_required` → `needs-maintainer-permissions`
     - `source_access_blocked` and missing-secret declarations (`TERMINAL_BLOCKER_MISSING_SECRETS`) → `needs-credentials`
     - `external_trigger_pending` → `needs-dependency`
     - Runner/brief-owned classes (`runner_capability_unmet`, `push_policy_timeout`, `network_policy_timeout`, `missing_files_scope`, `files_scope_excluded`, `target_code_blocker`, `unknown`) are AI-resolvable. Either hold them under a label that routes to the recovery supervisor (and show it in the dashboard as "AI recovery pending", not "blocked"), or keep `status:available`. Decide which, and document it.
   - `worker-permission-helper.sh:454`: already adds `needs-maintainer-permissions` (see `tests/test-worker-permission-helper.sh:141`). Keep it.
   - `pulse-fast-fail.sh:827-830`, `pulse-cleanup-worktree-state.sh:1252-1255`, `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:73`, `pulse-dispatch-core.sh:1092/1101/1687`, `shared-constants.sh:1662`, `pulse-cleanup.sh:695`: classify each one's reason and add the mapped label. Where the reason is machine-recoverable, use the AI-recovery route above rather than a human `needs-*`.
   - Central enforcement in `set_issue_status` (`shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh` ~line 794): when `new_status` is `blocked` and the passthrough flags add no `needs-*` label, log a warning and either refuse (return 2, which is a caller bug) or require a `--needs <label>` argument. Prefer refusing once every caller is updated, so new writers cannot regress.
3. **Self-healing sweep for existing false blocks.** Extend the GH#37978 unclassified-hold stage (`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` `tbr_discover_unclassified`, `_tbr_unclassified_listing`) or the label-invariant pass (`pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` `_normalize_label_invariants`, tested by `tests/test-label-invariants.sh`). For an open issue with `status:blocked` and no `needs-*`:
   - open native `blockedBy` edge or `blocked-by:` reference → add `needs-dependency` (deterministic);
   - terminal-blocker record whose reason maps above → add the mapped label (deterministic);
   - otherwise → queue for the recovery supervisor (as today) and count it in the supervisor dashboard as a false block. The supervisor must either solve or release it, or name the one human input with a `needs-*` label and a comment. Keep the existing trust boundary: the sweep itself never releases on missing evidence (GH#35540, GH#35569).
4. **Guidance:** whenever a `needs-*` label is applied with `status:blocked`, post (or update) one comment saying what is needed, who supplies it, the exact secure route (for example `aidevops secret set NAME`, never in issues), and what runs automatically afterwards. Credentials and permissions already have templates in `reference/worker-discipline.md`; reuse them.
5. **Docs:** in `.agents/reference/dispatch-blockers.md`, change the `status:blocked` row to "requires a companion `needs-*` label" and add rows for the two new labels. Update `.agents/reference/task-lifecycle.md` (~lines 44 and 181) and `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md` (~line 216, "`status:blocked` needs a structured reason/action").

## Acceptance

- No framework code path leaves an open issue with `status:blocked` and no `needs-*` label (unit-checked in the existing tests for each writer, e.g. `tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh`, `tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, `tests/test-label-invariants.sh`).
- Removing the blocker (dependency closes, credential retry lands, permission granted) removes both `status:blocked` and its `needs-*` label.
- The sweep labels existing dependency and terminal-blocker holds deterministically and queues the rest. A dry run on a managed repo reports zero unexplained `status:blocked` after one pass plus supervisor triage.
- ShellCheck is clean on every changed script.

## Verification

```bash
.agents/scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh

```

- `pulse-issue-reconcile-normalize.sh`: holds `_normalize_label_invariants_for_repo`, the label-invariant pass that `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` sources (GH#21376 split); the self-healing sweep lives there.
- `issue-sync-relationships-gh.sh:270`: dependency writer (`status:available` → `status:blocked`) that needs `needs-dependency`.
- `circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh:540`: blocks the original issue on a `blocked-by:` meta issue, so it needs `needs-dependency`.

title: Cloudron semver standing release policy rejects release-commit and image-digest pins
body:
## What

The semver-mode Cloudron standing release policy (GH#37697) cannot authorize a routine upstream bump of a package that pins its upstream by release commit and image digest. GH#38359 fixes the same class of failure for `upstream_mode: "commits"` only; semver-mode packages hit it too.

Observed on public `marcusquinn/cloudron-warmbly-app` (signed semver policy #34). `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --repo marcusquinn/cloudron-warmbly-app --issue 35` for routine bump PR #33 (Warmbly 0.8.1 -> 0.8.4, package 0.1.9 -> 0.1.10) printed:

```text
PR #33: standing policy #34 does not apply (NOT_ROUTINE: manifest changes beyond version and upstreamVersion)
```

Every upstream bump of that package changes, besides the whole-token `v0.8.1` -> `v0.8.4` substitution:

1. `CloudronManifest.json` `upstreamLicense.url` (`https://github.com/warmbly/warmbly/blob/<release commit SHA>/LICENSE`), pinned to the release commit as `docs/PUBLISHING.md` requires.
2. `Dockerfile` `ARG WARMBLY_COMMIT=<40-char release commit SHA>`.
3. `Dockerfile` `FROM ghcr.io/warmbly/warmbly/<svc>:vX.Y.Z@sha256:<digest>` for seven images, digests taken from the upstream release's `images.json` asset.

`check()` in `.agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py` excludes only `version`/`upstreamVersion` from manifest comparison, and the pinned-file rule allows only version-token substitution, so the policy is permanently inert for this package: each release needs `sudo aidevops approve issue`.

## Reproducer

```sh
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --repo marcusquinn/cloudron-warmbly-app --issue 35
```

Run against PR #33 head `8f5538fada4805dd014f65fb4b0c0f78f26c9bfc` (open on 2026-11-14), it printed the `NOT_ROUTINE` line above and `approval NO_APPROVAL; no merge`. The PR diff is limited to `CHANGELOG` (additions), `CloudronManifest.json` (`version`, `upstreamVersion`, `upstreamLicense.url`) and `Dockerfile` (tag, `WARMBLY_COMMIT`, seven image digests).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py`
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-evidence.py`

## How

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py`: in semver mode, accept a pinned-file/manifest change only when it is fully explained by proven upstream release identity:
  - commit SHA substitution old->new, where both SHAs are the peeled commits of the old and new upstream release tags (resolve via the GitHub API in the caller, like the commits-mode proof);
  - `@sha256:` digest substitution on a `FROM <registry>/<image>:<new tag>@sha256:` line, only where the digest equals the new release's published digest list (e.g. upstream `images.json`), or else fail closed;
  - `upstreamLicense.url` differing only by that same commit substitution.
- Reuse the GH#38359 commit-substitution code path rather than adding a second one; keep every other manifest field exact.
- If digest proof is too package-specific, add an opt-in signed policy field (for example `release_identity: {"commit_arg": "WARMBLY_COMMIT", "images_json_asset": "images.json"}`) so the signature covers the proof source.

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh` and `test-cloudron-release-evidence.py` pass, with a semver fixture whose Dockerfile changes tag, release commit and image digests plus a commit-pinned `upstreamLicense.url`: `ROUTINE_BUMP` when the SHAs/digests match the proven release, `NOT_ROUTINE` when any SHA or digest does not.
- `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --repo marcusquinn/cloudron-warmbly-app` (preview, no `--apply`) reports the policy as applicable to the next routine Warmbly bump.

Ref #38359

title: cloudron-release-approval-helper: request should supersede an unsigned same-version request bound to a closed PR
body:
## Observed

`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh request <repo> <pr>` matches existing open requests by the version marker `<!-- aidevops:cloudron-release-approval X.Y.Z -->`. When an unsigned request for the same package version is bound to a different PR (for example, a newer upstream bump that reuses an unreleased package version and supersedes the earlier PR), it fails:

```
ERROR: Existing version request has a different PR/head: refresh its signed body and obtain re-approval.
```

The helper has no refresh or supersede subcommand (usage: `request | policy-request | merge-guard | process`). Recovery needed manual steps: run `approval-helper.sh verify issue <old>` (→ `NO_APPROVAL`), comment, close the old request as not planned, then rerun `request`. The helper already supersedes unsigned *older-version* requests automatically after creating a new one (`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh` around lines 221-229).

## Expected

For an unsigned (`NO_APPROVAL`) same-version request whose PR is closed or no longer matches, `request` should supersede it (comment + close not planned) and create a fresh head-bound request, the same way as the existing older-request path. Signed or unverifiable requests should still fail closed and never be rewritten.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh` — `request` function, the `existing` branch (lines ~177-205)

## Verification

On a test package repo: create a request for PR A at version V, leave it unsigned, close PR A, open PR B with version V, then run `request <repo> B`. Expected: the old request is closed with a superseded comment, a new request is bound to PR B's head, and it prints `APPROVAL_COMMAND=`. Repeat with a signed old request; expected: fail closed with no edits.

title: feat(oauth-pool): bidirectional remote-sync of a pool account to another host/user
body:
## What

Add a first-class `oauth-pool-helper.sh remote-sync` capability. It keeps one OAuth pool account in sync both ways between the local pool and another host/user's aidevops pool (for example, a shared runner user), so a re-OAuth or token refresh on either side reaches the other automatically.

## Why (observed evidence)

A user needed one Anthropic pool account usable by aidevops/OpenCode under another Linux user on a remote host, and kept current after local re-OAuth. Plain `rsync` of `oauth-pool.json` is unsafe:

1. `pool_ops_refresh.py` stores the rotated `refresh_token` (`.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_refresh.py` line ~90), so two independent refreshers kill each other's grant. Only the newest `expires` is live.
2. A whole-file copy would overwrite the remote user's other providers/accounts.
3. Writers must honour the `oauth-pool.json.lock.d` owner-file lock (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-storage.mjs` `tryAcquireLock`).

A personal prototype (custom/ script, not in repo) proved the design:
- `get PROVIDER EMAIL POOL` / `put PROVIDER EMAIL POOL` single-entry helper. Tokens only move over stdin/stdout; `put` writes only if incoming `expires` is newer, clears `auth-error` + `authRefreshFailures*` on update, and inserts with `status: active` (carrying a live rate-limit cooldown).
- One ssh pipeline per sync: `local get | ssh remote put | local put`, with the remote side run as `sudo -n -u <user>`.
- ssh ControlMaster multiplexing is needed: rapid new connections got `kex_exchange_identification: Connection reset` from sshd (MaxStartups).
- macOS openrsync lacks `--chmod`.
- launchd `WatchPaths` on the pool file plus `StartInterval 60` (systemd timer/path unit on Linux).

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/` — add an entry get/put op (reuse existing lock/atomic-write helpers rather than duplicating them).
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh` — add `remote-sync [install|sync|status|enable|disable] --host H --remote-user U --provider P --email E`.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh` — scheduler install pattern (label `sh.aidevops.oauth-pool-remote-sync`).
- `.agents/reference/` OAuth pool docs — document the rotation hazard and that `status` prints only a sha256 fingerprint, never token bytes.

## Verification

- Offline: two temp pools with fake tokens. The newer entry flows A→B and B→A, the older never overwrites the newer, auth-error clears, other providers are untouched, and empty stdin is a no-op.
- Live: `status` shows matching refresh fingerprints on both sides after a sync. A second sync is a no-op, and the remote pool stays mode 600, owned by the remote user, with the lock released.

title: Lifecycle: retirement lock files of retired generations are never removed (5,730 accumulated)
body:
## What

Retired worktree generations leave their `retirement-<generation>.lock` file in the lifecycle state directory forever. On the maintainer's macOS host the directory now holds **5,730** zero-byte lock files (oldest from 2026-11-01). They take no space, but they cost inodes and slow every directory scan of the state dir, and the count only grows.

## Why

`worker_lifecycle/retirement.py` `_lock()` (around line 76) opens `store.directory / f"retirement-{generation}.lock"` with `O_CREAT`, flocks it, and closes the descriptor without unlinking. Leaving the file in place is deliberate for the live path: unlinking a flock file while another process may open it races (two holders of different inodes). The gap is that nothing ever removes the lock once its generation has reached a terminal retired state and no process can still need it.

## Reproducer

On a host where Pulse has retired worktrees for a few days:

```bash
fd -t f -g 'retirement-*.lock' --max-depth 1 ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/worker-lifecycle | wc -l
```

Observed 2026-11-14: `5730`. The count rises after every retirement and never falls, including after registry compaction.

## How

1. In `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/retirement.py`, add a sweep that removes `retirement-<generation>.lock` only when:
   - the generation's retirement is terminal in the registry (its final retirement event is recorded), and
   - the lock can be taken with `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)` on the same inode (`st_dev`/`st_ino` unchanged between open and unlink, matching the existing `_id(path)` check), so no holder exists at unlink time.
   Refuse (leave the file) on any unreadable state; never unlink a lock whose generation is unknown or still active.
2. Call it from registry compaction (`LifecycleRegistry.compact`, `worker_lifecycle/storage.py`), which already ages retired data, bounded per pass so a backlog of thousands does not block compaction.
3. Report the count removed and refused in the compaction result.

Reference pattern: the fail-closed, bounded sweep style in `worker_lifecycle/reclaim/sweep.py`, and the inode re-check in `_lock()` itself.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/retirement.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/storage.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_retirement.py`

## Acceptance

- After compaction, lock files of terminally retired generations are gone; locks of active or unknown generations remain.
- A lock currently held by another process is never unlinked.
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_retirement` (from `.agents/worker-lifecycle`) passes; ruff clean.

## Verification

From `.agents/worker-lifecycle`: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_retirement tests.test_storage -q`. On a host with a backlog, count `retirement-*.lock` files in the lifecycle state dir before and after one compaction pass.

## Session Origin

Observed while gathering runtime evidence for #38376 (phase 4 of #38051). Ref #38051.

title: gh-checks-wait/full-loop merge: stale Codacy PR result blocks merge after the finding is fixed
body:
## Observed

In a managed WordPress plugin repo (public, no branch protection), a PR's Codacy check stayed `ACTION_REQUIRED` after the flagged code was removed:

- Codacy's PR endpoint `GET /api/v3/analysis/organizations/gh/{org}/repositories/{repo}/pull-requests/{n}` reported `newIssues: 1`, analysed at the PR head (`isAnalysing: false`, head SHA matched).
- The issue (`rulesets-unusedcode.xml-UnusedLocalVariable`) carried the origin commit (first PR commit) and that commit's line text; the line no longer exists at head, and the line number now points at unrelated code.
- `GET .../commits/{head}/deltaIssues` returned 0 issues; local PHPMD `unusedcode` on the head file returned nothing.
- `POST .../reanalyzeCommit` with the stored `CODACY_API_TOKEN` returned 403 "Operation is not authorized".

`gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait <PR> --all` and `full-loop-helper.sh merge` treat every check as required when the branch is unprotected, so this stale Codacy state blocks the merge with no sanctioned override, while qlty "out of credits" is already classified as SKIPPED.

## Wanted

A bounded way to tell a stale Codacy PR result from a real one, so merges are not blocked by a fixed finding:

- In the checks/merge gate: when Codacy fails, query the head commit's `deltaIssues`; if it has no new issues and every PR-level issue's `lineText` is absent from the head file, report `STALE (codacy PR aggregation)` with that evidence and treat it like the qlty skip (recorded note, not a pass).
- Or document the recovery path in `reference/review-bot-gate.md` / `reference/ci-gate-policy.md` (for example a clean single-commit replacement PR), if an automatic classification is not wanted.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh` (check classification; the qlty-out-of-credits SKIPPED path is the reference pattern)
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` (merge pre-check)
- `.agents/reference/ci-gate-policy.md`, `.agents/reference/review-bot-gate.md`

## Verify

Reproduce with a PR whose first commit adds a PHPMD finding that a later commit removes; the gate should report the stale state with evidence instead of a terminal failure, and a real head-commit finding must still fail.

**Tags:** `interactive` `enhancement`

## Outcome

perf(worker): wait once, bounded, for the PR's required checks and merge in-session instead of handing every pending PR to pulse

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `worker POST_PR_HANDOFF wait for CI merge latency headless contract` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no open PR on `headless-runtime-contract.sh`; related merged work is GH#27658 (stop unbounded post-PR polling), GH#34931 (worker may merge its own PR), GH#36176 (re-verify POST_PR_HANDOFF)
- [x] File refs verified: `headless-runtime-contract.sh` lines 106-131, 241-249, 268-283 and `.agents/AGENTS.md:58` read at `origin/main` `6093070107`
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — prompt-contract change in one generator plus one always-loaded line; no runtime code change
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-14
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (productivity-mission session)
- **Issue:** GH#38388
- **Conversation context:** The user asked whether interactive full-loop sessions solve issues faster than Pulse workers, and whether worker complexity could be simplified to match. Session mining showed the main gap is after the worker opens its PR.

## What

After `commit-and-pr`, a headless worker waits for its own PR's required checks through the existing bounded helper (`full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks <PR> --timeout 200`, at most 8 chunks, about 27 minutes), then merges through `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, the same path interactive full-loop uses. A check that fails because of this PR is fixed in the same session with full context. Only work that is still pending after the bound, or that needs a human, review approval or native auto-merge, is handed to Pulse with `POST_PR_HANDOFF`.

## Why

Evidence from 2026-11-12T23:30Z to 2026-11-14T23:30Z (local read-only GitHub probes in the session workspace, not committed):

- Managed product repo A (private, placeholder name): interactive PRs 34 (31 merged, 0 rework); worker PRs 10 (7 merged, 4 needed conflict rework). Interactive issue solve p50 49 min; worker p50 287-577 min. Merge hop after the last check: interactive p50 2 min; worker p50 12, p75 55, p90 70 min.
- In repo A, one worker PR opened 3 min after dispatch, then sat unmerged 2.5 h until an interactive merge conflicted it; the repair PR took 6.5 h more. Another issue lost 9.5 h the same way.
- `marcusquinn/aidevops`: PR open-to-merge p50 interactive 23 min, worker 45 min.
- Local Pulse used at most 4 of 20 worker slots on 2026-11-14 (`pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`), so holding a slot for a bounded CI wait costs nothing measurable. Each avoided redispatch saves the ~5 min dispatch ceremony (`dedup.ceremony_total` avg 315 s) and a fresh context load.

Interactive sessions win because the same session owns the PR through merge. Workers exit at the PR (contract item 8, "Do not sleep, wait, or poll"), so every pending PR costs at least one Pulse merge pass, and slow ones collect conflicts from concurrent interactive merges.

GH#27658 removed unbounded model polling for human reviews (16 `sleep 120` loops until a 3600 s sandbox kill). This change keeps that protection: the wait is bounded, uses one helper with heartbeat output, covers required checks only, and never waits for human review or approval.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Worker contract text, one guidance line and one watchdog marker; behaviour is verified by the existing contract tests and live worker outcomes.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh:127` — Mandatory behavior 8: bounded required-check wait, one in-session repair round, then merge or `POST_PR_HANDOFF`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh:245-248` — watchdog section: allow only the bounded `wait-checks` chunks; keep the 240 s limit.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh:278-279` — pre-exit self-check wording for the new handoff condition.
- `EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md:58` — same rule in always-loaded guidance, no size increase.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh:562,565` — first-pass completion contract items 2 and 5 said "one merge attempt"/"attempt merge once"; align them with behavior 8.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-contract-clarity.sh:238-252` — assert the bounded wait, the review/approval polling ban and the no-`sleep` rule instead of the old "immediate state check" text.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh:165` — the embedded-prompt assertion quoted the old item 5 text.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:969` — `_activity_output_has_ci_wait` did not recognise `wait-checks`, so a quiet bounded wait could be killed as a stall; add the marker (hard-kill backstop unchanged).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh:80-92` — classifier case for the `wait-checks` marker.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh:786-794` — cap the last poll sleep at the remaining `--timeout` budget so the option is a real wall-clock bound.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_worker_headless_contract_text` is appended to every headless worker prompt by `headless-runtime-helper.sh`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** workers already call `full-loop-helper.sh merge` once; the change only delays that call until checks are terminal.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-headless-contract-clarity.sh`, `test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh` (via `test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`).
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because no config key is added.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed by `setup.sh` on release.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because nothing persistent changes.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the commit; workers return to one merge attempt and immediate handoff.

### Implementation Steps

1. Rewrite item 8 with the bounded wait: run `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$WORKER_REPO_SLUG" --timeout 200` up to 8 times, with one status line before each; exit 0 → merge; exit 1 → fix a failure caused by this PR, push, wait again once; exit 9 → `gh pr ready`, wait again; exit 2/8 after the bound → `POST_PR_HANDOFF`.
2. Keep the GH#27658 guard explicit: never wait for human review, approval or native auto-merge; never use `sleep` loops.
3. Align the watchdog and pre-exit text and the AGENTS.md line.
4. Run the contract tests and ShellCheck.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Pulse may merge the same green PR while the worker waits; `full-loop-helper.sh merge` and runtime classification already accept an already-merged PR (GH#34931).
- **Migration/rollback:** prompt text plus one watchdog marker; revert restores the old contract.
- **Watchdog:** each `wait-checks --timeout 200` call stays under the 240 s quiet rule because the helper now caps its last sleep at the remaining budget (before the cap, a live `--timeout 220` call on PR #38390 ran 248 s); the helper's 120 s heartbeat and the new marker defer stall kills; the hard-kill backstop and 3 h sandbox limit still apply.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older runners keep the old contract until they update; both behaviours are safe together.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a resumed session re-runs the bounded wait from the current PR state.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** API errors (exit 2) end the wait and hand off as today.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-contract-clarity.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** contract tests render the real prompt text; live check after release is worker PR open-to-merge time and the `post_pr_handoff` share in `worker-activity-helper.sh summary`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-contract-clarity.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`
- `todo/tasks/t19011-brief.md`
- `TODO.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The worker contract tells workers to wait for required checks with bounded `wait-checks` chunks and merge in-session, and still forbids waiting for human review or approval.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "wait-checks \"\\$PR_NUMBER\" --repo \"\\$WORKER_REPO_SLUG\" --timeout 200"
    path: ".agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Contract tests pass.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-contract-clarity.sh"
  ```

- [ ] After release, worker PR open-to-merge p50 in `marcusquinn/aidevops` and repo A falls below the 2026-11-14 baseline (45 min open-to-merge and 12 min merge hop respectively), measured over 24 h.

## Context & Decisions

- Chose a prompt-level bounded wait over a runtime-owned post-PR waiter for the first step: it reuses the existing helper and watchdog CI-wait handling and can be measured within a day. If token cost or watchdog kills rise, move the wait into the runtime and resume the same session on failure.
- 8 chunks × 200 s covers the observed CI p50 (21-28 min); 200 s leaves room for API fetch latency and stays below the 240 s quiet-output rule and the 3 h sandbox limit.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh:106-131` — execution contract
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh:241-283` — watchdog and pre-exit text
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:966-1008` — watchdog CI-wait deferral

title: setup.sh --non-interactive on a fresh Linux user prints warnings that need no action
body:
On a fresh Debian 13 user (systemd user manager, no prior OpenCode), `setup.sh --non-interactive` at 3.39.198 prints warnings that need no action, which makes real problems hard to spot:

1. `setup_opencode_plugins` (V1 pass) warns "aidevops OpenCode plugin was not registered; 'Anthropic Pool' may be unavailable" because `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` does not exist yet (`mcp-setup.sh` `_setup_opencode_v1_find_config`). A later stage then creates the file and prints "Re-registered aidevops plugin (was missing from config)". Creating the minimal config before the plugin stage, or skipping the warning when a later stage will write it, would remove the false alarm.
2. `cleanup_legacy_dashboard_launchagent` prints four `Failed to disable unit: Unit ... does not exist` lines (`sh.aidevops.dashboard.service/.timer`, `aidevops-dashboard.service/.timer`) on a machine that never had them. Checking `systemctl --user cat <unit>` first, or sending the disable output to /dev/null, would keep the stage quiet.
3. The OpenCode agent config generation warns "Build+ references subagent 'best-practices' but no best-practices.md found" and the same for 'ios-simulator': the Build+ subagent list names agents that are not in the release.
4. `check_quality_tools` on Linux prints "Install later: brew install shellcheck shfmt" with a newline inside the list; on apt systems `sudo apt-get install shellcheck shfmt` is the matching hint.

title: full-loop merge: deferred-cleanup marker is not git-excluded, so git add -A commits it in repos without a .agents ignore
body:
## What happened

In an interactive session, `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <repo>` merged a PR from a linked worktree and reported `LIFECYCLE_STATE=CLEANUP_DEFERRED`. It wrote `.agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred` into that worktree. The session then reused the worktree for the next PR in the same repository (a follow-up release branch from `origin/main`) and committed with `git add -A`, which AGENTS.md recommends for WIP commits. The commit picked up the marker. I caught it before pushing by diffing the commit against an earlier preflighted commit, then ran `git rm --cached` and amended.

The target repository is a WordPress plugin built from a starter. It does not ignore `.agents/`, so the marker shows up as an ordinary untracked file.

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh` (about lines 572-579) creates `${worktree_path}/.agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred` with `printf`/`mv` and never excludes it from Git. Several readers already treat it as framework state (`full-loop-helper-risk.sh` `_full_loop_runtime_paths`, `headless-runtime-worker.sh` `_HRW_DEFERRED_CLEANUP_EXCLUDE_PATHSPEC`, `worktree_recovery_cache_identity.py`), but nothing stops a plain `git add -A`/`git commit -a` from staging it in repositories without a `.agents/` ignore rule.

## Fix

When the helper writes the marker, also add the path to the worktree's local exclude file (`git -C "$worktree_path" rev-parse --git-path info/exclude`, which is shared by linked worktrees). Do the same for `.agents/loop-state` if that path is written the same way. Keep the write idempotent: append only if the line is missing. This needs no change to target repos' `.gitignore`.

## Verification

- In a scratch repo with no `.agents` ignore rule: create a linked worktree, write the marker through the helper function, then `git add -A`. `git status --porcelain` must not list the marker, and `git ls-files .agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred` stays empty.
- Existing `tests/test-full-loop-merge-worktree-cleanup.sh` and `tests/test-full-loop-wip-finalization.sh` still pass.
- Related history: #35709 (risk check counted the untracked marker), #38059 (reclaim refused marker-only worktrees).

title: Phase 5 of #38051: Stage 2: archive-then-remove for candidates that need preservation, archive always includes `commits.bundle`, verified before removal, journaled with the archive id.
body:
<!-- aidevops:generator=phase-autofile parent=38051 phase=5 -->

## What

Phase 5 of #38051: stage 2 of the reclaim sweep, **archive-then-remove**. It applies to candidates that phase 3's `classify()` marks `archive`: finished work (PR merged or issue closed, every owner ended) that still has uncommitted changes or unpushed commits. Today these are only counted (`archive_queued`) and skipped.

## Why

Design source: the maintainer decision "delete first, archive second" (https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38051#issuecomment-6848353680). Stage 1 (cheap, archive-free) runs first; stage 2 (expensive) runs after it in the same pass, so an exhausted budget never blocks the high-yield removals.

The root cause in #38056 is that a "published" archive omits `commits.bundle` and depends on the remote branch, which the merge flow deletes. Stage-2 archives must therefore always carry their own commits.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`: add an `archive --bundle-commits` option.
   - When the head is published, the option records `remote_branch_state: "bundled"` instead of `"published"`. `capture_archive_payload` (around line 463) and `archive_capacity_check` then bundle and estimate the commits.
   - With a non-`published` state, `dependency_commit()` in `worktree_archive_objects.py` makes the archive depend only on its base, and `verify-local` stops requiring the head on `origin`.
   - Default behaviour (GH#36607) is unchanged.
   - Zero commits since the base means no bundle is possible or needed. That archive depends only on the base, which lives on the default branch.
2. `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/`: add a stage-2 module. After the stage-1 loop in `sweep.py` `main()`, process the queued `archive` verdicts only under `--apply` with owners observed. For each one:
   1. Archive through the helper (`preservation.py` `_run`/`_helper` pattern: `git-only` policy, process-group timeout). Use `--bundle-commits`, `--reason post-pr-cleanup --issue N`, the repository slug and the origin default branch. Use `--unattributed` when no issue reference exists.
   2. Run `verify-local` on the archive.
   3. Remove through `host.remove`, using a CAS verifier: the evidence fingerprint must be unchanged (`decision.cas_verify`) and `source-matches ARCHIVE WORKTREE` must pass.
   4. Journal `reclaim-archived` (with the archive path and manifest sha256) before removal, then `reclaim-removed` carrying the archive id.
3. Dry runs report `archive_planned` and write nothing.
4. Do not start an archive when the remaining budget is below a minimum. Any tree left unprocessed is reported and re-judged on a later pass.
5. Repeated archive failures of the same tree go to the phase-4 reclaim quarantine, so one bad tree cannot spend every pass.
6. `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh`: add `archived=` to the Pulse log line.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-helper.sh`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/sweep.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/decision.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/progress.py`
- NEW: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/archive.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/preservation.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reclaim.py`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh`

## Acceptance

- A finished tree with uncommitted changes or unpushed commits is archived with `commits.bundle` whenever commits exist since the base. The archive passes `verify-local` even after the remote branch is deleted, and the tree is then removed.
- A source change between archive and removal refuses the removal (`evidence-changed` or source mismatch). The archive is kept, and the tree is kept.
- Archive or verify failure leaves the tree in place and is reported.
- The journal holds `reclaim-archived` and `reclaim-removed` events with the archive id. An identical replay is idempotent.
- Dry runs write no archive, journal entry, cursor or quarantine state.
- Stage 2 never runs before stage 1 finishes. A live owner, an open reference or unreadable state still refuses.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-helper.sh`
- From `.agents/worker-lifecycle`: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_reclaim tests.test_local_archive_verification -q`, then ruff and `shellcheck` on the changed shell files.
- A live dry run of `worktree-reclaim.py --budget-seconds 120 --limit 15` reports `archive_planned` and writes nothing.

## Session Origin

Auto-filed by `shared-phase-filing.sh` after phase 4 (#38376) merged; brief enriched interactively.
For #38051
