title: t19013: GH#38355 follow-up: closed-checkpoint dispatch scan must page past the 30 most recently updated closed PRs
body:
## Task


`_pmpc_reconcile_closed_checkpoints` must check every worker-branch PR that was closed unmerged since its previous complete scan, within the existing lookback. It must not stop at the 30 most recently updated closed PRs. A closed checkpoint draft must still get `auto-dispatch` back after a burst of closed-PR activity or a long pulse pause.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `closed checkpoint scan pagination pulse partial continuation window` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 1 commit (0d0eb38dc4, GH#38355) / 1 merged PR (#38370) / 0 open PRs touch the target files in last 48h (#38263 touches pulse fork reductions, not this function)
- [x] File refs verified: 6 refs checked, all present at HEAD `0d0eb38dc4`
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. Not in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`; the stop rule and stamp format are still the worker's choice
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped. The change is small and the stop-rule choice belongs to the worker

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-15
- **Session:** opencode:gh38355 full-loop closeout
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** This follows up on GH#38355 / PR #38370, released in v3.39.199. The closeout reported that the new closed-checkpoint scan reads one fixed page of closed PRs, and the maintainer asked for that limit to be captured.

## What

`_pmpc_reconcile_closed_checkpoints` must check every worker-branch PR that was closed unmerged since its previous complete scan, within the existing lookback. It must not stop at the 30 most recently updated closed PRs. A closed checkpoint draft must still get `auto-dispatch` back after a burst of closed-PR activity or a long pulse pause.

## Why

`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh:809` makes one call: `pulls?state=closed&sort=updated&direction=desc&per_page=30`. It has no pagination and no high-water mark. The scan runs only on a fresh traversal (`:806`), on the stale-blocked cadence (`PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_INTERVAL`, default 1800s, `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:960`). Sorting is by `updated_at`, so comments or labels on old closed PRs (release notes, bots) push genuine closures off the page.

Measured on 2026-11-15: this repo had 100 closed-PR updates in about 19h, roughly 5 per hour. A pulse outage of about 6h, such as the GitHub core-quota exhaustion seen during the v3.39.199 release, already exceeds 30 updates. A closure that falls off the page is never revisited. `_pmpc_list_candidates`' available-phase sweep (`:935-949`, `status:available,origin:worker` only) is a partial backstop. Issues that are not `origin:worker`, and in-review issues still assigned to the checkpoint runner (the case #38355 fixed), have no fallback and stay undispatchable.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The reference pattern is known: a bounded paginated read plus a cursor file in the existing state dir. The worker still has to choose the stop rule and the stamp semantics and record the choice. No trust boundary changes, because every restore still goes through `_pmpc_restore_closed_checkpoint_dispatch`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh:797-827`: paginate the closed-PR listing in `_pmpc_reconcile_closed_checkpoints` until reaching PRs older than the floor; persist the floor.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh:242-245`: let the `pulls?state=closed` fake serve per-page fixtures; add cases next to `test_closed_checkpoint_dispatch_recovery` (`:1152`).

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** the only caller is `_pm_reconcile_partial_continuations`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh:1020`, which ignores the return code (`|| true`).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** unchanged. Restores still go only through `_pmpc_restore_closed_checkpoint_dispatch` (`:760-795`). The new write is a per-repo stamp file under `${PULSE_PARTIAL_RECONCILE_STATE_DIR:-${HOME}/.aidevops/cache/partial-continuation}` (same dir as the traversal cursor, `:991-997`). Use a distinct filename suffix so it never collides with the cursor file `${repo_slug//\//__}`.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` (214 checks at `0d0eb38dc4`).
- **Schemas/config:** reuse `PULSE_CLOSED_CHECKPOINT_LOOKBACK_SECONDS` (default 604800, `:807`) as the hard floor. An optional page cap env var may be added; validate it the same way as `:808`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` by `setup.sh`; nothing generated.
- **Migrations/backfills:** with no stamp yet, fall back to the lookback floor. The first scan after deploy is therefore the backfill.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** reverting the commit restores the single-page read. A leftover stamp file is harmless.

### Implementation Steps

1. Read the stamp, a last-complete-scan epoch. Floor = max(stamp - margin, now - lookback). The margin, for example 3600s, absorbs clock skew and in-flight writes.
2. Page through `pulls?state=closed&sort=updated&direction=desc&per_page=100&page=N`. Apply the existing jq row filter (`:811-819`) per page. Stop when the page's oldest `updated_at` < floor, the page is short, the deadline (`$2`) is reached, or a page cap is reached. Stopping on `updated_at` is safe because `updated_at >= closed_at`.
3. Advance the stamp to the scan's start epoch only when the scan reached the floor. A deadline stop, page-cap stop or unreadable page leaves the stamp unchanged, so the next scan covers the gap again. Restores are already idempotent through the per-PR marker in `_pmpc_closed_checkpoint_release` (`:706`).
4. Keep the `review:1:` traversal gate (`:806`) so resumed pages do not rescan.
5. Run `shellcheck` and the test file. Then source the script in a shell with `gh` authenticated and call `_pmpc_reconcile_closed_checkpoints marcusquinn/aidevops $(( $(date +%s) + 120 ))` against a scratch `PULSE_PARTIAL_RECONCILE_STATE_DIR`. Confirm the stamp is written and the log shows no unexpected restores.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** two pulse hosts may scan the same repo. Each restore is already fenced by fresh reads and the per-PR marker. Write the stamp with temp-file plus `mv -f`, following `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:738`.
- **Migration/rollback:** with no stamp, the scan falls back to the lookback floor. On rollback the stamp is ignored.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older hosts keep the 30-PR read. The two versions cannot conflict, because each restore is idempotent.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a partial scan never advances the stamp, so a retry rescans the window. The marker prevents double comments.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** an unreadable page returns 1 without advancing the stamp. That keeps today's `|| true` caller semantics.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `_pmpc_reconcile_closed_checkpoints` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- **Current line count:** 25 lines
- **Estimated growth:** +25 to +35 lines
- **Projected post-change:** about 60 lines (60% of threshold)
- **Action required:** Watch. Extract a `_pmpc_closed_checkpoint_rows` page helper if the function passes 80 lines. The file is 1087 lines, under the 1500 limit.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the test file proves pagination, the stop rules and stamp semantics. ShellCheck and changed-file lint cover style gates. The scratch-dir live call in step 5 proves the production read path.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required. This is a single pulse helper; no shared contracts or root tooling change.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: paginate closed-checkpoint scan`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required. The change is to a single helper

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not change restore eligibility (`_pmpc_restore_closed_checkpoint_dispatch` and the helpers it calls) or the worktree-reuse fence from #38370.

**AI brief owner:** marcusquinn (maintainer)

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

title: npm global install falls back to sudo when the user's npm prefix has no lib/ yet
body:
`_npm_global_install_via_npm` (`.agents/scripts/setup/_common.sh`) decides that a global install needs sudo with:

    [[ ! -w "$(npm config get prefix 2>/dev/null)/lib" ]]

When the user's npm prefix is a fresh user directory (for example `npm config set prefix ~/.npm-global` with only that directory created), `<prefix>/lib` does not exist yet, so `-w` is false and setup runs `sudo npm install -g opencode-ai@latest`. On a host with passwordless sudo this installs OpenCode under root's prefix (`/usr/bin/opencode`) instead of the user's prefix, and the `~/.local/bin/opencode` shim points there.

Effects:
- A user who set a user-writable prefix to avoid sudo still gets a root-owned install.
- On a machine whose system disk is replaced while `/home` is kept (VM rebuild), the shim survives and points at a binary that is gone: `opencode: line 9: /usr/bin/opencode: No such file or directory`, and setup does not reinstall because nothing checks the shim's target.

Suggested fix: test the prefix itself and create `lib/` when the prefix is writable, e.g.

    prefix="$(npm config get prefix 2>/dev/null)"
    if [[ -w "$prefix" ]]; then mkdir -p "$prefix/lib" "$prefix/bin"; npm install -g "$pkg"; else sudo npm install -g "$pkg"; fi

and have `setup_opencode_cli` treat a shim whose target does not run as invalid, so it reinstalls.

Seen at 3.39.198 on Debian 13.

title: t19014: perf(ci-wait): resolve required check contexts once per wait, not every poll
body:
**Task ID:** `t19014` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-15 | **Started:** 2026-11-15
**Tags:** `interactive` `enhancement`

## Outcome

perf(ci-wait): resolve required check contexts once per wait, not every poll

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-15
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (t19011 / GH#38388 session)
- **Issue:** GH#38404
- **Conversation context:** t19011 (PR #38390) moves workers from immediate post-PR handoff to bounded in-session `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks` calls (up to 8 x 200 s). While measuring that wait on PR #38390, the REST core quota hit 0/5000 and the governed merge was deferred by read admission. The local API log showed `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh` making about 135 REST attempts over 6 wait calls (about 22 per 200 s call), dominated by `repos-pulls` (67) and `repos-other` (62).

## What

`wait_for_checks` in `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh` resolves the base branch's configured required contexts once per wait invocation (first successful read), not on every poll. Failed reads are not cached, so a transient error retries on the next poll.

## Why

`classify_state` (`gh-checks-wait-helper.sh:434`) calls `configured_required_contexts` (`:342`) on every poll. That function makes 3 REST reads: `repos/{repo}/pulls/{n}` (base ref), `branches/{base}/protection/required_status_checks`, and `rules/branches/{base}`. None of them change during a wait. The per-poll check fetch itself (`gh_pr_checks_observed_json`) is 1 REST identity read plus GraphQL pages, so these 3 reads are about 75% of the waiter's REST cost per poll. With t19011, each waiting worker spends them on every poll for up to about 27 minutes; several concurrent waiters compete with merges and Pulse for the same 5000/hour core quota. When admission defers a read, the wait returns exit 2 and the worker hands off, so REST spent on invariant reads directly shortens in-session ownership.

`classify_state` runs inside a command substitution (`:741`), so a global memo inside it would not persist; resolve in the loop body and pass the result in.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** One helper, one function boundary, existing fixture suite; behaviour stays identical except for fewer repeated reads.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh:696-750` — add `resolve_configured_contexts_once` (sets `_GCW_CONFIGURED_RC` / `_GCW_CONFIGURED_CONTEXTS`, caches only on exit 0); `wait_for_checks` resets the cache at wait start and calls it before `classify_state`, outside the command substitution.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh:434-457` — `classify_state` accepts optional args 7 (read exit code) and 8 (contexts); when absent, it keeps the direct call.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add the optional parameters to `classify_state`; keep the current fallback when they are omitted.
2. Resolve once in `wait_for_checks` outside the `$(classify_state ...)` substitution and pass both values.
3. Keep the zero-job (`zero_job_runs`) path unchanged; it runs only when contexts are missing after the settle window.

### Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t19014-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh` passes unchanged (116/116).

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh"
  ```

- [x] A wait of 3+ polls makes at most one `configured_required_contexts` read set (1 base read + protection + ruleset) per wait invocation.
- [x] A transient failure of the contexts read is retried on the next poll, not cached.

### Verification evidence

Controlled run with the suite's stub `gh` (call-logging prefix), `GH_TEST_MODE=required-protection`, `--timeout 2`, no sleep:

| Helper | GraphQL polls | Base reads | Protection reads | Ruleset reads |
|--------|---------------|------------|------------------|---------------|
| Before (`057a953903`) | 3-4 | 3-4 (one per poll) | 3-4 | 3-4 |
| After | 4 | 1 | 1 | 1 |

`GH_TEST_MODE=protection-error`, same settings, after: 5 polls, 5 protection reads (failure retried each poll), exit 8 (non-clear).

A live comparison on an open PR was attempted but other concurrent waiters on the same login shared the REST log, so route counts were not attributable per invocation; the stub run above is the acceptance evidence.

## Context & Decisions

- Per-invocation scope only. Caching across the 8 contract calls (file cache keyed by repo and base branch) is a possible later step; not needed for the main saving.
- A stale contexts answer cannot bypass a gate: GitHub branch protection still decides at merge time; the waiter only decides when to retry the merge.
- Related: t19011 / GH#38388 (bounded worker wait), GH#37888 (same-login REST drain attribution).

title: Phase 6 of #38051: Reclaim authorization for never-owned generations; switch profile fallback and enrolled-only readers
body:
## What

Phase 6 of #38051: Reclaim writes its own evidence-backed authorization for a never-owned enrolled generation. `profile-readme-publication-lib.sh` and the four `enrolled_only_authorized` readers switch to it. This is steps 1–3 of the maintainer decision [remove the manual ("operator-confirmed") retirement authorization](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38051#issuecomment-6847815202). Step 4 (deleting the legacy path) is phase 7.

## Why

`retire-enrolled-only --confirm` is "manual" in name only. `profile-readme-publication-lib.sh:328-346` calls it automatically as a fallback for its own prior worktree (`:612`), so `operator_confirmed: true` is a formality. Phase 7 cannot delete that path until Reclaim provides a replacement event that the readers accept.

## How

1. **Writer: new `worker_lifecycle/reclaim/unowned.py`.** It must be a leaf module importing only `storage`/`journal`: `reclaim/owners.py` imports `cleanup_plan`, so `cleanup_plan` can only import a leaf.
   - `authorize_unowned(store, path, generation, timeout)` records the facts checked:
     - owner check: no `bindings` row and no `created-worktree` receipt (the same predicate as `AdmissionRegistry.authorize_enrolled_only`, `admission.py:191-220`);
     - git state: `reclaim.host.nothing_to_lose` returns `nothing-to-lose`, so the tree is clean and HEAD is contained in a remote;
     - references: `reclaim.evidence.references(path.name)`;
     - evidence fingerprint: `reclaim.decision.fingerprint`, taken before and re-checked after the git-state check (CAS).
   - Event: `{"type": "reclaim-unowned-authorized", "schema": 1, "generation_id", "path", "fingerprint", "git_state": "nothing-to-lose", "owner_check": "never-bound", "references", "checked_at"}`.
   - The event is keyed for idempotency at `uuid5(UUID(generation), "reclaim-unowned-authorized")`. A replay finds the event and returns. The no-binding predicate, the event and the admission closure share one writer transaction, exactly like `authorize_enrolled_only`.
   - `unowned_authorized(store, generation)` is the reader: the event's type and generation match, admission is `closed`, and `_runs` is empty.
2. **Readers.** In `cleanup_plan.py`, `enrolled_only_authorized` becomes "legacy event OR `unowned_authorized`". Update its call sites: `retirement.py:257`, `recovery.py:24`, `legacy_takeover.py:44` and `cleanup_plan.py:275`. In `recovery.py:30`, record `"authorization": "reclaim"` instead of `operator_confirmed: True` when the Reclaim event was the proof.
3. **CLI.** Add a `worker-registry.py reclaim-unowned --path --repos-config --output-root` command in `registry.py`, and add the name to `refusal.py` and `cli_errors.py`. It reuses the eligibility and maintenance-scope checks in `cleanup.retire_enrolled_only` (`cleanup.py:196-237`). Evidence replaces `--confirm`, then retirement goes through `_candidate` as before (archive, verify, private move, native removal).
4. **Profile fallback.** `_profile_retire_enrolled_only_worktree` invokes `reclaim-unowned` (no `--confirm`). Rename it to `_profile_reclaim_unowned_worktree`.

Leave `retire-enrolled-only`, `authorize_enrolled_only`, `--confirm-legacy-path` and the `worker-lifecycle-state.sh:268` hint in place; phase 7 removes them.

## Acceptance

- A never-owned, clean, published enrolled tree retires through `reclaim-unowned` with no operator confirmation, and the journal holds `reclaim-unowned-authorized`.
- A dirty tree, an unpushed tree, a tree with any binding or creation receipt, or a fingerprint that changed during the check is refused with a named reason, and admission stays open.
- All four readers accept the Reclaim event, and the legacy event still works.
- A replay of the command is idempotent.

## Verification

```bash
cd .agents/worker-lifecycle && python3 -m unittest tests.test_retirement tests.test_reconstructible tests.test_reclaim tests.test_legacy_cleanup -q
ruff check --no-cache && mypy --config-file mypy.ini --platform linux && mypy --config-file mypy.ini --platform darwin   # from repo root, CI pins
shellcheck .agents/scripts/profile-readme-publication-lib.sh
```

Parent: #38051 (phase 6 of 7).

title: fix(setup): _runtime_helpers.sh npm_global_install shadows the canonical _common.sh policy (bun-only hosts cannot install OpenCode)
body:
## What

During `setup.sh`, the `npm_global_install` defined in `.agents/scripts/setup/_runtime_helpers.sh` replaces the canonical one in `.agents/scripts/setup/_common.sh`. As a result, the install policy added in PR #25532 (npm first for `opencode-ai` with a bun fallback; bun first for other packages) never runs in real setup.

## Evidence

- `setup.sh:89` sources `_common.sh`, then `setup.sh:113` sources `_runtime_helpers.sh`. The `_runtime_helpers.sh` `npm_global_install` (around line 375, after GH#38399) is defined without a guard, so it overrides `_common.sh`. Sourcing both files in that order and printing `declare -f npm_global_install` shows the `_runtime_helpers.sh` body.
- The `_runtime_helpers.sh` copy is npm-only and returns 1 when npm is missing.
- `_setup_opencode_installer` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh:752`) returns `bun` when npm is missing. Setup then prompts "Install OpenCode via bun?", and `_setup_install_opencode_package` → `npm_global_install` returns 1. **Bun-only hosts cannot install OpenCode through setup.**
- Callers expect the canonical policy. For example, `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install-opencode-services.sh:226` says "npm_global_install prefers Bun. Retry via npm".
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh` Tests 10/10b/10c extract only the `_common.sh` copy, so they pass while setup runs different code.

Found while reviewing and fixing GH#38399 (PR #38408).

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/setup/_runtime_helpers.sh`, wrap `npm_global_install` in `if ! type npm_global_install &>/dev/null; then ... fi`, following the `setup_prompt` fallback pattern in the same file and the `_npm_global_prefix_needs_sudo` fallback from GH#38399. Then `_common.sh` stays canonical whenever it is sourced, and the fallback still covers curl bootstrap.
2. Do not change `_common.sh` policy.

## Acceptance

- After sourcing `_common.sh` then `_runtime_helpers.sh`, `npm_global_install` is the `_common.sh` definition (it calls `_npm_global_install_via_npm`).
- With bun on PATH and no npm, `npm_global_install opencode-ai@latest` runs `bun install -g opencode-ai@latest`.
- Sourcing `_runtime_helpers.sh` alone still defines a working `npm_global_install`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/setup/_runtime_helpers.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-opencode-cli.sh`
- Source-order check: source `_common.sh` then `_runtime_helpers.sh`, then `declare -f npm_global_install`.

## Ripple

On hosts with bun, setup.sh installs generic npm packages (serve-sim, MCP servers, Codex, gws, cf) through bun first, as #25532 intended and as the Droid retry comment assumes. OpenCode stays npm-first.

Tier: `tier:simple`. One file, guard-only change.

title: fix: registry validation zipapp omits modules its bundled tests import (retirement_proof)
body:
## What

The portable registry validation zipapp (`python3 -B -m worker_lifecycle.bundle --suite registry`) bundles an exact module allowlist (`REGISTRY_SOURCES` / `REGISTRY_TESTS` in `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/bundle.py`). The bundled test `tests/test_retirement.py` imports `worker_lifecycle.retirement_proof` (already true on `main`), which is not in `REGISTRY_SOURCES`. Loading the bundled suite therefore fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'worker_lifecycle.retirement_proof'`, and `integration_validation.TEST_MODULES` includes `tests.test_retirement`.

GH#38405 hit the same class of gap for production modules (`cleanup_plan.py`/`recovery.py` importing `reclaim.unowned`) and fixed it by listing the reclaim closure. Nothing currently fails when the allowlist drifts from the real import closure.

## Evidence

```text
$ python3 -B -m worker_lifecycle.bundle --suite registry --output <tmp>/registry.pyz
$ python3 -I -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '<tmp>/registry.pyz'); import tests.test_retirement"
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'worker_lifecycle.retirement_proof'
```

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/bundle.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_events.py`

## How

1. body:
**Task ID:** `t19015` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-15 | **Started:** 2026-11-15
**Tags:** `interactive` `enhancement`

## Outcome

perf(pulse): a drained cycle exits at the next stage boundary instead of running its full maintenance tail

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-15
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (aidevops productivity mission, parent t19002 / GH#38332)
- **Parent:** GH#38332 (dispatch-starvation source flagged in its 2026-11-14 supervisor evidence comment)
- **Conversation context:** Measured on one 20-slot macOS runner while 3/20 slots were in use and the ready queue was non-empty.

## What

When a deploy asks the running Pulse cycle to drain (GH#37907, `LOCKDIR/drain_requested`), that cycle can no longer dispatch. It must stop running its remaining deferrable stages and exit at the next stage boundary. The activated bundle then starts on the next scheduler tick and adopts the handed-off census (GH#38048).

## Why

GH#37907 specified that a drained cycle "finishes the in-flight candidates, skips the floor refill and any new census, and exits the cycle so launchd starts the activated bundle". Only the dispatch half was implemented. `_dispatch_compute_capacity`, the serial and parallel dispatch loops, and the floor refill stop dispatching, but every other stage still ran. That covered the rest of `_run_preflight_stages`: cleanup/ledger, capacity, label maintenance (up to 488 s), trusted NMR reconcile, post-label refill, the housekeeping launch, and prefetch (about 426 s). It also covered the whole `_pulse_run_deterministic_pipeline`: orphan reaper, stale runs, Dependabot, merge pass, PR sweeps, TODO sync, graph rebuild, blocked refresh, canonical maintenance, and `dashboard_freshness_check` with its 600 s timeout.

Evidence, 2026-11-13T03:00Z to 2026-11-15T01:56Z (45.8 h). `pulse-cycle-index.jsonl` was correlated with the 41 bundle activations named in `pulse.log`:

| Measure | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Cycles running when a bundle activated (drained) | 40 of 64 (62%), 73% of cycle wall time |
| Time from activation to drained-cycle exit | p50 849 s, p90 1560 s |
| Total time alive with dispatch suppressed by a drain | 36,850 s (10.2 h, 22% of the window) |
| `pulse.log` drain skips | 62 `Dispatch_max skipped`, 54 `stopping early`, 84 floor refills stopped, against 108 `Dispatch_max: available=` |

Same-version drift redeploys and releases activate a bundle about every 66 minutes. The drain tail therefore costs about one sixth of every hour of dispatch time, and it also delays the new code it was meant to accelerate.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** One helper adds stage-boundary checks to three orchestration functions. Dispatch, claim and lock semantics are unchanged.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` — adds `_pulse_cycle_drain_exit <phase>` next to `_pulse_drain_requested_bundle`. It returns 0 when the drain marker names this cycle's lock owner and logs `Cooperative drain: skipping remaining cycle stages` once per cycle, with the `pulse_drain_fast_exit` stat. It also releases `_PULSE_MAIN_DISPATCH_RESERVE_S`, and marks `_PULSE_PREFETCH_DEGRADED=1` when prefetch has not run, so a GH#38162 drain-escape supervisor treats the previous cycle's STATE_FILE as incomplete (GH#34000). `PULSE_DRAIN_FAST_EXIT=0` disables it.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` (`_run_preflight_stages`) — checks once after mechanical blocker re-arm and once after early dispatch. The second check returns the promoted-prefetch rc, so a hard prefetch failure still aborts the cycle.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` (`_pulse_run_deterministic_pipeline`, `_pulse_drain_cycle_final_refill`) — checks before each phase. Drained paths still drain prefetch counters and accumulate merge health. The cycle-final refill leaves its trigger for the activated bundle.
- `EDIT: TODO.md` — task entry; records t19014 completion (PR #38407).

### Unchanged by design

- `_pulse_run_supervisor_phase` keeps its drain, census-handoff (GH#38048), starvation-escape (GH#38162) and deferral (GH#38210) logic.
- `_pulse_record_cycle_terminal` still records the cycle.
- In-flight stages finish; checks run only at boundaries.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck -x -P .agents/scripts .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-permission-block-breaker.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t19015-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A drained cycle logs `Cooperative drain: skipping remaining cycle stages` once and runs no further preflight or pipeline stage after the boundary where the drain was first seen.
- [ ] An undrained cycle runs every stage in its current order, and a drain marker that names another lock owner is ignored.
- [ ] Supervisor-phase drain behaviour, census handoff and the starvation escape are unchanged; a drain that skipped prefetch marks the state incomplete for the supervisor.
- [ ] `PULSE_DRAIN_FAST_EXIT=0` restores current behaviour.
- [ ] Runtime: drained-cycle exit p50 falls below 300 s over 24 h (from 849 s).

## Context & Decisions

- An alternative was to keep dispatching from the old bundle until it exits naturally. That removes four checks, but the new code would still wait about 14 minutes at p50 and the drained cycle would still run a full maintenance tail. Fast exit matches the GH#37907 design and brings both dispatch and activation forward.
- The skipped stages are either cadence-gated or run again in the activated bundle's first cycle. The standalone merge routine (120 s launchd) covers the merge pass, and the next cycle starts the async housekeeping lane.
- Back-to-back activations could keep skipping the maintenance tail. Drift redeploys are debounced to one per hour, and a drained cycle now exits within minutes, so the next cycle normally completes.

</details>

title: fix: reclaim never-owned authorization — stale event after refused replay; legacy/Reclaim recovery-event collision (follow-up to #38405)
body:
## What

Two edge cases in the phase-6 Reclaim never-owned authorization (#38405, parent #38051), found in independent review. Neither loses data, because retirement still archives and verifies before any removal. Both leave misleading or stuck state.

1. **A stale authorization survives a refused replay.** Suppose a process crashes after `AdmissionRegistry.close_unowned` commits `reclaim-unowned-authorized` and closes admission, but before the retirement plan is recorded. If the tree is then edited, a second `reclaim-unowned` run refuses (`uncommitted-changes`). The first event and the closed admission remain, and `unowned_authorized()` never compares the stored `fingerprint` with the current tree. `cleanup_pass` or `cleanup-worktree` can then retire the changed tree on the old authorization. The archive protects the data, but the refusal output is wrong.
2. **Mixed legacy and Reclaim recovery evidence can collide.** `recovery.recovery_evidence` writes `retirement-recovered` under one event ID whatever the proof kind. A legacy `retire-enrolled-only --confirm` run that dies before its plan is recorded stores `{"operator_confirmed": true}`. A later `reclaim-unowned` run builds `{"authorization": "reclaim"}` under the same ID. `store._event` then raises `StoreConflict("event-id-payload-conflict")` and the tree stays stuck. This fails closed and is transitional until phase 7 removes the legacy path.

## Reproducer

Both cases come from code review; no production reproduction yet.

1. In a disposable store, run `reclaim.unowned.authorize` on a clean, pushed, never-owned tree. Then write an untracked file into the tree. Then call `never_owned.reclaim_unowned`. The result is `reclaim-refused`/`uncommitted-changes`, yet `unowned_authorized(store, generation)` still returns True.
2. Store `retirement-recovered` with `{"operator_confirmed": true}` (the legacy `recovery_evidence` payload) for a generation. Then call `recovery_evidence` for that generation with a Reclaim authorization present. It raises `StoreConflict("event-id-payload-conflict")`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/unowned.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/never_owned.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/recovery.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup_plan.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_retirement.py`

## How

- **Files:** `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/unowned.py` (`authorize`, `unowned_authorized`), `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/never_owned.py` (`reclaim_unowned`), `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/recovery.py` (`recovery_evidence`, the event key near the `retirement-recovered` uuid5).
- **Case 1:** when `_checked` refuses and an authorization event already exists for the generation, return a distinct status such as `reclaim-refused` with `stale_authorization: true`. Then do one of these:
  - make the cleanup readers fail closed until a fresh check passes, for example by comparing the stored `fingerprint` with `reclaim.decision.fingerprint(path)` wherever a path is available (`cleanup_plan.never_owned_authorized` callers);
  - or reopen admission only when no retirement plan exists.

  Reopening must not race `admit` or a planned retirement, so prefer the reader-side fingerprint comparison.
- **Case 2:** when `retirement-recovered` already exists, reuse its stored payload. Alternatively, key the event by proof kind. Keep replay idempotent.
- **Pattern:** follow the existing tests in `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_retirement.py` (`test_reclaim_unowned_*`).

## Verification

- `cd .agents/worker-lifecycle && python3 -m unittest tests.test_retirement tests.test_bundle`. Add one regression test per case: crash after authorization then edit; and a legacy recovery event followed by Reclaim.
- Ruff, and mypy with `--config-file mypy.ini` for both `--platform linux` and `--platform darwin`.

## Related

Ref #38051
Ref #38405

title: Local-only egress gate: title generation bypasses chat.params, can reach a non-local provider (GH#34125 follow-up)
body:
## Description

Operator-bound local-only sessions (GH#34125, `AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_POLICY=local-only`)
enforce the egress gate (`assertLocalOnlyEgress`) inside `chat.params`. Title
generation never invokes `chat.params` at all, so the title sub-call (and its
`small_model` fallback) is invisible to the gate.

## Evidence

Reproduced live with a throwaway config (`enabled_providers: ["mac-local",
"anthropic"]`, no `small_model`/`agent.title.model` pin) and
`AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_DEBUG=1`. The bound session's main turn correctly ran on
`mac-local` (no leak there), but `~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-plugin.log`
recorded, for that same session ID:

```
provider-auth: redistributed 4 system blocks (4021 chars) to user message to
  stay under third-party detection threshold (... session=<that session>)
cache-stability: session=<that session> family=aux segment=history ...
```

Both log lines only fire inside the Anthropic-native-provider request-body
pipeline (`provider-auth-body.mjs`, used only for genuine Anthropic API
traffic). No `VAULT_POLICY_DENIED` was ever logged for that session. The aux
(title) request reached Anthropic's request-body construction with zero gate
visibility — `chat.params` never saw it to deny it.

## Fix (already on a branch, PR opened, not merged)

`title-routing.mjs` (`applyLocalOnlyTitleRouting`), wired into
`config-hook.mjs` after `applyCompactionRouting`: when bound and the primary
`config.model` is already a local, egress-verified provider, force both
`agent.title.model` and `small_model` onto that same primary model,
unconditionally overriding any non-local pin. Tested with a new
`tests/test-title-routing.mjs` (6 cases); `tests/test-model-routing.mjs` (23)
and `tests/test-local-only-policy.mjs` (23, including the real-plugin
sentinel tests) still pass.

title: Independent review routes cannot read linked-worktree diffs in OpenCode (research-only staging, ai-research OAuth)
body:
## Problem

`reference/review-core.md` requires independent review for high/critical changes, but in OpenCode the documented fresh-context routes could not read a linked-worktree diff during GH#38405 (phase 6 of #38051):

- `research-only` subagent refused paths outside `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/research-staging/`, and refused staging entirely when any credential-like filename existed in that directory.
- `ai-research` (`thinking`/`standard` tiers) failed Anthropic OAuth inside its isolated runtime.
- `specialist-advisor` / `domain-focused` need a JSON evidence envelope; there is no documented one-command way to build that envelope from a worktree diff (the blind packet path in `reference/agent-routing.md` "Blind acceptance review" covers acceptance, not code review).

What worked: `Task subagent_type=general` with an explicit read-only, no-delegation prompt that runs `git diff origin/main...HEAD` in the worktree. That review found a real major defect (process census ordered after authorization), fixed before merge in PR #38418.

## Proposed fix

1. `.agents/reference/agent-routing.md` ("Blind acceptance review" section, ~line 155) and `.agents/reference/review-core.md` (~line 70 "Provenance", ~line 145): document a supported code-review route for a linked-worktree diff, including how to stage the diff for `research-only` (e.g. `review-evidence-helper.sh` writing the bundle into research-staging) and the fallback order when a route fails.
2. Make the research-staging credential-filename refusal report which file blocked it, so the parent can clean it rather than abandon the route.
3. Optional: `ai-research` should fail with a clear auth-route diagnostic rather than a raw OAuth error.

## Verification

- In OpenCode, an independent reviewer can read a staged worktree diff via the documented route without `general`.
- `rg -n "research-staging" .agents/reference/agent-routing.md .agents/reference/review-core.md` shows the documented route.

Paths for item 2/3 are not yet identified; start with `rg -n "research-staging" .agents/` and `rg -n "credential" .agents/scripts/*research*`.

title: Local-only egress gate: log content-free denials and binding state so background (title) blocks are diagnosable
body:
## Problem

When the local-only egress gate (GH#34125) denies a background model request, nothing is logged. The request is refused correctly, but `~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-plugin.log` shows no record of the denial. Background requests include OpenCode title generation (`agent=title`, `small: true`) and other requests whose failure never shows up as a session error.

So operators cannot tell "the gate blocked it" apart from "the gate was never bound". In #38420 the reporter spent about 2 hours on a misdiagnosis. They saw a `provider-auth: redistributed ...` line, found no `VAULT_POLICY_DENIED` in the plugin log, and concluded that title generation bypasses the gate. A live A/B during review showed that the gate does block `agent=title` when bound. The reported signature appears only when the session is unbound.

## Evidence

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/local-only-policy.mjs` `assertLocalOnlyEgress` / `deny()` only throws a `LocalOnlyPolicyError`. It never logs.
- Callers: `index.mjs:280`, `index.mjs:759` (V1 `chat.params`), `v2.mjs:517`, `v2.mjs:551-553` (V2 `context`/`http`).
- OpenCode `ensureTitle` does not surface title-stream failures as `session.error`, so `provider-error-diagnostics.mjs` (`localFailureCheck`) never sees a title denial.
- Repro, bound run: `stream providerID=anthropic ... agent=title`, then silence in both the OpenCode log and the plugin log.

## Proposed change

1. Emit one content-free line through the plugin console router before each egress denial throws. Suggested form: `[aidevops] local-only: denied surface=<chat|context|http> agent=<name|unknown> provider=<id|unknown> session=<id|none> reason=<non-local-provider|non-loopback-endpoint>`.
   - Never log the endpoint URL, message content or credentials.
   - Do it in the callers, or pass an optional logger into `assertLocalOnlyEgress`, so the pure function stays side-effect free.
2. At plugin init, log the binding state once (`bound`, `reason`, `localProvidersSource`, provider count), content-free. This lets operators confirm that the serving process is bound.
3. Document both lines in `.agents/reference/vault.md` (local-only section), with the diagnostic hint: "no `local-only: bound` line means this process is not bound; attached TUIs inherit the server's env, not the client's".

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/local-only-policy.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-local-only-policy.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/vault.md`

Changes by file: `local-only-policy.mjs` gets an optional logger param or an exported formatter. In `index.mjs`, change the two `chat.params` call sites and add the init log near `initLocalOnlyPolicy`. In `v2.mjs`, change the `context`/`http` call sites and add the init log. The test file extends the sentinel harness. `vault.md` gets the diagnostic note.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-local-only-policy.mjs` still passes. Extend the existing real-plugin sentinel harness (`sentinel: bound session blocks a remote provider before send`) to assert that the denial line is printed and that it contains no sentinel content.
- Manual: with a throwaway `OPENCODE_CONFIG` (`model: ollama/<fake>` on loopback, `small_model: anthropic/<model>`), run `AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_POLICY=local-only opencode run --print-logs "hi"` and confirm `local-only: denied surface=chat agent=title provider=anthropic`. Without the env var, confirm that no `local-only: bound` line appears.

body:
**Task ID:** `t19016` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-15 | **Started:** 2026-11-15
**Tags:** `interactive` `bug`

## Outcome

perf(profile): project OpenCode usage rows per table instead of materializing the full message history

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-15
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (aidevops productivity mission, parent t19002 / GH#38332)
- **Conversation context:** Host contention diagnosis on the 20-slot macOS Pulse runner. Load average was 87 on 16 cores while Pulse census scans and dispatch pre-launch checks were running slowly.

## What

`_get_model_usage_from_opencode` in `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh` should compute the all-time model-usage table from small projected rows. It must not copy every message's raw JSON into a SQLite temp B-tree. The output must stay byte-for-byte identical.

## Why

The query builds `all_messages AS (SELECT session_id, data FROM message UNION ALL SELECT session_id, data FROM archive.message)`. Later CTEs reference it twice, through the main `GROUP BY` and the `total_session_count` scalar subquery, so SQLite materializes it (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`: `MATERIALIZE all_messages`). On this install that copies about 9.2 GB of message JSON (2.19 GB main and 6.99 GB archive, 1.1M rows) to temp storage before any aggregation. The hourly `sh.aidevops.profile-readme-update` launchd job runs at Nice 10 with `LowPriorityBackgroundIO`, so that copy took hours:

| Evidence | Value |
| --- | --- |
| r908 executions.jsonl durations | 8,320 s, 18,561 s; the 2026-11-14T20:24Z run was still running at 7 h 19 m |
| Runs back-to-back (StartInterval 3600) | continuous for at least 4 days (`profile-readme-update.log` start times) |
| The one sqlite3 query still running at diagnosis | 62 min |
| Same aggregation, projected per table (measured on the real DBs) | 15 s, 55 models, 1,044,716 requests |
| Observability-DB queries in the same run | 3 s and 1 s; not a cause |

The hourly job is a background statistics task. It held sustained temp-file I/O on the same host that runs Pulse, its workers and the interactive sessions.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** One SQL restructure in one shell library. The output contract is unchanged and was verified for equality on a sampled fixture.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh` — add `_opencode_assistant_rows_sql <table>`, which emits the existing projection and filter for one table. `_get_model_usage_from_opencode` builds `assistant_messages_raw` as the main projection, `UNION ALL` the archive projection when the archive exists. The later CTEs and the final aggregate stay unchanged. Only the small projected rows can be materialized.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck -x -P .agents/scripts .agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh`
- `TODO.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` for the OpenCode usage query never materializes raw `data` columns.
- [ ] Output is identical to the previous query with and without the archive DB.
- [ ] The existing profile README boundary test passes.
- [ ] Runtime: the next r908 runs after deploy complete in minutes, not hours.

## Context & Decisions

- A TTL cache for all-time totals was rejected. It would still need a multi-hour scan once a day, and the defect is the query shape, not the cadence.
- `_token_totals_from_opencode_db` already projects inside each `UNION ALL` branch, and the observability queries are flattened by SQLite (measured at 1–3 s), so they are unchanged.

title: Worktree cleanup never removes on Linux hosts with lingering or SSH sessions: non-dumpable same-UID tasks make the path census permanently uncertain
body:
## What

On a shared Linux host, `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto` removes almost no
worktrees. Each removal fails closed with
`managed-worktree: ValueError: same-boot process census active or unavailable`
(or `CalledProcessError: evidence unavailable`) and then reports
`Skipped <branch> - cleanup lease was not acquired`. The pulse's finished-worktree
reclaim on the same host reports `refused=119`. On the observed host, two
operators' linked worktrees had grown to several hundred GB and `/home` was at
94–96% while cleanup was running.

## Root cause (observed, read-only)

`worktree_process_census.path_census()` requires `uncertain == 0`
(`worktree_lifetime_quiescence.empty_census`). `collect_path_references()`
counts every **same-UID task whose `/proc/<pid>/{cwd,fd,environ}` raises
`PermissionError`** as uncertain. Some same-UID processes are always
non-dumpable on a normal Linux login host, so the census can never be empty:

| Operator | Uncertain tasks | Non-dumpable same-UID processes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | 53 (stable across 3 samples) | `ssh-agent` ×33, `sshd` ×17 (per-session privsep children), `gpg-agent` ×2, `(sd-pam)` ×1 |
| B | 4 (stable across 3 samples) | `gpg-agent` ×2, `(sd-pam)` ×1, `ssh-agent` ×1 |

- `(sd-pam)` exists for every user with a systemd user manager. Lingering
  users, who need it to run routines, always have one.
- An `sshd` session child exists for every open SSH session.
- No task of either kind referenced the candidate worktree (`references: 0`);
  only `uncertain` blocked removal.

Result: on any Linux host where the operator has lingering enabled or an open
SSH session, the framework cannot remove worktrees.

## Reproduce

As the affected user, for a merged and idle worktree path:

```python
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.expanduser("~/.aidevops/agents/scripts"))
import worktree_process_census as c
print(c.path_census("<worktree path>"))   # status available, references 0, uncertain > 0
```

Then classify the uncertain tasks by `comm`: they are the non-dumpable processes
listed above.

## Suggested fix directions (needs design review; keep fail-closed)

1. Non-dumpable tasks owned by root-executed binaries (`sshd`, `(sd-pam)`) are
   created by privileged setuid/PAM paths. An unprivileged process cannot
   `chdir` them into a worktree, but `comm` is mutable, so do not trust names.
   Instead, verify immutable facts readable without dumpability, for example
   `/proc/<pid>/stat` (start time, ppid chain to a root-owned parent) together
   with `status` `CapEff`/`NoNewPrivs`.
2. An optional, narrowly scoped privileged census helper (root via sudoers,
   read-only `/proc` path matching for one path, output = counts) for
   multi-user Linux hosts.
3. In all cases, report the uncertain-task classes in the skip reason. Today
   the message `cleanup lease was not acquired` hides the real cause.

## Acceptance

- [ ] On a Linux host with lingering enabled and an open SSH session, `clean
      --auto` removes a merged, clean, idle worktree that no process references.
- [ ] A worktree that a same-UID process actually uses (cwd/fd) is still refused.
- [ ] Skip output names the census uncertainty class instead of only "lease not
      acquired".

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_process_census.py` (`collect_path_references`,
  `inspect_path_references`)
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_quiescence.py` (`empty_census`, caller)
- Caller message: the `managed-worktree` removal path in
  `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh` / `worktree-clean-lib.sh`

**Task ID:** `t19017` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-15
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug`

## Outcome

fix(opencode-db-archive): an archive-DB event-expiry deferral must not skip the live-DB session move

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-15
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (aidevops productivity mission, parent t19002 / GH#38332)
- **Conversation context:** Found while diagnosing a 62 GB live `opencode.db` whose hourly archive had not completed in more than 72 hours (21 consecutive deferrals).

## What

In `cmd_archive`, a deferral from the optional archived-event expiry pass (`_archive_expire_events` returns 2 when `opencode-archive.db` has any holder) should skip only the expiry. The primary work, moving eligible sessions out of the live DB, should still run. The command keeps returning 2 overall so the async scheduler still treats the pass as incomplete and retries.

## Why

`.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` `cmd_archive` (around line 1175) runs `_archive_expire_events ... || return $?`. Any reader of the archive DB therefore cancels the whole live-DB archive for that cycle. Examples are the profile README model-usage query (`ATTACH ... AS archive`), session-time scans and session lookups. Evidence in `~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-db-archive.log` at 2026-11-15T03:00Z: `Archive event expiry deferred — archive holder state is active or unknown`, then `rc=2` for the main DB, with no retention, preflight or batch lines. That cycle never reached the session move.

The session move itself does not check archive-DB holders. Only `_archive_mutation_preflight` gates the active DB, and SQLite WAL allows a write while readers are attached. Blocking the move on archive-DB readers is therefore stricter than the move needs and inconsistent with its own checks.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** One control-flow change in one function, covered by an existing suite.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` — in `cmd_archive`, capture the expiry rc. Return immediately for rc 1 or 3 (errors). For rc 2, continue to `_archive_mutation_preflight` and the move. At the end, if the move path returned 0 and expiry returned 2, return 2. With `--events-only`, return the expiry rc unchanged.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh` — only if an existing case asserts the old early return. Adjust that assertion. Add no new harness.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck -x -P .agents/scripts .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An expiry deferral (rc 2) no longer prevents the session move in the same invocation.
- [ ] The overall rc remains 2 when expiry was deferred, so the scheduler does not record a complete pass.
- [ ] Expiry errors (rc 1 or 3) still stop the command.
- [ ] The existing archive test suite passes.

## Context & Decisions

- Low frequency: 10 occurrences across the whole archive log. The main trigger, the hours-long profile README query, was fixed by t19016 / PR #38427. Other archive-DB readers remain, so the coupling is still worth removing.
- Not in scope: the live DB's 90-day interactive retention (filed separately) and the 60 s per-DB budget.

**Task ID:** `t19018` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-15
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `feat`

## Outcome

feat(backups): detect a Backblaze safety freeze or stale last upload and surface it as a user action

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-15
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (aidevops productivity mission, parent t19002 / GH#38332)
- **Conversation context:** Host I/O diagnosis showed the Backblaze client had not uploaded a file in 7.5 days. Nothing in aidevops noticed or told the user.

## What

`optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh` gains a read-only Backblaze health check, run on macOS when `/Library/Backblaze.bzpkg` exists, that reports one of:

- `ok` — last upload recent and no freeze
- `stale:<hours>` — last upload older than a threshold (default 48 h)
- `safety_frozen:<hint>` — the client reports a safety freeze

A non-`ok` result is surfaced through an existing user-attention channel as a short human action, for example: "Backblaze backup frozen since <date>; open Backblaze and resolve the safety freeze (needs your private encryption key)". It is not an issue the user has to read.

## Why

On this host the newest `bztransmit` log repeats, every pass since 2026-11-08 19:29:

```text
ERROR BzUiUtil::Get_safety_frozen_StateFromLastSyncHostInfoXml - client is safety_frozen with hint: bzcf_missing_on_client
... this client is safety frozen and a PRIVATE_ENCRYPTION_KEY, so not attempting silent self_repair
```

`bzreports_lastfilestransmitted/bzstat_lastfile_transmitted.xml` has `date="20261107155908"`. Daily `bztransmit` logs grew from about 1 MB to 50–72 MB while the client retried every 5 s. Only a human with the private key can resolve this, and the framework already inspects Backblaze configuration (`_backblaze_apple_exclusions`, `_backblaze_path_statuses`) but never its health. Offsite backup silently stopped for a week.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** One read-only probe in an existing helper, plus routing to an existing notification path.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh` — add `_backblaze_health`, following the existing `_backblaze_*` helpers near line 343. Read `gmt_millis` from `.../bzreports_lastfilestransmitted/bzstat_lastfile_transmitted.xml`. Scan only the newest `bzlogs/bztransmit/bztransmit*.log` for the last `safety_frozen with hint: <hint>` line. Never print other XML attributes, which can contain account identifiers. Missing or unreadable files report `unknown`, never `ok`. Paths must be overridable by env, like `AIDEVOPS_BACKBLAZE_BZINFO`.
- `EDIT: .agents/workflows/optimise-macos-indexing-backups.md` — one line documenting the health result and the user action.
- Notification route: unknown path. Find the existing user-attention or notice channel (for example `rg -n 'attention|notify|toast' .agents/scripts/*-helper.sh`) and reuse it. Do not create a new channel.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck -x -P .agents/scripts .agents/scripts/optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/optimise-macos-indexing-backups.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The health result is one of `ok`, `stale:<hours>`, `safety_frozen:<hint>`, `unknown` or `not-installed`, and is read-only.
- [ ] No account identifiers or encryption fields are printed.
- [ ] A non-`ok` result reaches the user as a one-line action through an existing channel.
- [ ] The existing helper tests pass.

## Context & Decisions

- The framework cannot resolve the freeze itself: it needs the user's private encryption key, which must never pass through AI. Detection and a precise action line are the automatable part.

**Task ID:** `t19019` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-15
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `feat`

## Outcome

perf(opencode-db): restore archived interactive sessions on resume so the live DB can keep 30 days instead of 90

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-15
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (aidevops productivity mission, parent t19002 / GH#38332)
- **Conversation context:** Host contention diagnosis on the 20-slot Pulse runner (load ~87 on 16 cores). Every full-file consumer of the live OpenCode DB scales with its size.

## What

1. Resuming an archived interactive session (`opencode --session ses_...` or the aidevops resume or lookup path) restores it from `opencode-archive.db` first, as headless workers already do (`_seed_worker_db_session_context` → `opencode-db-archive.sh restore --session <id>`).
2. Once (1) ships, the default interactive live retention (`OPENCODE_DB_ARCHIVE_INTERACTIVE_RETENTION_DAYS`, currently 90) drops to 30.

## Why

Measured on this host on 2026-11-15:

| Fact | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Live `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` | 62.2 GB, `freelist_count=0` (all live pages) |
| Sessions in live DB / older than 30 d / oldest | 7,253 / 3,250 / 2026-09-23 (53 days) |
| Approximate growth | about 1.2 GB per day, so about 105 GB at the 90-day steady state |
| `message` table share | about 2.2 GB; the rest is mostly `part` (tool output) |

Every full-file consumer of the live DB scales with that size:

- Time Machine includes the file and copies changed files whole. It completes a backup every 4–5 h here.
- Backblaze queued it hourly for a "large file requires disk copy".
- Whole-history readers (profile README, session-time) scan it.
- VACUUM needs a DB-sized rewrite, which is unreachable on always-on hosts (`reference/opencode-maintenance.md`).

Interactive retention is 90 days because archived interactive sessions cannot be resumed without a manual `restore`.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** The resume hook location must be found, and must cover the TUI launch paths without breaking non-aidevops OpenCode use.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/opencode-session-restart-helper.sh` (interactive resume path) — restore before OpenCode opens the session; a missing archive is a no-op. Other interactive launch paths, such as the opencode-aidevops plugin session start, are unknown: find them with `rg -n 'restore --session|_seed_worker_db_session_context|--session' .agents/scripts .agents/plugins`. Reuse `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-restore.sh`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` — `DEFAULT_INTERACTIVE_RETENTION_DAYS` from 90 to 30, only after the resume restore is verified.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/opencode-maintenance.md` — retention table and the resume behaviour.

### Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-restore.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-session-restart-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/opencode-maintenance.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`

_Integration scope recovery (worker, 2026-11-15): the stated verification test asserts the old 90-day default (sessions 89/91 days old in its split-retention case), so its boundary must move to 30 days for the acceptance criterion "existing archive tests pass". No other file is added._

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Resuming an archived interactive session through the aidevops resume path restores it with subagent children and opens normally.
- [ ] The default interactive retention is 30 days, and the env override still works.
- [ ] The existing archive tests pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Halting growth is the first outcome: archived rows free pages that later writes reuse. Shrinking the file still needs a maintenance-window VACUUM. Do not force one here.
- Rejected: excluding the live DB from backups. Session history is valuable, and a backup exclusion trades data safety for I/O.

title: privacy guard: gh-write-helper still blocks a public-repo-tracked domain in issue/PR bodies after #38231
body:
## Observed

On v3.39.195, `gh-write-helper.sh issue create` and `pr create` against a public plugin repo were blocked with `[privacy-scan][BLOCK] ... <domain> (basename of <owner>/<domain>)`. `<domain>` is the public company domain. A private repo shares the name, but the domain is already tracked on many lines of the target public repo (plugin header `Author URI`, Pro Plugins URLs, docs). After merge, `full-loop-helper.sh merge` was blocked the same way and could not record the qlty skipped-check note in the PR body.

#38228 / PR #38231 (merged 2026-11-14, v3.39.191) was meant to exempt entities already present in the target public repo's tracked tree, for pushes and public writes. The pre-push path may be covered, but the issue/PR body path (`gh-write-helper.sh` → `privacy_scan_public_text()`) still blocks. Each write needed `AIDEVOPS_GH_PRIVACY_BYPASS=1`, which trains agents to bypass the guard.

The commands ran from the target repo's canonical checkout (where `git grep -F <domain>` finds matches), with `--repo <owner>/<public-repo>`.

## Expected

For a public write with `--repo OWNER/REPO`, an entity found in that repo's tracked tree on its default branch is not a new disclosure. The check should resolve the tree from `--repo` (local clone from repos.json, or `gh api` search as a fallback), not only from the current directory. The same applies when `full-loop-helper.sh merge` edits the PR body.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh`: `privacy_scan_public_text()` and the public-tree exemption added in PR #38231; check how the target repo's tree is chosen for issue/PR bodies.
- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`: how `--repo` is passed to the scan.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`: the post-merge PR body edit (qlty skipped-check note).
- `.agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard.sh`: add a case: a body containing an entity tracked in the target repo, written with `--repo`, passes.

## Verification

`gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo <owner>/<public-repo> --body-file <file containing the tracked domain> --dry-run`, or the test-suite case, passes without `AIDEVOPS_GH_PRIVACY_BYPASS`; an entity not in the target tree still blocks.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: t19020: feat(greeting): session-greeting advisories ask only for real human action (c...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19020` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-15 | **Started:** 2026-11-15
**Tags:** `interactive` `feat`

## Outcome

feat(greeting): session-greeting advisories ask only for real human action (canonical noise, duplicate families, stale daemon advisory, App-read remedy)

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `advisory toast session greeting ordering remedy noise`, `canonical recovery advisory DS_Store uncommitted noise` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: no open PRs or issues touch the target files; recent commits are e0c21939f7 (t19004) and 9001538f44 (GH#38273), which this builds on
- [x] File refs verified at HEAD `3176ba3296`
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. Local display and diagnosis only; no dispatch, merge or trust-boundary change

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-15
- **Session:** opencode interactive productivity mission (Parent #38332 / t19002 evidence track)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** The maintainer asked that users rarely, if ever, need to read into issues or local state. Session mining for that mission found the session-start greeting asking for human attention on noise, while the one high-leverage human action is buried.

## What

The session-start greeting (`aidevops-update-check.sh::_check_advisories` → OpenCode toast) should list only advisories that need a human, each with the correct next step. Specifically:

1. Canonical-checkout diagnosis should ignore untracked OS/runtime metadata (`.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`, `desktop.ini`, and OpenCode's `.opencode/` dependency artefacts), so those files alone never raise "requires manual review".
2. The canonical-recovery advisory's `Effect:` text should state the real effect. Since t2871, pulse does not pause PR processing for a dirty canonical checkout.
3. Per-repo advisories already counted by the setup-debt `[WARN]` aggregate (`sync-pat-*`, `cross-account-inherit-*`, `repo-onboarding-*`) should not be listed again one by one.
4. Per-reason `underfill-*` and per-repo `canonical-recovery-*` advisories should collapse to one line per family.
5. The generic "Run in your terminal: `aidevops security`" suffix should appear only on security advisories. Every line keeps its dismiss hint.
6. The GitHub App read-routing advisory should be classified `[WARN]` and carry its own setup command in the displayed line.
7. (Scope added during implementation.) The displayed summary should skip writer metadata (epoch stamps, `[advisory:<id>]` headers, `#` lines) and unwrap `title:`. A healthy auto-update daemon should clear a stale `daemon-disabled` advisory on any update, not only interactive TTY runs. Evidence: the advisory had been shown since 2026-11-06 while `aidevops auto-update health-check` reported `HEALTHY (last run 242s ago)`; `macos-user-lookup` displayed only `1794625049`.

## Why

Measured on 2026-11-15 (local machine, point-in-time):

- `~/.aidevops/cache/session-greeting-opencode.txt` was 59 lines, from 51 advisory files. 23 `Repository: …` lines and 2 SYNC_PAT/cross-account lines repeated the three setup-debt `[WARN]` aggregates. 6 `UNDERFILL_ATTRIBUTION` lines were pulse diagnostics with AI-runnable remedies.
- 7 `[CANONICAL DIAGNOSTIC] <repo> requires manual review` lines. For 5 repos the only dirty path was an untracked `.DS_Store`; for 1 it was an untracked `.opencode/package-lock.json` written by OpenCode's plugin install (its generated `.opencode/.gitignore` covers `package.json` and `bun.lock` but not npm's lockfile). `canonical-recovery-routine.sh` retries every tick and retains them forever (`tick complete: scanned=7 cleared=0 retained=7`).
- The advisory body claims "PR processing, CI failure routing, and completion sweep are paused for this repo". That text dates from t2871 (2ada606812). Today the only caller, `pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:193-195`, ignores the return code, and canonical maintenance is diagnostic-only (`pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh:300-323`).
- The App read-routing advisory (`github-app-read-routing`) reports that 78% of known REST cost could move off the PAT. Pulse logs show 56 progress-stage deferrals (`dispatch_max`, `preflight_early_dispatch`, `preflight_post_label_refill`, `approval_merge_trigger`) in the `emergency` REST band at `0/5000`. Yet this advisory is an unprefixed info line buried mid-toast, and its suffix sends the user to `aidevops security`, which does not set up an App.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Display-layer aggregation plus a narrow porcelain filter, both following existing patterns (`worktree-helper-add.sh:80-102` already filters `?? .DS_Store`). No dispatch or trust-boundary change.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-recovery.sh:165-182`: in `_pcr_detect_state`, drop untracked (`??`) records from `git status --porcelain -z --untracked-files=all` (raw paths, untracked directories expanded) whose path is OS metadata (basename `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`, `desktop.ini`) or an OpenCode dependency artefact under `.opencode/` (`package-lock.json`, `bun.lock`, `package.json`, `node_modules/*`) before classifying `uncommitted`. Tracked edits and every other untracked path remain `uncommitted`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-recovery.sh:337-338`: correct the `Effect:` text. Keep lines 1-4 unchanged: `canonical-recovery-routine.sh::_crr_extract_repo_path` parses line 4.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh:373-443`: in `_check_advisories`, skip setup-debt-covered prefixes when the aggregate line was emitted, collapse the `underfill-*` and `canonical-recovery-*` families, and limit the `aidevops security` suffix to `[SECURITY ADVISORY]`/`[ADVISORY]` lines.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/github_auth_usage.py:98-110`: prefix line 1 with `[WARN]` and include the `app create` command plus the unbound owners in it.
- `EDIT: aidevops.sh:559-561` and `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh:712-746`: non-interactive updates call `_update_check_daemon_health --clear-only`, which removes a stale advisory when healthy and never writes. Line 1 of a written advisory carries the fix command.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_check_advisories` output feeds the greeting cache and `greeting-toast.mjs::classifyLines` (prefix-based buckets). `canonical-recovery-routine.sh` parses advisory line 4 only.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none new. Advisory files are rewritten by their existing writers. Once a repo's state is `clean`, `canonical-recovery-routine.sh` removes the stale advisory on its next tick.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-debt-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-update-check-gh-slurp-prerequisite.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-underfill-attribution.sh`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed by `setup.sh`; nothing generated.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** a revert restores per-file listing; advisory files are disposable.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- A human's untracked `.DS_Store` is never meaningful work, and the canonical checkout is still never mutated (diagnosis only).
- Mixed versions: older hosts keep listing every advisory line. No file-format change except the App advisory's line 1.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-debt-helper.sh
```
