title: fix(gh-permission): ETag 304 on the REST route is misread as api-failure, so permission lookups fail closed permanently
body:
## What

Since t19029 (`4c520c00cc`, 2026-11-15), `_gh_collaborator_permission_lookup_uncached` (`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh:588-685`) sends `If-None-Match` with the stored ETag. It treats the reply as a 304 only when stdout is empty:

```bash
[[ "$rc" -ne 0 && -z "$api_response" && -n "$stored_etag" ]] &&
	grep -qE '^gh: HTTP 304([[:space:]]|$)' "$err_file" && not_modified=1
```

On the default REST route (`_rest_api_call read gh api -i …`), `gh api -i` writes the 304 status line and headers to stdout, so `api_response` is never empty. `not_modified` stays 0, `rc` is 1, and the lookup returns `rc=2 reason=api-failure`. The ETag entry is kept, so **every later lookup for the same repo and user also gets a 304 and fails**. After the first successful read, a permission verdict never succeeds again.

## Reproducer

1. Look up a permission once for a repo you do not own: `_gh_collaborator_permission_lookup <org>/<repo> <you> perm`. It returns `rc=0`, `perm=admin` and stores an ETag.
2. Run the same lookup again in a fresh shell so the in-process memo is empty. It now returns `rc=2`, `AIDEVOPS_GH_COLLAB_PERMISSION_HTTP=304` and `AIDEVOPS_GH_COLLAB_PERMISSION_REASON=api-failure`.
3. Every later lookup repeats step 2 until the ETag file under `~/.aidevops/cache/gh-collaborator-permission-etags/` is removed.

## Evidence (2026-11-16 ~00:35Z, deployed 3.39.20x runtime)

- Probe sourcing `shared-constants.sh` and calling `_gh_collaborator_permission_lookup`:
  - `<private-org>/<repo> marcusquinn` → `rc=2 permission= http=304 reason=api-failure`; the live API returns `admin`.
  - `marcusquinn/aidevops marcusquinn` → the same `rc=2 http=304 reason=api-failure`.
- `_gh_collaborator_permission_request rest <url> <etag>` → `rc=1`, stdout 1,197 bytes starting `HTTP/2.0 304 Not Modified`, stderr `gh: HTTP 304`.
- A plain shim `gh api -i -H 'If-None-Match: …'` returns empty stdout, which is the case the code assumed. The REST route does not.
- `~/.aidevops/cache/gh-collaborator-permission-etags/` holds 96 entries. Almost all were written between 12:12 and 14:16 on 2026-11-15 and have not been rewritten since, which fits "first read succeeds, every read after it fails".
- User-visible effect: `interactive-start-helper.sh --issue <N> --repo <private-org>/<repo>` warned that `@marcusquinn is not a maintainer-equivalent collaborator` and skipped the claim, although the user is an org admin. Every fail-closed consumer is affected for any repo whose owner is not the user: interactive claims and lockdown, `_gh_current_user_allows_repo_write` (pulse repo meta, issue sync, stats sweeps), merge author checks and dispatch-claim trust.

## Fix

After parsing the response, treat it as not-modified when a stored ETag was sent, the transport failed, the body is empty, and either the parsed status is `304` or stderr reports `gh: HTTP 304`. The stored verdict still comes only from an earlier 200 for the same repo, user and route, and a 304 without a stored verdict still fails closed (`#aidevops:trust-boundary` unchanged).

## Files

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh:612-654` — the not-modified detection.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-collaborator-permission-etag.sh` — regression test with a stub `gh` for both 304 output shapes, plus a 304 with no stored verdict.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-collaborator-permission-etag.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`
- Re-run the probe after deploy: `rc=0 permission=admin http=304 reason=ok`.

title: perf(gh-transport): conditional ETag GETs so repeated REST reads cost zero quota
body:
## What

Make governed native REST GETs conditional. The transport governor (`.agents/scripts/gh-transport-governor.py`) should keep each eligible response's ETag and stdout, keyed by credential digest plus the exact `gh api` arguments. It then sends `If-None-Match` on repeats. When GitHub answers `304 Not Modified`, it replays the stored stdout with exit 0. An authorized 304 does not count against the primary rate limit.

## Why

The owner's REST-core quota now runs out before each hourly reset. When that happens, Pulse dispatch, workers and interactive sessions all stop until the reset.

Evidence from the maintainer host, reset window ending `1794791541` (2026-11-16):

- `gh api rate_limit` (native binary): `used=4622` about 50 minutes into the window, then `403 API rate limit exceeded` (`used=5000`) about 10 minutes before reset.
- `gh-api-calls.log` gh-pat rest-core `attempt` rows in that window: 4,347, about 94% of observed usage. The drain is aidevops' own governed traffic, not a foreign consumer.
- Top REST families over 60 minutes (`pulse-diagnose-helper.sh api-budget`): `repos/:o/:r/issues/:id` 1,137, `issues/:id/comments` 794, `pulls/:id` 427, `user` 200, `commits/:id` 139. Most are repeated reads of the same objects by `pulse-wrapper.sh`, `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`, `dispatch-claim-helper.sh`, `headless-runtime-helper.sh` and `full-loop-helper.sh`.
- `gh_native_response._response_metadata` already records an authenticated 304 as cost 0, but no caller sends validators. The only exception is the collaborator-permission ETag cache (t19029, GH#38562).

## How

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/gh_conditional_cache.py`. It decides eligibility, derives the key from the credential digest and normalized argv, does private atomic storage with a size cap and age pruning, and extracts the ETag from the included-headers frame.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-governor.py` `run()`. It adds `If-None-Match` when an entry exists and captures native stderr. On 304 with an entry, it replays the stored stdout and returns 0. On 200, it stores the ETag and stdout. On any other status, it replays stderr unchanged.
- Eligible requests: core-resource GET with no caller `--include`, `--silent`, `--template` or conditional headers. A `--jq` filter must not reference `now`, `env` or `$ENV`. The stored output is the post-`--jq` stdout, so gh's own gojq semantics are preserved without re-implementing jq.
- Trust boundary: a replay happens only after GitHub confirms the representation for the same credential and request is unchanged, so it is equivalent to a live read. Entries are 0600 in a 0700 directory under `~/.aidevops/state/gh-transport/`, keyed by the credential digest, so identities never share entries.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh_conditional_cache.py`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-governor.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py`

## Acceptance

1. A repeated eligible GET whose ETag still matches returns exactly the earlier stdout and exit 0. The attempt row records status 304 and cost 0.
2. A changed resource (200) replaces the stored entry. 4xx/5xx and transport failures keep native behaviour, and a 404 drops the entry.
3. Ineligible shapes (`--include`, `--silent`, `--template`, time- or environment-dependent `--jq`, caller validators, non-GET, `rate_limit`) send no validator and store nothing.
4. Live check after deploy: `rest-window-attribution.py`-style counts show 304 attempts for the hot families, and core usage per hour drops.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py`
- Existing transport tests: `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim-transport-cases.sh`
- Live: repeat `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .state` through the shim and confirm a status-304 attempt row in `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log`.

title: t19052: fix(worker): avoid permission holds from absolute system paths in bash commands
body:
**Task ID:** `t19052` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-16
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug`

## Outcome

fix(worker): avoid permission holds from absolute system paths in bash commands

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop headless workers from pausing for maintainer permission because they wrote absolute system paths (`/usr/bin`, `/bin`, `/tmp`, ...) into a bash tool command line. The usual cause is an inline restricted `PATH` used to put test stubs first.

## Why

Evidence: #38523 paused on `perm-2a1e7540c77f77ad`. One `bash` request named `/usr/bin/*` plus `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/gh38523-test/bin/*`. OpenCode applies the external-directory boundary to every absolute path in a shell command. The tmp half is already owned recovery (GH#35128/GH#35676), but `/usr/bin/*` is not, so the whole capture became a `needs-maintainer-permissions` hold. Workers never need to name OS binary directories: those binaries already run through `PATH`.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh`, setup-shortcuts bullets near "Never seek a broad external_directory grant": add one short bullet. Never write absolute paths outside the worktree into bash tool commands. Put stubs under `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR`, set `PATH` and fixtures inside a worktree script, and run that script with a worktree-relative command.
2. `.agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh` `permission_capture_is_temp_write_recovery()`: also classify `bash`/`read` patterns on OS-owned binary directories (`/bin`, `/sbin`, `/usr/bin`, `/usr/sbin`, optionally with `/*`) as owned recovery. This grants nothing and only avoids the human hold. Extend the recovery text to say "set PATH inside a worktree script".
3. `.agents/reference/dispatch-blockers.md` "Scratch `external_directory` requests": document the system-bin case and the avoidance pattern.
4. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-permission-helper.sh`: add the #38523 shape (tmp bin + `/usr/bin/*` via bash) as recovery. Keep `/usr/local/bin/*` and write/edit on `/usr/bin/*` as non-recovery.

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-permission-helper.sh` passes, including the new cases.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh` passes.
- ShellCheck is clean on the changed scripts.

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh
- .agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh
- .agents/reference/dispatch-blockers.md
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-permission-helper.sh

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #38523 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #38523

**Parent issue:** #38523 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** GH#38506 phase 4: install record function and cross-platform installs report
**Parent labels:** `enhancement,status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:interactive,consolidation-in-progress`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #38523 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#38523 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 38523 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #38523, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 38523 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 38523 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 38523 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 38523 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38523" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #38523 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #38523.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

Parent: #38506

For #38506 (phase 4 of 6).

## What

Nothing records what aidevops, its helpers or its AI sessions install on a computer: name, method, path, who installed it, why, and how it gets updates. Users cannot see it, the updater cannot tell copies apart, and retirement cannot find installs. Linux has no installed-program view at all (`local-permissions-check-helper.sh` about line 588 is macOS-only). This phase adds the record and a read-only report. Phases 5 and 6 depend on its interface.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg -n 'inventory is macOS-specific' .agents/scripts/local-permissions-check-helper.sh`

**Actual output** (at `2a093cf4f7`):

```text
588:		printf 'Host/runtime app inventory is macOS-specific.\n'
```

**Expected:** a cross-platform report of what aidevops installed, why, and how each item is updated.

- No shared install-record function exists: `rg -n 'install_record' .agents/scripts` has no match.
- On the reporting Linux host, programs placed in `~/.local/bin`, `~/.bun/bin`, npm global, `uv tool list`, `~/.aidevops/runtimes` and `~/.aidevops/tools` had no record of origin or update path (see the parent issue, sections 4 and 8).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/install-record-helper.sh`
- `aidevops.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-help-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/local-permissions-check-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/localdev-helper-init.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/yt-dlp-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/comfy-cli-helper.sh`

Scope discovery (worker, GH#38523): `install-record-helper.sh` is new (record library + CLI + report). `aidevops.sh` routes `aidevops installs`; `aidevops-help-lib.sh` lists it in help. `local-permissions-check-helper.sh` points Linux users at the new report from its macOS-only inventory message. The first wired helpers are `localdev-helper-init.sh` (`ensure_mkcert`, including the `~/.local/bin` download fallback), `yt-dlp-helper.sh` (`install_ytdlp_isolated`) and `comfy-cli-helper.sh` (`cmd_install`). The report is a dedicated subcommand, so `aidevops status` is not edited.

## How

- Shared record function, sourced by helpers after a successful install: `install_record <name> <method> <path> <reason> <update-path>`, appending JSONL to `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/installs.jsonl` (installer = calling script or `session`, ISO date). Never record secrets or full command lines with tokens.
- A CLI for sessions: `install-record-helper.sh add --name … --method … --path … --reason … --update …`.
- Report: `aidevops installs` (or `aidevops status --installs`), in plain language, on Linux and macOS. It lists recorded installs, then known-untracked items in `~/.local/bin`, `~/.bun/bin`, the npm global prefix, `uv tool list`, and `~/.aidevops/{runtimes,tools}`. It flags broken shebangs (interpreter missing after a Python upgrade) and apt packages installed above the distro version from disabled sources (`apt-cache policy`). Report only: no auto-update, no deletion.
- Wire two or three existing helpers to call `install_record` as the reference pattern; the rest follow in later phases.
- Keep `aidevops update` unchanged (#29712).

## Verification

- `install-record-helper.sh add …` then `aidevops installs` shows the entry; `shellcheck` clean.
- On a Linux host and a macOS host, the report lists untracked binaries in `~/.local/bin` and flags a deliberately broken shebang in a temp dir pointed at by an override variable.
- Running a wired helper's install records exactly one entry; a re-run does not duplicate it.

Shared record function, sourced by helpers after a successful install: `install_record <name> <method> <path> <reason> <update-path>`, appending JSONL to `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/installs.jsonl` (installer = calling script or `session`, ISO date). Never record secrets or full command lines with tokens. Re-recording the same install must not duplicate the entry.
- CLI for sessions: `install-record-helper.sh add --name … --method … --path … --reason … --update …`.
- Report: `aidevops installs` (or `aidevops status --installs`), in plain language, on Linux and macOS. It lists recorded installs, then known-untracked items in `~/.local/bin`, `~/.bun/bin`, the npm global prefix, `uv tool list`, and `~/.aidevops/{runtimes,tools}`. It flags broken shebangs (interpreter missing after a Python upgrade) and apt packages installed above the distro version from disabled sources (`apt-cache policy`). Report only: no auto-update, no deletion. An override variable must let the scan directory point at a temp dir for verification.
- `aidevops.sh` routes `aidevops installs`; `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-help-lib.sh` lists it in help. The report is a dedicated subcommand, so `aidevops status` is not edited.
- `local-permissions-check-helper.sh` (macOS-only message near line 588) points Linux users at the new report.
- Wire the first helpers to call `install_record` as the reference pattern (the rest follow in later phases): `localdev-helper-init.sh` (`ensure_mkcert`, including the `~/.local/bin` download fallback), `yt-dlp-helper.sh` (`install_ytdlp_isolated`) and `comfy-cli-helper.sh` (`cmd_install`).
- Keep `aidevops update` unchanged (#29712).

**Worker guidance: avoid the external-directory permission pause** (per @marcusquinn). A previous worker paused on `perm-2a1e7540c77f77ad`: one `bash` call named both `/usr/bin/*` and `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/gh38523-test/bin/*`, which looks like an inline restricted `PATH`. OpenCode treats every absolute path written in a bash command line as outside the worktree, so naming `/usr/bin` needed maintainer approval. To verify `install-record-helper.sh` without a permission request:

- Put stub binaries under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`, created with `mktemp -d` **inside a script**.
- Set the restricted `PATH` **inside that script**, not in the bash tool command. Build it from variables, e.g. `PATH="${stub_bin}:$(getconf PATH)"` or `PATH="${stub_bin}:${PATH}"`.
- Run the check as a single worktree-relative command, e.g. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/<test-file>.sh`. Follow the pattern in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-permission-helper.sh`, which builds its fixtures under a temp root inside the script.
- Never write a literal `/usr/bin`, `/bin`, `/tmp` or `$HOME/...` path into the bash tool command line.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `install-record-helper.sh add …` then `aidevops installs` shows the entry; `shellcheck` is clean on all edited scripts.
- [ ] On Linux and macOS, the report lists untracked binaries in `~/.local/bin` and flags a deliberately broken shebang in a temp dir pointed at by an override variable.
- [ ] Running a wired helper's install records exactly one entry; a re-run does not duplicate it.
- [ ] No secrets or token-bearing command lines are recorded.
- [ ] `aidevops installs` is routed in `aidevops.sh` and listed in help; `aidevops update` is unchanged.
- [ ] The Linux path in `local-permissions-check-helper.sh` points to `aidevops installs`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: aidevops.sh

## What

`aidevops_bounded_operation` (and the GPT image tool, which shares the resolver) rejects a session-owned linked worktree of a repo registered in `repos.json` when the OpenCode session started inside a *different* Git repository. A session rooted in the framework repo that full-loops a PR in another registered repo gets:

```json
{"schema":"aidevops.interactive-operation/v1","error":"Operation workdir belongs to an unrelated Git repository."}
```

Interactive sessions routinely start in the framework repo and orchestrate work in other registered repos. title: pulse: GH#38162 drain starvation-escape supervisor blocks the activated bundle's dispatch, leaving all worker slots idle
body:
## What

When a cooperative bundle drain is pending, the GH#38162 starvation escape launches the LLM supervisor *before* the activated bundle's first cycle. The wrapper then waits for the supervisor (`waiting_for_worker` on `session=supervisor-pulse`). The supervisor cannot launch workers (GH#36343: `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` rejects `WORKER_SESSION_KEY=supervisor-pulse`). So every worker slot stays empty for the whole supervisor session, which can run up to 55 minutes.

## Observed evidence (2026-11-16, one runner)

- `pulse.log`: `Dispatch_max stopping early: cooperative drain requested for activated bundle 3.39.209-... (GH#37907)`, then `LLM supervisor: cooperative drain requested, but no supervisor attempt within 7200s — evaluating supervisor before bundle ... starts (GH#38162 starvation escape)`, then `[lifecycle] waiting_for_worker pid=<supervisor>` at 02:25:51Z.
- `pulse-wrapper.sh --command capacity` returned `14|0|14` at about 02:30Z, 02:37Z and 02:42Z. Dispatchable `status:available` candidates existed throughout (for example about 20 award-enrichment issues in one managed repo).
- The supervisor's own work (terminal-blocker recovery decisions) needs no idle slots. It only needs the wrapper not to block on it.

## Why it matters

Throughput: an escape added to stop supervisor starvation now starves dispatch. The longer the supervisor runs its recovery queue, the longer all slots stay empty.

## Suggested fix (worker decides)

Pick one of these in `pulse-wrapper.sh` / the LLM-supervisor launch path:
1. Launch the starvation-escape supervisor detached from the cycle (as the normal path does, if it already does), so the activated bundle's cycle and dispatch wave start immediately.
2. Or run the activated bundle's first dispatch wave before the escape supervisor, as the GH#38210 deferral already does in the `deferring the GH#38162 escape until after ... first dispatch wave` branch. That branch did not fire on this pass, because the log took the `evaluating supervisor before bundle ... starts` branch.

Files to inspect: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` (grep `GH#38162`, `GH#38210`, `starvation escape`), and the supervisor launch and wait path that logs `waiting_for_worker`.

## Verification

During a pending cooperative drain with the starvation escape due, `capacity` should show workers launching while the supervisor session is still running. `pulse.log` should show `Dispatch_max` launches with timestamps inside the supervisor session.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`

title: t19055: fix(setup): refuse ephemeral OpenCode targets in the Pulse direct shim writer
body:
**Task ID:** `t19055` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-16 | **Started:** 2026-11-16
**Tags:** `interactive` `bug`

## Outcome

fix(setup): refuse ephemeral OpenCode targets in the Pulse direct shim writer

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


**Task ID:** `t19055` | **Issue:** GH#38581

## Origin

Interactive session (productivity mission), from tracing the largest recent worker local-error family. On 2026-11-15 between 11:28 and 11:54 UTC, 19 headless worker launches on one host failed with exit 127 before any model work. Each failure excerpt shows the live daemon shim failing at line 9:

```text
~/.local/bin/opencode: line 9: $TMPDIR/tmp.XXXXXXXXXX/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.1/bin/opencode: No such file or directory
```

GH#38475 / t19031 traced the trigger: Test 14 in `test-resolve-pulse-runtime-binary.sh` called `_pulse_write_direct_opencode_shim` with the caller's real HOME. That replaced the live shim with one pointing at a fixture that was deleted moments later. t19031 made the test hermetic, and t19034 / GH#38481 now pauses a runner after three evidenced runtime-missing launches. Both treated production code as correct.

## What

`_pulse_write_direct_opencode_shim` in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-pulse.sh` is the only one of the three OpenCode shim writers with no ephemeral-target guard. The other two are `_setup_ensure_opencode_stable_shim` in `.agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh` and the one in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`. Both refuse a target under `$TMPDIR`, `/tmp`, `/var/tmp` or `/var/folders/*/*/T/` unless HOME itself is ephemeral. `_resolve_pulse_runtime_binary` makes the gap worse. When the stable-shim writer correctly refuses an ephemeral target, `_pulse_normalize_opencode_binary` returns the raw path. The direct writer then writes it into the live `~/.local/bin/opencode` anyway, and `_persist_pulse_runtime_path` can record the temp path in `~/.config/aidevops/scheduler-runtime-bin`.

Change:

1. `_pulse_write_direct_opencode_shim` returns 1 without writing when the target, or its physical path, is ephemeral and HOME is not. Use `_setup_opencode_binary_is_ephemeral` when it is declared, matching the other writers' `"${HOME}/.aidevops-home"` HOME test.
2. `_pulse_validate_opencode_candidate` rejects the same candidates, so discovery continues to durable installs and a temp path is never shimmed or persisted.

Fixture tests whose HOME is itself ephemeral keep their current behaviour.

## Why

A single misdirected shim write stopped all worker dispatch on the host for 26 minutes. The test fix closed one caller, not the class: any future direct caller, including a setup run with `OPENCODE_BIN` under a temp dir, can repeat the outage. A writer-level guard makes the live shim safe regardless of caller hygiene.

## How (files)

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-pulse.sh`: `_pulse_validate_opencode_candidate` (about line 265) and `_pulse_write_direct_opencode_shim` (about line 349). Reference pattern: `_setup_ensure_opencode_stable_shim` in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh:1166-1182`.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/tests/test-resolve-pulse-runtime-binary.sh`: add one case that runs the direct writer with a non-ephemeral HOME and an ephemeral target, and asserts that nothing is written and the result is non-zero.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-pulse.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-resolve-pulse-runtime-binary.sh`
- `TODO.md`

## Acceptance

- With a durable HOME and an ephemeral target, `_pulse_write_direct_opencode_shim` returns non-zero and leaves no shim.
- The existing `test-resolve-pulse-runtime-binary.sh`, `test-tool-install-opencode.sh` and `test-setup-opencode-cli.sh` cases still pass.
- ShellCheck is clean on changed shell files.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-resolve-pulse-runtime-binary.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-pulse.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-resolve-pulse-runtime-binary.sh
```

title: opencode-browse-helper: PATH fallback picks xdg-utils browse (xdg-open) when browse CLI is not installed
body:
## Observed

On Ubuntu with the browse CLI not installed in `~/.local/bin`, every
`aidevops opencode-browse` command runs the system `browse` command from
xdg-utils (an alias for `xdg-open`) instead of the OpenCode browse CLI:

- `aidevops opencode-browse pair --list` → `xdg-open: unexpected option '--list'`
- `aidevops opencode-browse status` → `gio: file:///<cwd>/status: Error when getting information for file ...`

`type -a browse` shows `/usr/bin/browse` and `/bin/browse` only. The helper
never reports "browse CLI not installed", so the documented hPanel automation in
`services/hosting/hostinger-client-access.md` ("Drive hPanel without taking over
the screen") fails with a misleading error, and a stray argument can be handed
to `xdg-open` (which may try to open a file or URL in the desktop session).

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/opencode-browse-helper.sh` `browse_bin()` (around lines 71-83)
checks `${XDG_BIN_HOME:-~/.local/bin}/browse` first, then falls back to any
`command -v browse` on PATH without checking that it is the browse CLI.

## Fix

- In `browse_bin()`, only accept a PATH `browse` that is the OpenCode browse
  CLI. For example: reject it when `readlink -f` resolves to `xdg-open`, or
  require a known `--version`/`help` signature. Return 1 otherwise so callers
  print the existing "not installed" guidance and `install` hint.
- `cmd_installed` (exit 0 when installed) should use the same check.

## Verification

- On a host where `/usr/bin/browse` is xdg-utils' alias and the CLI is not
  installed: `aidevops opencode-browse status` reports the CLI as not installed
  (no `xdg-open`/`gio` output), and `aidevops opencode-browse installed` exits 1.
- With the CLI installed in `~/.local/bin`, behaviour is unchanged.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-browse-helper.sh` clean.

title: planning-commit-helper complete: reports 'no planning PR was created' after opening the PR, and leaks its temp planning worktree
body:
## What

`planning-commit-helper.sh complete <task> --pr <N>`, run from an
interactive session's linked worktree, pushed the planning branch and opened
the planning PR. It then exited 1 and printed:

```text
[todo_commit_push] Planning publication stopped after pushed; caller planning edits are cleaned and the disposable worktree is retained.
AIDEVOPS_PLANNING_RECOVERY_REMOTE_STATE=pushed
AIDEVOPS_PLANNING_RECOVERY_PR_STATE=open
AIDEVOPS_PLANNING_RECOVERY_WORKTREE_STATE=retained
[plan] Task completion publication failed; no successful direct push or planning PR was created
```

The PR was created and open, so the final line is wrong. The disposable
`*-planning-<id>-*` worktree was also left behind. One private managed repo
now has **29** retained detached `-planning-` worktrees, which suggests this
happens every time it runs from an interactive session.

## Root cause (from reading the deployed scripts)

1. `shared-todo-commit.sh` `_todo_finalize_planning_pr` calls
   `_todo_remove_temp_worktree`. If that fails, it sets
   `cleanup_state=retained` and **`terminal_rc=1`**, even when the push and
   the PR succeeded.
2. `_todo_remove_temp_worktree` calls `worktree_managed_require_removal_proof`
   (`audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`). For the temp worktree,
   `worktree-managed-lifetime.py status` reports `"state": "running"`,
   `"manager": "owner-cgroup"`, `process_reconciliation.active: 1`, and the
   owner is the calling interactive session, which is still alive. The
   managed-lifetime proof fails, so the helper can never remove a worktree
   that its own live session owns.
3. `planning-commit-helper.sh` `complete_task` then prints "no successful
   direct push or planning PR was created", whatever
   `AIDEVOPS_PLANNING_RECOVERY_PR_STATE` says.

## Proposed fix

- Register the temp planning worktree under the helper's own short-lived
  owner (or seal it before removal), so the removal proof passes once the
  helper finishes with it. Alternatively, let `_todo_remove_temp_worktree`
  remove worktrees the current helper created in this run (matching
  publication id and generation).
- Treat a cleanup failure after a successful push and PR as a warning, not
  `terminal_rc=1`. Set `TODO_COMMIT_PUSH_RESULT=pr` and return the PR URL.
- In `planning-commit-helper.sh`, word the failure message from the actual
  recovery state, for example "PR #N created; temp worktree cleanup failed".

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh` (`_todo_finalize_planning_pr`,
  `_todo_remove_temp_worktree`, `_todo_create_planning_pr`)
- `.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh` (`complete_task` message)
- Possibly `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`
  (`worktree_managed_require_removal_proof`)

## Verification

- From an interactive linked worktree, run
  `planning-commit-helper.sh complete tNNN --pr <merged PR>` on a test repo.
  It should exit 0, print the planning PR URL, and leave no
  `*-planning-*` worktree behind (`git worktree list`).
- ShellCheck clean on the edited scripts.

title: Follow-up to #38506: OpenCode sessions hide uv tools; installs report false alarms; ShellCheck never updated
body:
## Description

This follows up #38506, which is closed and locked; its lock notice asks for new issues that reference it. The #38506 fixes are now deployed on the same Ubuntu 26.04 host. I ran the new `aidevops installs` report and the updater's read-only check, and found four remaining problems. Each was checked against current code (`main` at `6745ed41de`).

1. **Inside OpenCode sessions started by the aidevops launcher, uv tools are invisible, and new uv tools would go to a session-only folder.**
   - **Cause:** the launcher exports a per-project `XDG_DATA_HOME` (`opencode-launcher-helper.sh:489`), and every command a session runs inherits it. uv keeps tools in `$XDG_DATA_HOME/uv/tools` and their commands in `$XDG_DATA_HOME/../bin`.
   - **What it breaks inside a session:**
     - `uv tool list` says "No tools installed".
     - The installs report leaves out all three uv tools on this host.
     - The updater's check reports Outscraper MCP as "not installed". Run without the session variable, it reports 0.1.2, up to date.
   - **Why it matters now:** #38524 and #38529 just made `uv tool install` the standard route for Python command-line tools, in helpers and in sessions. On uv's own reported paths, a session following that route would install into a folder that is not on the user's `PATH`. The user's own `uv tool upgrade` would not see it there.
   - **Precedent:** the same inherited variable caused #28075 for mkcert, and that was fixed for mkcert only (`localdev-helper-init.sh:110-119`).

2. **The report's APT section flags removed packages.**
   - `apt_report()` checks every package dpkg knows (`install-record-helper.sh:138`). That includes packages that were removed and left only configuration files behind (dpkg state `rc`).
   - For those packages, `apt-cache policy` prints `Installed: (none)`. The report takes `(none)` as the installed version (`:163`), and `dpkg --compare-versions '(none)' gt <version>` succeeds.
   - On this host, all 15 flagged lines are old kernels that apt has already removed. The report says each is "newer than enabled sources; installed version has no active source". Both statements are false, and a non-developer cannot tell this is harmless.

3. **Tools that aidevops installs and updates are labelled "origin and update path unknown".**
   - Only three helpers record installs: `localdev-helper-init.sh:133`, `comfy-cli-helper.sh:117` and `yt-dlp-helper.sh:773`.
   - Setup and the updater record nothing, and `report()` does not consult the updater's tool list (`install-record-helper.sh:190-219`, heading at `:202`).
   - So these appear under "update path unknown", even though `tool-version-check.sh` checks and updates them: OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Chrome DevTools MCP, GSC MCP, Playwriter, Claude Code MCP, Google Workspace CLI, Outscraper MCP and Cursor CLI. `aidevops` itself appears there too.
   - The same list includes things that are not installed programs:
     - directories in `~/.local/bin`;
     - an empty npm scope folder left behind by `npm uninstall -g`;
     - each npm tool twice (command and package folder), and each uv tool up to three times.
   - As a result, the list does not yet answer #38506's main question: which programs on this computer are looked after, and which are not.

4. **The updater never reads ShellCheck's version, so it never updates ShellCheck.**
   - `get_installed_version()` reads only the first line of `--version` output (`tool-version-check.sh:444`). ShellCheck prints its name on line 1 and `version: 0.11.0` on line 2.
   - So the ShellCheck row (`:236`) is always `unknown`.
   - `unknown` never reaches the update list (`:737-738`, `:980`).
   - No impact on this host, where Ubuntu updates ShellCheck. On hosts that rely on `aidevops update` for it, it is never updated.

## Expected Behavior

- uv tool installs and checks run from an AI session use the same uv tool folders as the user's terminal and the background updater.
- The APT section lists only installed packages, and only when the installed version really has no enabled source.
- Tools that aidevops installs or updates are not labelled "origin and update path unknown". The untracked list holds installed programs only, each listed once.
- The ShellCheck row shows the installed version, so the updater can report and update it like the other rows.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** each command below was run in a Bash tool call of an OpenCode session started by the aidevops launcher, unless marked `env -u XDG_DATA_HOME`.

```text
printenv XDG_DATA_HOME
uv tool list
uv tool dir --bin
env -u XDG_DATA_HOME uv tool list
env -u XDG_DATA_HOME uv tool dir --bin
aidevops installs report
env -u XDG_DATA_HOME aidevops installs report
dpkg-query -W -f='${binary:Package}\t${Version}\t${db:Status-Abbrev}\n' linux-image-7.0.0-38-generic linux-image-7.0.0-43-generic
```

**Expected output:** see Expected Behavior. In a session, `uv tool list` and the installs report show the same three uv tools as the user's terminal. The APT section shows none of the 15 removed kernel entries. Updater-managed tools are not listed as unknown. The ShellCheck row shows `0.11.0`.

**Causal status**: confirmed for findings 2, 3 and 4, and for finding 1's wrong report and check results. For finding 1's install location, the evidence is uv's own `uv tool dir --bin` output. No `uv tool install` was run from a session, to avoid changing the user's machine.

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `aidevops installs report` (`aidevops.sh:1713` dispatches to `install-record-helper.sh`, functions `report()` and `apt_report()`); the updater check `tool-version-check.sh` (`check_tool()`); the session environment set by `opencode-launcher-helper.sh:489`.
- **Call chain**: one chain per finding, numbered to match.
  - (1) launcher `export XDG_DATA_HOME`, then OpenCode, then the session's Bash tool, then `uv tool list` / `uv tool dir --bin` (`install-record-helper.sh:198-199`). The same variable reaches the helper calls `yt-dlp-helper.sh:37,758`, `comfy-cli-helper.sh:32,94`, `linter-manager.sh:171` and `security-helper.sh:1061`.
  - (2) `apt_report()` runs `dpkg-query -W` with no status filter (`:138`), then `apt-cache policy`. It takes `Installed: (none)` as the version (`:163`), compares it with `dpkg --compare-versions` (`:148-151`) and prints the line (`:153-154`).
  - (3) `report()` scans fixed folders and the npm prefix (`:190-219`) and labels everything missing from the install ledger as unknown (`:202`). Setup and the updater never call `install_record`.
  - (4) `check_tool()` goes to the `*)` branch of `_tool_installed_version()` (`:664-665`), then `get_installed_version()`, which reads only the first line (`:444`). The result is `unknown`, `_classify_tool_status` keeps it `unknown` (`:737-738`), and it is not queued at `:980`.
- **Integrated verification**: each chain was run through its production command on this host, with the outputs shown above. That covers `aidevops installs report` in the session and with `env -u XDG_DATA_HOME`, `uv tool list` and `uv tool dir --bin` in both environments, and `tool-version-check.sh --json` in both environments.

**Causal code**:

```text
a0615ae835  install-record-helper.sh (report, apt_report) - #38576
62fba63a48  tool-version-check.sh:236 ShellCheck row (2026-03-27)
9550315a7b  tool-version-check.sh:444 first-line-only version read (2026-03-09)
opencode-launcher-helper.sh:489  per-project XDG_DATA_HOME exported to the whole session
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use an Ubuntu host with at least one `uv tool` installed and at least one old kernel removed by apt but not purged (dpkg state `rc`).
2. Start OpenCode through the aidevops launcher. In a session, run `aidevops installs report`, `uv tool list` and `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh --json`.
3. Run the same three commands with `env -u XDG_DATA_HOME`, and compare.
4. In either run, look at the APT section, the untracked list and the ShellCheck row.

## Workarounds Applied

- **Finding 1:** while checking mkcert on this host, sessions had to run `env -u XDG_DATA_HOME mkcert -CAROOT` to see the real certificate folder. In this investigation, `env -u XDG_DATA_HOME` was needed again to see the real uv tools.
- **Findings 2-4:** no workaround. The removed-kernel entries are harmless and were left alone.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.39.210 (runtime bundle built from `9513a6cb7efa`)
- **Latest version**: 3.39.210
- **Install method**: unknown (`~/.local/bin/aidevops`)
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode 1.19.5, started through the aidevops launcher
- **AI Model**: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
- **OS**: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.3.9(1)-release
- **Working repo**: a private repository
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.103.3 (2026-10-26)

## Additional Context

### Things to consider

- **Finding 1:** OpenCode's database isolation needs the per-project `XDG_DATA_HOME`, but the commands sessions run may not.
  - Only uv and mkcert are known to be affected. Other tools that read this variable were not checked.
  - Where a fix belongs is for the maintainers to decide: the launcher, the plugin's command environment, or each helper.
- **Finding 3:** what is the untracked list for? A full inventory, or only programs nobody looks after?
  - If setup and the updater recorded their installs, or the report checked the updater's tool list, many of the 62 lines here would move out of "unknown".
  - Installs made before the ledger existed will stay "unknown" unless something backfills them.
- **Finding 2:** packages that are removed but not purged are common after Ubuntu kernel updates. This probably appears on most Ubuntu hosts.
- **Finding 4:** other rows may also print their version somewhere other than the first line. Only ShellCheck was checked.

### Related

#38506 (parent, closed), #38524, #38526, #38529, #38574 / #38576, #28075.

title: hostinger-helper and credential registry: support account-tagged Hostinger API tokens (provider default + token selector)
body:
## Observed

`services/hosting/hostinger.md` and the credential naming convention
(`tools/credentials/credential-inventory.md` "Naming new credentials") tell
operators to store account-tagged secrets, for example
`HOSTINGER_<ACCOUNT>_API_TOKEN`. But `hostinger-helper.sh` (`api`, `ssl-status`,
`wordpress-detect`, `fleet inventory`, `cron`) only checks and injects the bare
`HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN`.

The registry's conventional-variable defaults (`DEFAULT_ENV` in
`.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_fields.py`) cover anthropic, cloudflare,
github, hetzner, openai and vercel, not hostinger. So
`aidevops secret default hostinger HOSTINGER_<ACCOUNT>_API_TOKEN` can be recorded
but never makes `HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN` resolve.

Workaround used on 2026-11-16 for a new Hostinger account whose token was stored
account-tagged: `aidevops secret alias HOSTINGER_<ACCOUNT>_API_TOKEN HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN`.
This works, but the alias is documented as a *retired name*, and it cannot
choose between two Hostinger logins (each token only sees its own login's orders).

## Fix

1. Add `"hostinger": "HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN"` to `DEFAULT_ENV` in
   `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_fields.py`, so
   `aidevops secret default hostinger NAME` injects the declared token under
   `HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN`. Update the table in
   `tools/credentials/credential-inventory.md` "Resolution at injection".
2. In `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh`, accept an explicit token secret
   name for multi-login setups, for example `--token-secret NAME` or an
   environment variable `HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN_SECRET=NAME`, used by `api_call`,
   `fleet_command` and `cron_command` where they currently hard-code
   `aidevops secret check/inject HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN`. Keep the current default.
3. Update `services/hosting/hostinger.md` "Configuration" with the naming and
   default/selection guidance.

## Verification

- Registry: with `HOSTINGER_X_API_TOKEN` recorded (`--provider hostinger`) and
  `aidevops secret default hostinger HOSTINGER_X_API_TOKEN`,
  `aidevops secret check HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN` exits 0 and
  `python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/credential_inventory.py injection-map`
  lists the pair.
- Helper: `hostinger-helper.sh api api/hosting/v1/orders` works with only the
  account-tagged secret plus the default; with two tokens, the explicit
  selector picks the requested login.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh`; existing credential
  inventory tests pass.

title: t19056: fix(opencode-db-archive): persist batch adaptation across runs so the shared ...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19056` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-16
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug` `priority:high`

## Outcome

fix(opencode-db-archive): persist batch adaptation across runs so the shared DB archive and worker-event expiry stop livelocking

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


**Task ID:** `t19056` | **Issue:** GH#38590

## Origin

Interactive session (productivity mission), from diagnosing host saturation and repeated archive deferrals on one macOS host. The shared OpenCode DB has not archived a session since 2026-10-23, and the GH#38491 worker-event expiry (released in v3.39.210) has never expired an event there.

Evidence (2026-11-16, read-only queries plus `~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-db-archive.log`, attributed per active DB):

- Shared `opencode.db` is 72.25 GB; `opencode-archive.db` is 31.9 GB.
- Since 2026-10-23T23:00Z: 176 runs reached the shared DB, 67 printed `Found N sessions eligible`, 0 printed `Archived N/M sessions`, 59 ended with `Terminated: 15 sqlite3 "$ACTIVE_DB" <<BATCH_SQL` (the per-DB deadline killed the first batch), and 62 printed `Archive interrupted; ... the active transaction will roll back`. Eligible backlog: 3389 on 2026-10-23 → 4833 on 2026-11-02 → 6467 on 2026-11-14 → 6631 on 2026-11-16T03:00Z.
- `event`: 2,904,220 rows, 64.9 GB of payload (`SUM(octet_length(data))`). Of those, 1,333,893 rows (35.7 GB) belong to sessions in `ledger.worker_sessions` that have been inactive 60+ minutes, which is exactly the GH#38491 expiry filter. Yet every `Worker event expiry pass complete` line on this host reports `expired 0 ... 0 B freed`, including the shared-DB run at 2026-11-16T03:00Z.
- The 500-row expiry selection took 7.33 s cold and 0.01 s warm (host load 180-245 on 16 CPUs). The pass gets `max_duration/4` = 15 s, and `_archive_expire_worker_events` breaks on rc 124 without distinguishing "timed out" from "nothing to expire".
- `opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh` runs the hourly `--worker-events-only` pass only after a full pass completed that day. Because the shared DB's full pass never completes, every hourly run is another full pass with the same 60 s outcome.

## What

`_archive_run_batches` in `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` shrinks `next_limit` only after a batch *succeeds* (about line 1581). Every run restarts at `ARCHIVE_BATCH_SIZE` (500, or 10 in held mode) and the 64 MiB `OPENCODE_DB_ARCHIVE_BATCH_BYTES`. `_archive_select_batch` (about line 1491) sizes each candidate with a separate `sqlite3` process using `LENGTH(CAST(data AS BLOB))`, which loads every payload, including overflow chains. When sizing plus copy + verify + delete (`_archive_execute_batch`, about line 1650) does not fit the remaining per-DB budget (`OPENCODE_DB_ARCHIVE_ASYNC_BUDGET_SEC`, 60 s, enforced by `_archive_with_deadline`), the deadline kills the batch, SQLite rolls it back, and the next run retries the identical batch. Worker-event expiry (`.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-worker-events.sh`) has the same failure mode with a fixed 500-row / 64 MiB batch.

Change:

1. **Persisted adaptation (both batch loops).** Keep a per-DB state file keyed by a hash of the active DB path, next to the existing `~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-db-archive.deferrals`, not beside the DB. Write an in-flight marker holding the current limits before each batch write. If a run starts and finds the marker, the previous batch never committed (deadline, SIGTERM or SIGKILL): halve the limits (floors: 1 session or 10 event rows; 1 MiB). After a committed batch, clear the marker and double the limits back toward the defaults. A worker-event batch that returns rc 124 halves its limits the same way.
2. **Cheap sizing.** Size the candidate prefix in one SQL query that uses `octet_length()` (SQLite 3.43+ reads only the record header; see `_archive_worker_event_size_expr`) with a cumulative window sum, instead of one `sqlite3` process per candidate. Keep the `LENGTH(CAST(... AS BLOB))` fallback for older SQLite.
3. **Order by value.** In `_archive_move_phase`, give worker-event expiry the larger share of the budget when the expirable set is non-empty. Events of terminated workers are expendable (GH#38491), and expiring them first means the session move no longer copies and verifies those bytes into the archive.
4. **Head-of-line protection.** If a 1-session batch is still interrupted, record that session ID as oversized-deferred and exclude it from `candidate_filter` on later runs. Log one warning naming the session and the remedy: a manual run with a larger `--max-duration-seconds` while the host is idle.
5. **Unambiguous logging.** Have the worker-event pass report `timed out after Ns; 0 committed` separately from `expired 0`. Add one per-DB line with per-phase seconds (event expiry, worker-event expiry, candidate preparation, sizing, each batch write).

Keep the idle gate, held-mode cap, copy → verify → delete semantics and per-DB deadline unchanged.

## Why

The archive is the only bound on the shared DB that every headless worker merges into (`_merge_worker_db` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-database.sh`, 5 s busy timeout). Worker exit-86 shared-schema initialization failures also appear on this host; a causal link to DB size is not yet proven. A livelock that defers forever also misleads the deferral-streak notice, which blames holders, and 35.7 GB of reclaimable events stay in place.

## How (files)

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`: `_archive_run_batches` (about 1525-1588), `_archive_select_batch` (about 1491-1523), `_archive_execute_batch` (marker around the write, about 1650), `_archive_prepare_candidates` (oversized-deferred exclusion), `_archive_move_phase` (about 1202, budget split). Reference pattern for state files: `DEFERRALS_FILE` in `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh`.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-worker-events.sh`: `_archive_expire_worker_events` (rc 124 handling, persisted batch size, timeout log line).
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh` (existing archive and worker-event cases live here): add one case where a stubbed batch write exceeds the deadline once; assert that the next run halves the limit and archives at least one session.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-worker-events.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`
- `TODO.md`

## Acceptance

- A run interrupted during a batch write leaves a marker, and the next run halves the session and byte limits before selecting.
- A committed batch clears the marker and grows the limits back toward the defaults.
- A worker-event batch that times out is logged as a timeout and halves its row/byte limits for the next run.
- Candidate sizing for one batch uses one SQLite query when `octet_length()` is available.
- A 1-session batch that is still interrupted is skipped on later runs, with one warning naming it.
- The existing archive and worker-event tests pass; ShellCheck is clean.
- After deployment, the shared-DB entries in `~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-db-archive.log` show non-zero `Worker event expiry pass complete: expired N` and `Archived N/M sessions` lines, and the eligible count falls across consecutive nightly runs.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-worker-events.sh
rg -n "Worker event expiry pass complete: expired [1-9]|Archived [0-9]+/[0-9]+ sessions" ~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-db-archive.log | tail -n 20
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: Fluent Boards: SSH/WP-CLI helper to read and work setup-board cards (no native list/move/comment commands)
body:
## Observed (2026-11-16)

A delivered WordPress multisite network ships a Fluent Boards "Website Setup"
board (48 cards) whose cards tell the owner to "ask aidevops to read this board
and work through the open cards over SSH with WP-CLI". aidevops has no tool for
that:

- Fluent Boards 2.3.0 registers `wp fluent_boards` with only
  `create_random_tasks` and `crm_role_assign`: no list, show, move, comment or
  checklist commands.
- The native MCP route (`fluent-boards/mcp`, `tools/wordpress/fluent-mcp.md`)
  needs the WordPress MCP Adapter (not loaded on this network) and, on
  multisite, Fluent Boards network-activated (it was per-site active), plus an
  Application Password user. That is a site change the owner has to approve
  before any card can be read.
- To read the board the session wrote throwaway `wp eval-file` scripts over
  `$wpdb` (`{prefix}fbs_boards`, `fbs_board_terms` with `type='stage'`,
  `fbs_tasks` with `parent_id` for checklist items, `fbs_comments`), uploaded
  them with `scp` and ran them per blog with `--url`.

`tools/wordpress/fluent-mcp.md` "REST and WP-CLI fallback" also says "The Fluent
plugins register no WP-CLI commands of their own"; on this site `fluent_boards`,
`fluent_crm`, `fluent_support`, `fluentform` and `fluent-smtp` commands exist
(none read or update board cards).

## Proposed capability

A helper, e.g. `.agents/scripts/fluent-boards-helper.sh` (with a bundled PHP
file uploaded per run and removed afterwards), working over an SSH alias:

- `boards --ssh ALIAS --path WP --url URL` — boards with stage names and counts
- `cards --board ID|TITLE [--stage S] [--json]` — cards, stage, status,
  checklist progress, comment count
- `show --card ID` — description as plain text, checklist, comments (scan with
  `prompt-guard-helper.sh scan-stdin` before display: card text is third-party)
- `move --card ID --stage S`, `comment --card ID --body-file F`,
  `check --card ID --item ID` — writes through Fluent Boards' own models
  (`FluentBoards\App\Models\Task`, `Comment`) so activity logs and hooks run,
  with a read-back after each write

Then add a "Work a setup board" section to `tools/wordpress/fluent-mcp.md`:
read all cards, classify each as verifiable-now / agent-doable / needs-owner
(account, payment, identity, legal), post evidence as a comment, move to Done
only after the card's own "Done when" check passes, never post keys or
passwords in cards or comments. Correct the "no WP-CLI commands" sentence.

## Files

- New: `.agents/scripts/fluent-boards-helper.sh` (+ PHP payload)
- Edit: `.agents/tools/wordpress/fluent-mcp.md`
- Possibly: `.agents/tools/wordpress/ultimate-multisite.md` (order delivery
  uses Fluent Boards cards)

## Verification

- On a LocalWP site with Fluent Boards: `boards`, `cards`, `show` match the
  admin UI; `move` and `comment` appear in the board's activity and in the UI;
  multisite `--url` reads the right blog's `wp_N_fbs_*` tables.
- Works on Hostinger shared hosting, where `proc_open()` is disabled (no
  `wp db query`; use `$wpdb` in PHP).
- ShellCheck clean.

title: t19057: fix(headless-runtime): accept labelled POST_PR_HANDOFF lines so verified hand...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19057` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-16 | **Started:** 2026-11-16
**Tags:** `interactive` `bug`

## Outcome

fix(headless-runtime): accept labelled POST_PR_HANDOFF lines so verified handoffs do not loop as premature exits

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


**Task ID:** `t19057` | **Issue:** GH#38596

## Origin

Interactive session (productivity mission), from tracing the 24h `premature_exit` worker family (24 runs, all exit 77, 11 session keys; 407 of 640 worker-minutes on those keys went to premature exits). One key, `issue-25152` in a managed app repo, used all 10 continuation retries in a single run, replying each time with an unchanged handoff report.

Read-only analysis of the shared OpenCode DB (last 72h) found 22 premature-exit continuation prompts across 12 worker sessions. The assistant reply that triggered each continuation:

| Trigger | Count |
|---|---|
| `POST_PR_HANDOFF` written in a form other than an exact standalone line | 9 |
| no terminal marker (invented states such as `FULL_LOOP: PARTIAL, not complete`, or real incomplete work) | 9 |
| BLOCKED prose in checkpoint-continuation sessions (separate GH#37926 receipt path, out of scope) | 3 |
| other | 1 |

The missed handoff forms were `FULL_LOOP: POST_PR_HANDOFF`, `POST_PR_HANDOFF: <summary>`, `` `POST_PR_HANDOFF`: <summary> `` and `Outcome: POST_PR_HANDOFF. <summary>`.

## What

1. `output_has_post_pr_handoff_signal` and the `has_post_pr_handoff` check inside `output_has_completion_signal` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`) accept only a line exactly equal to `POST_PR_HANDOFF`. `_HEADLESS_BLOCKED_LINE_PATTERN` in the same file already tolerates a leading `Outcome:`/`Status:`/`Result:` label, bold/backtick wrapping and trailing prose. Add `_HEADLESS_POST_PR_HANDOFF_LINE_PATTERN` with the same shape: the marker must lead a model-text line, optionally after `>` quote markup and an `Outcome|Status|Result|State|FULL_LOOP` label, optionally wrapped in `**`, `__` or backticks, and followed only by end of line or a `:`, `.`, `;`, space-hyphen, `—` or `–` separator. Reject negated forms (`POST_PR_HANDOFF: not yet`, `: none`, `: no`) and mid-sentence mentions (`I will mention POST_PR_HANDOFF later`, `POST_PR_HANDOFF is not valid here`). `TASK_COMPLETE` stays exact.
2. The premature-exit continuation prompt in `_handle_cmd_run_continuation_attempt` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-run.sh`) always says "implement the required code changes … create a PR", even after the worker's PR has merged. Add one sentence: when the task's PR already exists (open or merged) and only CI, review, merge or work outside this attempt remains, end with `POST_PR_HANDOFF` alone on its own line, and always put the terminal marker alone on its own line.

## Why

A missed handoff marker turns a finished worker into a continuation loop. The model reports the same state each turn, then the run exhausts its continuation budget and is recorded as `premature_exit`, which feeds fast-fail and escalation and can redispatch a task that is already handed off. The marker only routes into `_hrw_gate_post_pr_handoff`, which independently verifies the exact-head PR, summary and linkage. A false positive therefore lands on the verified-handoff failure path, never on unverified success.

## How (files)

Keep synthetic-part and tool-output exclusions unchanged.

title: t19058: fix(setup): ai-session deploy redeploys incrementally when canonical main adv...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19058` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-16 | **Started:** 2026-11-16
**Tags:** `interactive` `bug`

## Outcome

fix(setup): ai-session deploy redeploys incrementally when canonical main advances mid-deploy instead of rolling back into a full setup

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


**Task ID:** `t19058` | **Issue:** GH#38607

## Origin

Interactive session (productivity mission). A manual `aidevops update` to v3.39.211 timed out after 900s waiting for the setup lock. The lock owner was an auto-update `setup.sh --stage ai-session` that ran for about 35 minutes:

1. The incremental deploy captured `current_sha=1c8d94d1e8d5` and spent 14m25s in `deploy_aidevops_agents` (05:16:15Z→05:30:40Z).
2. Canonical `main` fast-forwarded to `3a6362f78661` at 05:28:59Z (a governed merge's canonical sync).
3. Verification failed with `Runtime bundle convergence failed: source checkout HEAD 3a6362f78661 does not match release commit 1c8d94d1e8d5`. Setup rolled the consistent 1c8d94 bundle back and ran a full setup, which redeployed for another 6m56s.

Read-only classification of all 193 `falling back to full setup` events in `~/.aidevops/logs/auto-update.log`:

| Cause | Count | Last 3 days |
|---|---|---|
| stale activation refused (older candidate) | 83 | 0 |
| setup implementation changed | 43 | 3 |
| **convergence: source checkout HEAD advanced** | **35** | **5** |
| setup.sh changed | 20 | 1 |
| deploy verification: stale core plugin file | 8 | 0 |
| other | 4 | 0 |

`deploy_aidevops_agents` wall time (from `setup-stage-timings.log`): median 207–318s per day for 2026-11-12..15, then 447s with p90 864s on 2026-11-16. The host runs 14–33 deploys a day. With a multi-minute deploy and frequent merges, the canonical checkout moving mid-deploy is routine, not exceptional.

## What

Make one bundle stage describe one commit end to end, and let the ai-session verification accept that commit when the checkout has only fast-forwarded past it.

1. `_runtime_bundle_stage` resolves the full source commit once (`_AIDEVOPS_STAGED_SOURCE_SHA`). The bundle ID, manifest `git_sha`, copied tree, `aidevops.sh` and `VERSION` all come from that one short window, followed by an assertion that HEAD did not move during the copy. Before this change:
   - the manifest re-read HEAD after the npm installs;
   - `aidevops.sh` was installed after post-copy;
   - `VERSION` was copied in post-copy.

   Any of these could mix a later commit into a bundle labelled with the earlier one.
2. `_runtime_bundle_validate` compares the bundle VERSION with the version read at the pinned commit. `_verify_deployed_core_plugin_freshness` compares the 54 core plugin files with the pinned commit's Git objects (`_core_plugin_file_check`), not the live checkout.
3. `runtime-bundle-verifier.sh`: opt-in caller-local `_AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_VERIFY_ALLOW_SOURCE_ADVANCE=1` accepts a source checkout whose HEAD is a descendant of the expected commit and records `_AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_VERIFY_SOURCE_ADVANCED_TO`. The manifest, bundle ID, VERSION, stamp and sentinel checks still pin the expected commit. Release, update and full-loop adoption callers do not set it and keep exact equality.
4. `setup.sh` `_setup_ai_session_verify_deploy <floor_sha>`: sets the allowance and verifies the activated bundle's stamp commit when it lies between the setup-start floor and HEAD. When the checkout advanced, it prints an info line instead of rolling back. The full-setup fallback captures the floor before the full setup runs, not after.

## Why

Each race costs a rollback of a correct runtime plus a full setup: a second multi-minute deploy, plist and scheduler refreshes, and a long-held setup lock. The lock blocks manual `aidevops update` and other setup callers; the 900s lock wait exits 1. The newer commit is deployed on the next auto-update cycle either way, so the full setup buys nothing.

## How (files)

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/runtime-bundle-verifier.sh` — `_runtime_bundle_verify_source`: opt-in descendant acceptance; reset `_AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_VERIFY_SOURCE_ADVANCED_TO` in `verify_aidevops_runtime_bundle_convergence`.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy-bundle.sh` — new `_runtime_bundle_source_sha` and `_runtime_bundle_assert_source_unchanged`; `_runtime_bundle_write_manifest` takes an optional pinned SHA; `_runtime_bundle_validate` takes the pinned version; `_runtime_bundle_stage` pins and moves `aidevops.sh` and `VERSION` into the copy window.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh` — `_core_plugin_file_check` helper used by `_verify_deployed_core_plugin_freshness`; post-copy copies VERSION only when the stage has not already.
- EDIT `setup.sh` — `_setup_ai_session_verify_deploy` and the ai-session full-setup fallback floor.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/runtime-bundle-verifier.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy-bundle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh`
- `setup.sh`
- `todo/tasks/t19058-brief.md`
- `TODO.md`

## Acceptance

- With the allowance set, a bundle at commit X verifies when HEAD is a descendant of X. It is rejected when HEAD has diverged or when a sentinel differs. Without the allowance, any HEAD ≠ X is rejected exactly as before.
- A bundle's ID, manifest `git_sha`, `aidevops.sh` and `VERSION` all come from the same commit. A HEAD move during the copy fails the stage with an explicit message instead of producing a mixed bundle.
- Existing suites pass: `test-runtime-bundle-verifier.sh`, `test-atomic-runtime-bundle-deploy.sh`, `test-agent-deploy-staging-invariant.sh`, `test-setup-scoped-dispatch.sh`, `test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh`, `test-script-drift-detection.sh`, `test-deploy-mutex.sh`, `test-agent-deploy-pulse-runtime.sh`, `test-runtime-bundle-rollback.sh`, `test-status-runtime-bundle-integrity.sh`.
- ShellCheck clean on changed shell files.
- Post-release production signal: `Runtime bundle convergence failed: source checkout HEAD … does not match release commit` stops appearing in `auto-update.log`, and `Checkout advanced to … during deploy` appears instead.

## Non-goals

- Deploy wall time itself (bimodal 22–44s vs 416–866s) — separate investigation; copies measured at 4–7s and `du` passes at about 17s, so the cost lies in later post-copy or activation steps.
- `aidevops update`'s own post-setup verification keeps exact equality with the pulled commit.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck -x setup.sh .agents/scripts/runtime-bundle-verifier.sh .agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy-bundle.sh .agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh
for t in test-runtime-bundle-verifier test-atomic-runtime-bundle-deploy test-agent-deploy-staging-invariant test-setup-scoped-dispatch test-aidevops-update-transaction test-runtime-bundle-rollback; do bash ".agents/scripts/tests/$t.sh"; done
rg -c "source checkout HEAD [0-9a-f]+ does not match release commit" ~/.aidevops/logs/auto-update.log
```

</details>

`claim-task-id.sh` reallocates task IDs whose TODO.md entry uses a non-`[ ]`/`[x]` checkbox, such as declined/cancelled `- [-] tNNN`. Make the TODO.md collision guard treat every checkbox state as occupied.

  `[-]` (declined), `[~]` or any other single-character state is not matched.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh` `_id_exists_in_todo`, match any single checkbox character: `\[[^]]\]` (or an explicit set covering space, `x`, `X`, `-`, `~`, `!`).

3. Add a case to the existing claim-task-id collision test (search `.agents/scripts/tests/` for `_id_exists_in_todo` or `TODO.md collision`) with a `- [-] tNNN` entry.

## Verification

- The collision test above passes and a `[-]` entry is skipped like `[x]`.

Duplicate IDs inherit labels and TODO state from the declined task and break `ref:GH#` mapping. The allocated ID in the observed run was abandoned unused.

title: claim-task-id.sh falls back to a staler default-branch counter and reissues used task IDs
body:
## What

When `resolve_implicit_counter_branch` refuses a stale dedicated `task-id-counter` branch (`COUNTER_BRANCH_STALE ... refusing implicit migration`), `claim-task-id.sh` falls back to the default branch's `.task-counter`, even when that counter is far *more* stale. Allocation then walks forward from an old value and reissues task IDs that are already used by GitHub issues and PRs. The collision guard only sees TODO.md `[ ]`/`[x]` lines, so it misses most of them.

## Evidence (observed 2026-11-16 in a managed project repo)

- Dedicated branch counter: 22418. TODO.md seed: 24871, from two out-of-band IDs (`t24870`, `t24330`) whose issues were created on 2026-11-15 without a counter claim. Default-branch `.task-counter`: 18604.
- `claim-task-id-counter.sh` (deployed copy ~line 779) refused the dedicated branch because `candidate_counter < todo_seed`, then used the default branch at 18604, which is below both.
- Claims that day allocated `t18605` (a declined `[-]` entry, see marcusquinn/aidevops#38609), `t18612` (declined) and `t18617`. Each had been used before: `t18617` already titled closed issue `#14171` and three merged PRs. Two new issues were created with duplicate IDs and had to be retitled.
- Separately, the TODO issue-sync workflow then rewrote `ref:GH#<old>` on the declined `t18605` line to the new issue number, destroying the original reference (commit message `chore: sync ref:GH#NNNNN to TODO.md [skip ci]`).
- Recovery that worked: `claim-task-id.sh --sync-counter-branch` fast-forwarded the dedicated branch to 24871. The next claim auto-selected it.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh` `resolve_implicit_counter_branch`: when the dedicated branch is behind only the TODO seed, but ahead of the default branch counter, never fall back to the lower default-branch counter. Either auto-run the existing audited `sync_counter_branch` catch-up (forward-only), or fail closed with the `--sync-counter-branch` remedy, instead of allocating from a stale source.
2. In any allocation path, treat `max(selected counter, todo_seed)` as the floor so allocation never starts below the TODO seed.
3. Issue-sync TODO writer (the workflow/script that emits `chore: sync ref:GH#... to TODO.md`): do not overwrite an existing different `ref:GH#` on a task line; report the duplicate instead.

## Verification

- Extend the existing claim-task-id counter tests (search `.agents/scripts/tests/` for `COUNTER_BRANCH_STALE`) with a fixture where dedicated < TODO seed and default < dedicated: allocation must not return an ID below the TODO seed.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh`.

## Related

- marcusquinn/aidevops#38609 (`[-]` entries not treated as collisions).
