**Task ID:** `t19066` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-16 | **Started:** 2026-11-16
**Tags:** `interactive` `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(runtime): service PATH must keep aidevops gh/git shims ahead of npm global bin

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `service PATH gh shim bypass launchd npm global bin` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: last change to `runtime-env.sh` is GH#38526 / PR #38549 (the regression source); 0 open PRs touch it

## What

Service PATH (launchd `EnvironmentVariables.PATH`, systemd `Environment=`, cron) must keep the aidevops shim directories (`~/.aidevops/agents/scripts`, `~/.aidevops/bin`) ahead of the npm global bin. Since GH#38526 / PR #38549 the npm global bin leads the service PATH. On Homebrew-node hosts `npm prefix -g` is `/opt/homebrew`, so `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh` and `/opt/homebrew/bin/git` shadow the aidevops `gh` shim and the canonical-git guard for every launchd daemon and its children.

## Why

Evidence (2026-11-16, after the plist regeneration at 05:50):

- `plutil -extract EnvironmentVariables.PATH raw ~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.aidevops.pulse-watchdog.plist` starts `/opt/homebrew/bin:~/.bun/bin:~/.local/bin:~/.aidevops/agents/scripts:~/.aidevops/bin`.
- Pulse re-execs into a runtime bundle (`pulse-runtime-pin.sh:290`), so the `export PATH="${SCRIPT_DIR}:${PATH}"` re-prioritisation at `pulse-wrapper.sh:308` prepends a bundle dir, which every later `runtime-env.sh` source (`runtime-env.sh:293` → `aidevops_compose_path`, line 46) strips. The inherited service order then wins: a live pulse child (`_dlw_observer`) has `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:...` with no shim dir ahead of it.
- A 3-minute process probe of native `gh` processes: 149 of 266 had bare argv0 `gh` (PATH lookup straight to native) rather than the canonical Cellar path the shim always uses. Parents: `pulse-wrapper.sh`, `stats-wrapper.sh`, bundled `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`, `review-bot-gate-helper.sh`, `timeout 15 gh ...`.
- Impact: those calls skip `gh-api-calls.log` instrumentation, REST/GraphQL budget routing, the transport governor and write guards, and daemon `git` calls skip the canonical-git guard. Unaccounted REST-core usage blocks dispatch through `rest-core-quota` (GH#38332 / GH#37888).

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/runtime-env.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-launchd-sanitized-path.sh`

### Change

- `.agents/scripts/runtime-env.sh` `aidevops_service_path` (about line 91): build `stable_path` as `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts:~/.aidevops/bin:<npm global bin>:~/.bun/bin:~/.local/bin`. This keeps GH#38526's requirement (npm global bin ahead of `~/.bun/bin`) and restores the invariant stated at `runtime-env.sh:268-269` ("framework shims intentionally lead PATH"). Update the function comment.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-launchd-sanitized-path.sh` `test_sanitized_path_filters_unsafe_entries`: update the order assertion and add a case with `_AIDEVOPS_NPM_GLOBAL_BIN` set to a dir containing a `gh`, asserting the shim dirs precede it.

Plists regenerate on the next `aidevops update` / `setup.sh` (launchd install-if-changed), so the fix applies after release + update.

## Acceptance

- `aidevops_service_path` output starts with `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts:~/.aidevops/bin:` and lists the npm global bin before `~/.bun/bin`.
- With that PATH, `command -v gh` resolves to the aidevops shim even when the npm global bin contains `gh`.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-runtime-env.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`

title: fix(canonical-recovery): stale mkdir lock after auto-update timeout blocks all further updates
body:
## What

When systemd kills an auto-update run while it holds `aidevops-canonical-recovery.lock`, the lock directory is left behind. After that, every auto-update run stops at `BLOCKED: canonical recovery lock is already held`, so the host never updates again until someone runs `rmdir` on the lock by hand.

## Observed (one Linux host, user systemd, 2026-11-15 → 2026-11-16)

- 2026-11-15 10:56:41 local: `aidevops-auto-update.service` started a commit-freshness fast-forward of the canonical aidevops checkout. The audit log recorded `operation.verify "Canonical current-branch fast-forward authorized"` (`reason=aidevops-update`), and a dirty-state backup was written.
- 11:06:41: systemd hit `TimeoutStartSec=600`, logged `start operation timed out. Terminating.`, and killed the run (`status=15/TERM`, `KillMode=control-group`).
- The `EXIT` trap that calls `rmdir` on the lock did not run, so `<common_dir>/aidevops-canonical-recovery.lock` (an empty directory) stayed in place.
- From 11:07 on, every 10-minute run logged `BLOCKED: canonical recovery lock is already held` followed by `Audited canonical fast-forward failed; preserving local history`. That happened 123 times over about 20.5 hours. The host stayed on v3.39.203 while v3.39.211 was available.
- Recovery: no process held the lock (checked with `ps`), and it was an empty directory 20.5 h old, so `rmdir` was run by hand. The next run updated to v3.39.211 and then v3.39.212. Every run since has finished successfully.

## Why

The lock is a bare `mkdir` with no owner PID or timestamp, and it is cleaned up only by a shell `EXIT` trap. That trap does not run when the process is killed by SIGKILL, and it does not run reliably when SIGTERM hits a child process mid-pipeline. Nothing ever expires the lock, so a single timeout stops updates on that host until someone finds and removes it. The host then falls behind on fixes, such as the ETag change needed by #37888.

## How

Files to modify (all paths verified on `main`):

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh`. There are three acquisition sites: `ffl` fast-forward (`local lock=` near line 1083, `mkdir` near line 1103), transfer (`transfer_lock` near line 1423), and `fast-forward-current` (`lock_dir` near line 1636).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/deploy-agents-on-merge.sh`. `SOURCE_LOCK_DIR` near line 196 shares the same directory.

Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh:346-374` already handles its own lock safely. It writes the owner PID, removes the lock when that PID is dead or reused (t2421), and expires it by age.

Suggested approach:

1. When acquiring the lock, write an owner record (`pid`, process start time, `epoch`, operation) inside the lock directory.
2. If the lock is already held, read the owner record. If the PID is dead, or alive but with a different start time (meaning the PID was reused), log the takeover to the tamper-evident audit log (`canonical-recovery-audit.jsonl`) and take the lock over atomically, for example by renaming it to a quarantine name and then running `mkdir`.
3. A lock directory with no owner record (left by the old format) can be taken over only when no `canonical-recovery-helper.sh` or `deploy-agents-on-merge.sh` process exists for the repo and the directory is older than the longest supported holder timeout.
4. Keep the existing safety rules: never take over a lock whose owner is alive, and never touch the preservation or backup refs.

Optional, separate concern: `TimeoutStartSec=600` was too short for this run (fast-forward plus dirty-state preservation plus deploy). Check whether the auto-update timeout or the fast-forward duration needs its own fix. File that separately if it recurs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Killing a holder with SIGKILL while it holds the lock does not block the next `fast-forward-current` run for longer than one auto-update interval.
- [ ] A lock held by a live process is still respected, with no false takeover.
- [ ] Every takeover writes one audit record that names the dead owner.
- [ ] `shellcheck` is clean on the edited scripts, and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery-helper.sh` passes.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh .agents/scripts/deploy-agents-on-merge.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery-helper.sh
```

Found while running the read-only Pulse-host baseline for #35359. A host stuck on an old version also blocks the re-measure step in #37888.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-lock.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-ffl.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/deploy-agents-on-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery-helper.sh`

title: t19067: perf(checkpoints): land a paused landable worker draft at once instead of after the fuse window
body:
## What

When `dispatch-stalled` would pause a stalled worker draft head (two stalls with no higher model tier, or the per-PR fuse), and that draft is landable now, land it immediately instead of pausing. Landable means additive (no removed or renamed files), `MERGEABLE`, all reported checks green, and a non-closing `For #N` link to the issue. Use the existing GH#37779 terminal action's land branch (`gh pr ready`, then the guarded Pulse merge pass). Non-landable heads keep today's behaviour: attention record, re-arm windows, fuse, then the 12h terminal close.

## Why

Interactive full-loop sessions merge verified partial progress and continue from the default branch. Workers instead park it in drafts behind exact-head continuation, 12h re-arm windows that double per stall (up to 2^6), the per-PR fuse, and a further 12h "brief owner" window. The design asks for a human decision that, per the project's operating aims, users should rarely need to make.

Evidence from the 24h Pulse log up to 2026-11-16T10:00Z:

- One private managed repository (`<private-repo>`) has 60 open worker draft PRs; 39 are `MERGEABLE` with no failing checks.
- 357 dispatch candidate evaluations ended `dispatch_with_dedup rc=1`, costing 22,175s. Draft-checkpoint reasons (`worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` 79, `stale_draft_checkpoint` 71) are the largest category.
- 25 distinct drafts paused (`STALLED_CHECKPOINT_TIER_UNAVAILABLE` / `REARM_BLOCKED`); 17 are still open. 7 are landable now (MERGEABLE, green, non-closing `For #N`), and 7 more show `UNKNOWN` mergeability that GitHub computes lazily.
- The terminal action has landed only once in the whole log (a `per_pr_fuse` land in `<private-repo>`, merged 2026-11-15T16:58Z, issue stayed open). That shows the land path works; it is just gated behind days of windows.
- Dispatch rounds routinely end `PRIORITY_RESERVATION requested=8 held=8 launched=0` while these issues sit behind draft checkpoints.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-terminal-action.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-fuse.sh`
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`

### Change

- `pr-checkpoint-terminal-action.sh`: add `AIDEVOPS_PCC_LAND_PAUSED_CHECKPOINTS` (default `1`; `0` restores waiting). Give `_pcc_terminal_checkpoint_action` an optional 7th argument `land_only`, which returns 1 with `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_TERMINAL_SKIPPED reason=not_landable` instead of closing. Add `_pcc_land_paused_checkpoint`: a cheap pre-check on the PR JSON the caller already holds (checks success, `MERGEABLE`, non-closing `For #N` link), skipped when a current trusted revision approval owns scheduling; otherwise call the terminal action with cause `paused_landable` in `land_only` mode. All existing fresh-evidence fences, the fenced claim and the one-record-per-head marker still apply.
- `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` `_pcc_dispatch_stalled`: add `mergeable,mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup` to the existing `gh pr view` fields (no extra call). As the first step of the pause branch (`stalls >= 2` without an escalation tier, or the fuse), call `_pcc_land_paused_checkpoint` and return 0 when it lands.
- `tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-fuse.sh`: keep the legacy fuse cases on `_PCC_LAND_PAUSED_CHECKPOINTS=0`. Add one case: a fused landable head lands at once (`cause=paused_landable`, `gh pr ready`, no attention post, no continuation dispatch), regardless of the terminal window.
- `reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md` "Bounded terminal action": document immediate landing and the opt-out.

## Acceptance

- A paused, landable worker draft is marked ready in the same evaluation, with one `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_TERMINAL_ACTION ... action=ready_for_merge cause=paused_landable` record per head.
- Non-landable paused heads keep the existing attention/re-arm/fuse/close behaviour; `AIDEVOPS_PCC_LAND_PAUSED_CHECKPOINTS=0` restores the previous behaviour exactly.
- No additional `gh` call for paused heads that fail the cheap pre-check.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` (sources the fuse module)
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-tier-escalation.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-attention.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-terminal-action.sh .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- Post-deploy: `rg "cause=paused_landable" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` shows landings, and the affected repository's open worker-draft count falls as those PRs merge.

title: t19068: fix(recovery): a changed recovery policy ends human_decision suppression
body:
**Task ID:** `t19068` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-16 | **Started:** 2026-11-16
**Tags:** `interactive` `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(recovery): a changed recovery policy ends human_decision suppression

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

A changed repository recovery policy ends the 24-hour suppression of a recorded `human_decision`, so the Pulse recovery supervisor re-assesses those issues on its next pass with the authority the maintainer just delegated.

## Why

`_tbr_decision_active` in `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` suppresses re-assessment of a recorded decision for `BLOCKER_RECOVERY_DECISION_TTL` (default 86400 s). It ends early only when a maintainer replies (GH#38311). When a repository restores, adds or changes its recovery policy, decisions recorded as `human_decision` *because no delegated authority existed* stay parked for up to a day, and are only reconsidered on the next 3-hour supervisor slot after that.

Observed: a managed private repository lost its policy when `.aidevops.json` became untracked (the t19065 migration case); the supervisor recorded 40 `human_decision` outcomes there (25 on 2026-11-16 alone), most of them routine outlier/source choices that the repo's `outlier_hold` / `session_cap_split` actions delegate. One decision says so explicitly: "Maintainer authorizes the factory split ..., or enables session_cap_split in the repo default-branch recovery policy; no delegated policy exists for this runner". Restoring the policy at the conventional location does not wake them.

## How

- `tbr_record`: for `wake == human_decision`, stamp `policy_fingerprint`: a hash of the policy's normalized `.actions` JSON (`jq -S -c`), or `none` when `recovery-policy-helper.sh` exits 3. On a failed observation, omit the field. Reuse `_terminal_blocker_hash` (`.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:142`); source that file lazily, as other functions in the helper already do.
- Fingerprint the actions, not `revision`: `revision` is the default-branch commit SHA and changes on every commit, which would cancel every suppression on each merge.
- One per-process cached loader feeds both `_tbr_policy_enabled` (unchanged contract: 0 enabled, 1 absent/empty, 2 unreadable) and the fingerprint, so a pass loads each repo's policy at most once.
- `_tbr_decision_active`: for `human_decision` within the TTL, when the current fingerprint is readable and differs from the recorded one, return 1 (not active). Treat a missing recorded field (legacy records) as `none`, so repos without a policy are unaffected and a newly restored policy wakes legacy decisions once. Unreadable current policy keeps suppression (fail closed on observation, as today).
- Document the rule in the helper header and `reference/recovery-policy.md`.

## Acceptance

- A `human_decision` recorded with fingerprint `none` stops suppressing once a policy with actions loads; the same record keeps suppressing while the policy stays absent or unreadable.
- A record stamped with the current fingerprint keeps suppressing until the TTL or a maintainer reply, as today.
- Non-`human_decision` wakes are unaffected.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-discovery.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-recovery-policy.sh` pass; ShellCheck clean.

## Files to modify

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` (`_tbr_policy_enabled`, `_tbr_decision_active`, `tbr_record`, header)
- EDIT `.agents/reference/recovery-policy.md`
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-discovery.sh` (decision-active cases near line 759)

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/recovery-policy.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-discovery.sh`

</details>

<details>

## Brief Workflow

title: fix(pulse): NMR triage on Anthropic-OAuth-only runners is misclassified and relaunched every cycle
body:
## What

Public NMR triage reviews never complete on a runner whose only headless provider is Anthropic via OAuth, and the pulse misreports the cause. Make the pulse (1) classify this failure correctly and (2) stop relaunching triage every cycle on a runner that cannot run it, leaving the item for a runner with native provider auth.

## Why (observed evidence, 2026-11-16)

- `~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`, `role=triage`: every triage review since the runner's pool became Anthropic-only failed: 6 of 6 runs (`triage-review-38459` x2 on 2026-11-15, `triage-review-38640` x4 on 2026-11-16). Each run returned `result=local_error`, `exit_code=86`, and took about 1.3 s, so no model was called. Earlier triage runs on `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` all succeeded.
- `pulse.log` logs each one as `Triage runtime failure for #38640 ...: triage-runtime-failed` and retries on the next cycle (5 consecutive cycles between 09:50Z and 11:00Z).
- Reproduction with a harmless prompt: `headless-runtime-helper.sh run --role triage --session-key diag-... --dir <workspace> --title diag --prompt "Reply with the single word OK." --model anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 --agent triage-review` exits 86. Its 20th output line is the explicit error from `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh:112-118`:
  `Public triage provider authentication unavailable: Anthropic OAuth requires the plugin disabled by OPENCODE_PURE (Model not found)`

## Root cause

1. **Misclassification (regression of GH#33057 / PR #33324).** `.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch-review.sh:174-177` classifies the failure from `head -c 1000` of the combined stdout+stderr file. The runtime now prints about 19 `[lifecycle]` INFO lines (about 4-5 KB) before the error, so the marker that `_triage_runtime_infra_failure_reason` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch-core.sh:477-495`) matches never reaches the sample. The result falls through to the generic `triage-runtime-failed`.
2. **Unbounded futile retry.** Even a correct `triage-provider-auth-unsupported` result is only treated as an infrastructure failure (`pulse-ancillary-dispatch-core.sh:528`): it keeps no retry budget, so the pulse relaunches the same impossible triage every cycle. The runner cannot complete it until its provider pool changes.

## How (worker-ready)

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch-review.sh` (around lines 172-187): build the classification input so fixed markers anywhere in the bounded output file are found. For example, grep the file with fixed strings for the known markers, or sample head plus tail. Keep the existing rule that raw content is never persisted or logged.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch-core.sh` (`_triage_runtime_infra_failure_reason` and the caller that applies the infra result): when the reason is `triage-provider-auth-unsupported`, record a runner-local capability cooldown keyed by a fingerprint of the provider pool and auth types. `dispatch_triage_reviews` then skips model launch, logging one line per cooldown, until the fingerprint changes. Follow the existing `runner_capability_unmet` cooldown pattern used by dispatch enumeration (`Dispatch enumeration: ... runner_capability_unmet cooldown skipped ... (requirements unchanged; ttl=...)`).
- Optional, preferred if cheap: have triage model resolution skip providers whose only credential is OAuth for the public-triage boundary. A runner that also has an API-key or OpenAI credential then still triages.
- Do not weaken the trust boundary at `headless-runtime-invoke.sh:109-118`. Pure public triage must still never use the OAuth plugin or an ambient credential.

## Verification

- Extend the existing classification cases in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-triage-output-shape.sh` (see the `TRIAGE_TEST_RUNTIME_EXIT_STATUS=86` case near line 1116): put the auth-unavailable marker after more than 4 KB of lifecycle lines and assert `triage-provider-auth-unsupported`.
- On an Anthropic-OAuth-only runner with one pending NMR item, after one failed attempt, `pulse.log` shows the cooldown skip line instead of a new `Triage runtime failure` per cycle, and `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` gains no new `role=triage` `exit_code=86` rows until the provider pool changes.
- ShellCheck clean on the changed scripts.

# Installed-runtime canary acceptance for the managed worktree lifecycle

For #35359 (child; parent stays open for the per-account matrix and fleet closeout).

## What

Run the installed-runtime canary that #35359 step 5 requires, on one Pulse install, and record a redacted result. Use an isolated disposable repository and a harmless bounded worker, never production tasks. Prove each of:

1. Automatic and manual launch: generation, run id and provenance recorded.
2. Actual process identity bound to the recorded run.
3. Verified completion and sealing.
4. Archive-location receipt.
5. Independent restore from the archive.
6. Source removal only after restore verification.
7. Supported AUTO_MERGE and resumable interrupted-merge capture and restore through the installed scripts.

## Why

All known installs (2 accounts x 2 hosts, baselines on #35359) are `partial`: deployed and observed, but no install has passed the canary. Matching SHA-256 values, registry samples and `exit 0` do not establish that archive and restore work in the installed runtime.

## How

- Files Scope: `EDIT: .agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md` (redacted matrix row, near the "canary-1" row). Keep the file at or under the 500-line markdown ratchet. No implementation edits.

title: t19069: fix(setup): a service PATH generator change regenerates installed scheduler p...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19069` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-16 | **Started:** 2026-11-16
**Tags:** `interactive` `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(setup): a service PATH generator change regenerates installed scheduler plists

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `launchd plist PATH regenerate setup.sh non-interactive drift` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: last plist drift change is t19030 (`9a0c1dffea`); 0 open PRs or claimed issues touch the target files

## What

A change to the launchd service PATH generator (`aidevops_service_path` in `.agents/scripts/runtime-env.sh`) or the plist environment-override library (`.agents/scripts/plist-env-overrides-lib.sh`) regenerates the installed scheduler plists on the next update, the same way a scheduler template change already does.

## Why

t19066 (PR #38644, released in v3.39.213) moved the aidevops `gh`/`git` shim directories ahead of the npm global bin in `aidevops_service_path`. The deployed runtime contains the fix, but at 2026-11-16 11:42Z, an hour after the release deployed, every installed plist still had the old PATH. `com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist` and `sh.aidevops.pulse-watchdog.plist` both began `/opt/homebrew/bin:...`, and their mtimes (05:43 and 05:50) were earlier than the release. The plist content is generated from `runtime-env.sh`, but neither regeneration path watches that file:

- `scheduler_template_hash` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-template-hash.sh:52`) hashes only `setup/modules/schedulers*.sh` and `setup/_scheduler_runtime.sh`, so `check_launchd_plist_drift` (`.agents/scripts/auto-update-freshness-lib.sh:214`) sees no drift.
- `_setup_ai_session_plan_file` (`setup.sh:1319`) maps only those scheduler files to `_SETUP_AI_SESSION_NEEDS_SCHEDULERS`, so the incremental update stage never reruns the scheduler pass for a `runtime-env.sh` change.

As a result, a PATH fix takes effect only when an unrelated scheduler template happens to change. Until then, the native `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh` shadows the shim for every launchd daemon. Before t19066, a 3-minute probe saw 149 of 266 `gh` processes bypass the shim, losing call accounting, budget routing and write guards.

**Scope update (rebase, 2026-11-16):** GH#37888 (`6b46b0490c`) landed on `main` first and added `runtime-env.sh` to both the hash and the incremental planner. title: fix: native systemd lifecycle test fixtures are stale against registry-authorised retirement
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Fix stale native systemd lifecycle fixtures and name the missing-repository-config refusal

## What

The two opt-in native tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py` (`test_native_child_lifetime_and_guard`, `test_native_pulse_and_manual_share_one_lifecycle`) fail on current `main` at their archive-and-remove step. They exercise the production path `archive_worktree_path_recoverably` + `remove_archived_worktree_path`, which now calls `worker_lifecycle_cleanup_worktree` (registry-authorised retirement, GH#36224, 2026-11-01). The fixtures were written for the older managed-lifetime path only. Make the fixtures match the production path so the tests pass on a systemd host, and make the first failure name its cause.

This is evidence from a rollout canary on one Linux user-systemd Pulse host (`aidevops` v3.39.213, deployed SHA equal to `main`). It is a test/fixture drift finding, not a proven product regression. Parent rollout: #35359 (do not close it with this issue).

## Why

The installed-runtime canary for #35359 needs a real "archive, independent restore, source removal" pass. Those steps have never run because the tests stop before them. The opt-in tests are not run in CI (`rg AIDEVOPS_TEST_SYSTEMD .github` finds nothing), so the drift went unnoticed. Canary-1 reported "25 tests, 2 skipped", which are these two.

## Reproducer

Reproduced twice, root cause confirmed with a traceback in a scratch copy. Steps, on a Linux host with a working user-systemd manager:

1. Use a directory outside any canonical checkout as the working directory (the canonical Git guard blocks `git init` inside one).
2. Run: `AIDEVOPS_TEST_SYSTEMD=1 python3 <repo>/.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py -v`

Observed: 23 of 25 pass. Launch, `setsid` descendant, removal guard, sealing, proof and idle observation all pass. Both native tests then fail with:

```
[worker-lifecycle] retirement-refused status=unavailable detail=unexpected-error error=FileNotFoundError rc=2
```

Layers found, in order:

1. **No repository config in the fixture `HOME`.** `worker_lifecycle_cleanup_worktree` (`.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-state.sh:69-111`) passes `--repos-config "${HOME}/.config/aidevops/repos.json"`. The fixture replaces `HOME` with an empty directory, so `read_owned_file` raises `FileNotFoundError` in `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup.py:30-38` (`_repository_entries`). `cli_errors.error_details` maps it to a bare `FileNotFoundError`, and `_worker_lifecycle_report_refusal` prints it as `unexpected-error`. GH#36494 requires a named cause.
2. **Worktree not enrolled in the worker-lifecycle registry.** With a `repos.json` added, the error becomes `ValueError: not-enrolled` (`cleanup.py:188`, `enrollment.py:165`): the fixture worktree has no `aidevops-generation.json` marker. The fixtures enroll only in the managed-lifetime registry (`worktree-managed-lifetime.py enroll`), a separate registry.
3. **Fixture not isolated from the real registry.** When `AIDEVOPS_WORKSPACE_DIR` is set in the environment, `worker_lifecycle_state_dir` resolves to the real per-user registry, so the fixture's `cleanup-worktree` call reads real state (it only refused as `not-enrolled`; nothing was changed). The fixture must set `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_STATE_DIR` to a directory under its own temp root.
4. **Ordering trap.** Registering the fixture repo in `repos.json` before its `git commit` makes the canonical Git guard treat it as a canonical checkout (`BLOCKED by canonical Git guard ... git commit`). Write `repos.json` immediately before the archive step.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py
- EDIT: .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup.py (name a missing/unreadable repository config as a refusal, for example `repository-config-unavailable`, instead of letting `FileNotFoundError` escape)
- EDIT (only if the refusal mapping lives there): .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/refusal.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cli_errors.py
- EDIT (if a focused unit case is the cheapest way to pin the refusal): .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_failure_category.py

### Reference pattern

- Fixture enrollment for the worker-lifecycle registry: `worker-registry.py --state-dir <dir> init`, then `enroll --path <worktree> --initialize` (see the argparse table in `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/registry.py:60-192`) and the existing unit tests under `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/` for how they build an isolated store.
- Named-refusal precedent: GH#36494 / GH#38056 handling in `cli_errors.py` and `refusal.py`.
- Keep every fixture path under the test's own temp root; set `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_STATE_DIR` and write `repos.json` (`{"initialized_repos": [{"slug": "owner/repo", "path": "<fixture repo>"}]}`) just before the archive step.

### Hazards

- Do not weaken the retirement guards, thresholds or registry checks to make the test pass; the fixture adapts to the production path, not the reverse.
- After layers 1-4 are fixed, later steps (archive, `verify`, restore, source removal, `proof`) have never run; further fixture gaps may appear. Fix those in the same PR if they are fixture-only; file a separate issue if a real product defect appears.
- No new test framework, harness, or CI test gate. Do not add the opt-in tests to CI in this issue.

### Verification

```bash
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && AIDEVOPS_TEST_SYSTEMD=1 python3 <repo>/.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py -v
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py
git diff --check
```

Run the first command on a host with a working user-systemd manager and from a directory outside any canonical checkout. Expected: 25 tests, 0 failures, no leftover `aidevops-worker-fixture*` user units and no leftover `managed-*` temp directories. Run the existing worker-lifecycle unit tests touched by the `cleanup.py` change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both native tests pass on a user-systemd host, through archive, independent restore and source removal.
- [ ] The fixtures use an isolated lifecycle state directory and never read or write the real per-user registry.
- [ ] A missing or unreadable repository config produces a named refusal, not `unexpected-error ... FileNotFoundError`.
- [ ] The default (non-systemd) run of the test file still passes; no guard or threshold is changed.
- [ ] The PR uses `For #35359` (not `Resolves`) for the parent rollout and `Resolves` for this issue.

## Context

Found while running the #35359 step-4 canary on one Pulse host. The result is also recorded on #35359. This issue does not change the rollout status of any host: they stay `partial` until the installed-runtime canary passes.

title: Worktree lifecycle canary defects: producer verify disagrees with archive verify; misleading FileNotFoundError on pre-existing state dir
body:
## What

The installed-runtime canary on #38658 (https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38658#issuecomment-6916380126) found two small, reproducible defects in the worktree-lifecycle tooling. Neither blocks the canary itself, and neither is tracked anywhere else. Fix both in one PR.

1. **Producer verify disagrees with archive-helper verify.** On the same disposable archive:
   - `worktree-archive-helper.sh verify` accepts it.
   - `worktree_recovery_producer.py verify` returns `producer:archive-layout-changed` with exit 1.

   It is not yet known whether this is a caller error (wrong arguments or an unsupported archive type for the producer) or a real layout check that is wrong.
2. **Misleading admission error.** If the lifecycle state directory already exists but is empty, `worker-launch.py --initialize` refuses admission with `reason=FileNotFoundError`. The real cause is that the private-path check expects the directory to be absent. The error text should name that check and the path's state.

## Why

Both cost operator time when a reported failure doesn't match its real cause. Item 1 also means one of two verifiers gives a false negative. Recovery tooling must not reject a valid archive, or accept an invalid one, depending on which verifier the caller happens to use.

## Reproducer

Observed on deployed v3.39.213 in a disposable HOME. Full canary log: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38658#issuecomment-6916380126

1. Producer disagreement: archive a disposable worktree with `worktree-helper.sh remove`, so that it is retired to a compact archive. `worktree-archive-helper.sh verify <archive>` then exits 0, but `worktree_recovery_producer.py verify` on the same archive prints `producer:archive-layout-changed` and exits 1.
2. Misleading reason: `mkdir -m 700 <state-dir>` (empty), then run `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker-launch.py --state-dir <state-dir> --worktree <wt> --initialize -- true`. It prints `admission-denied reason=FileNotFoundError` after about 2 s. Exact flags: see the `launch.py` argparse block.

The mechanism for item 2 has been confirmed from the code (see How). The cause of item 1 has not.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_producer.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/launch_state.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/launch.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`

Details (verify on `main` before editing):

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_producer.py`. Find where `archive-layout-changed` is emitted and compare its layout expectations with the archive helper's verifier.
- READ (reference): `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`, the `verify` / `verify-structure` paths. Treat these as the accepted contract for compact archives.
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/launch_state.py:18` `initialize_or_open()`. If the directory already exists, `LifecycleRegistry.initialize()` raises `FileExistsError`. The function then waits 2 s for "another initializer" and re-raises whatever `LifecycleRegistry(state_dir)` throws. For an empty directory that is `FileNotFoundError`, because the database is missing. Distinguish "exists but empty or uninitialised" from "another initializer is still committing", and raise a named error for the former. Do not repair or replace existing state; that contract stays.
- EDIT if needed: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/launch.py:104-107` (`_run_observed`) and `_reason()`, so that the named error reaches `admission-denied reason=`. CLI entry point: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker-launch.py`.

Steps:

1. Reproduce item 1 in a disposable HOME. Create a compact archive with `worktree-archive-helper.sh`, then run both verifiers on it. If the producer is being called incorrectly, document the correct invocation and make the error message say so. If the producer's layout check is wrong, fix it. Do not loosen verification.
2. Reproduce item 2. Pre-create an empty lifecycle state directory, run `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker-launch.py --initialize`, and confirm that the reason now names the private-path validation failure.

Not in scope (still open on #38658): the 24 h idle-archive receipt, the missing binding under the `pulse` manager override (`AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_MANAGER=pulse-cgroup-v1`), and removal refused with `proc-observation-unavailable` for an exited PID. #38659 covers the last of these if it shows up on production rows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For the same compact archive, both verifiers agree, or the producer's rejection message names the actual mismatch or the wrong invocation.
- [ ] An empty, pre-existing lifecycle state directory produces an admission reason that names the private-path validation failure, not `FileNotFoundError`.
- [ ] Existing suites still pass: the two worktree scripts below, and the worker-lifecycle unittest discovery that CI runs (`.github/workflows/code-quality.yml:744`).

## Verification

```bash
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests -v
```

Run any reproduction under a disposable HOME and worktree base. Never against the production registry.

Ref #38658, #35359.

title: Test fixtures hardcode /usr/bin/true, failing two suites on hosts without /usr/bin
body:
# Test fixtures hardcode `/usr/bin/true`, so two suites fail on hosts without `/usr/bin`

## What

Two test suites hardcode absolute `/usr/bin/true` (and `/usr/bin/false`) as stand-in helper executables. On a NixOS host `/usr/bin` contains only `env`, so those paths do not exist, the fixtures silently take a different code path, and the suites fail with misleading assertions that look like product defects.

## Evidence

Observed while running the focused dependency tests for the Pulse lifecycle rollout (GH#35359) on a Linux NixOS host, aidevops 3.39.212, deployed SHA `0719998ae`:

- `test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`: **98/99**, failing `verified transfer drift is a pre-claim prerequisite with a fail-closed CAS repair`.
- `test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh`: fails `repeated zero-output launches switch to URL-only bootstrap prompt`.

Both pass on hosts that have `/usr/bin/true`, which is why this has not been seen before.

`bash -x` trace of the dispatch failure, with the decisive lines:

```
+ _dsi_origin_identity_prerequisite /tmp/.../repo owner/repo
+ [[ true == true ]]
+ [[ -x /usr/bin/true ]]
+ return 0
+ [[ '' == repository_identity_drift ]]
+ exit 1
```

The gate at `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-origin.sh:85` is `[[ -x "${_DSI_TOKEN_HELPER:-}" && -x "${_DSI_ASKPASS_HELPER:-}" ]] || return 0`. It is correct: it declares itself inapplicable when the helpers are not executable. The fixture is what is wrong — it sets both to a path that does not exist on this platform, so the gate never runs and the expected `repository_identity_drift` is never produced.

`test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh` has the same shape: `/usr/bin/true` is the "snapshot helper succeeds" fixture and `/usr/bin/false` is the "snapshot helper fails" fixture. With neither path present, the success case breaks while the failure case passes by accident, which is the worse of the two outcomes.

**Diagnostic note for whoever picks this up:** `$(command -v true)` is *not* a fix. `command -v` resolves the shell builtin and returns the bare word `true`, so `[[ -x true ]]` is still false and the suite still fails. I verified that wrong fix first. `type -P` forces external-binary lookup and returns a real path.

## Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh`

`.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-origin.sh` is a read-only integration point. Do not relax its applicability gate to make the fixture pass.

## Reference pattern

Replace the hardcoded absolute paths with `$(type -P true)` / `$(type -P false)`.

## Not affected, do not change

`rg '/usr/bin/true'` also matches these, which are inert string literals, never executed:

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh:949` — argv inside a denied-override assertion.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scheduler-dedup-linux.sh` — crontab line contents in fixture files.

The remaining matches in other suites were not individually checked on this host and may or may not belong to the same class.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh
```

Expected: dispatch 99/99 and the zero-output suite exit 0. Both verified locally with the `type -P` change; dispatch went from 98/99 to 99/99.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Neither suite depends on an absolute path under `/usr/bin` for an executable fixture helper.
- [ ] Both suites pass on a host where `/usr/bin` contains only `env`.
- [ ] The applicability gate in `dispatch-single-issue-origin.sh` is unchanged.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean on both files.

## Open question, not in this scope

A gate that self-disables when its helpers are missing is right for dispatch, but it means pre-claim origin-identity drift detection quietly does not apply on a host where the token or askpass helper is absent. I have no evidence that this happens with the framework-provided helpers in production, so I am not filing it as a defect. Worth a deliberate look by whoever owns GH#33629.

title: t19071: fix(pulse): fix-the-fixer detector caches verdicts so hourly runs progress wi...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19071` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-16 | **Started:** 2026-11-16
**Tags:** `interactive` `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): fix-the-fixer detector caches verdicts so hourly runs progress within the 60s stage bound

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `fix-the-fixer detector timeout verdict cache` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: last changes are #38623 (auth capability reporting) and GH#36535 (direct label check); 0 open PRs or claimed issues touch the detector
- [x] File refs verified at `9160ac3864`: `pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector.sh:118` (`_hash_text`), `:476-557` (`cmd_check`), `:559-589` (`_log_run_summary`), `:594-686` (`cmd_run`); `pulse-wrapper.sh:1586-1590` (60s stage bound); `pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh:432-468` (hourly sentinel)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-16
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (productivity mission, GH#38332 follow-up)
- **Conversation context:** a pulse stage-timing audit found that the detector's cold path never finishes.

## What

Each hourly detector run makes forward progress and finishes inside the Pulse stage bound:

1. A completed classification (`YES` or `NO`) is cached per `slug + issue number + sha256(title + body)`. Later runs skip a cached, unchanged issue without an LLM call. An edited title or body changes the hash and is classified again. `SKIP` and `SKIP_AUTH` outcomes are never cached, so they retry.
2. `cmd_run` enforces its own wall-clock budget below the stage timeout. When the budget is spent it stops taking new issues, writes the run summary and exits 0.

## Why

Evidence from one runner (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log`, `pulse.log`, `pulse-wrapper.log`, 2026-11-16):

- `fix_the_fixer_detector` ran 48 times: 26 ended rc=124 at 61-63s (`worker_killed ... reason=stage_timeout_60s`), and the other 22 were 2s warm sentinel skips. **Every cold run timed out.**
- Each cold run classifies a few issues before the kill, but `NO` verdicts are not remembered. The next run re-classifies the same issues first: one managed-repo issue got `verdict=NO` in 4 consecutive runs and another in 3. Issues later in the iteration order are never reached.
- The kill also prevents `_log_run_summary`, so `~/.aidevops/cache/fix-the-fixer-detector-status.json` never exists, and `pulse-check-helper.sh` (`.current_state.fix_the_fixer_detector`) has no evidence to report.

Impact: dispatch-system issues miss the `fix-the-fixer` label and its extra worker observability (t3077), and every hour the detector spends about 60s of Pulse time plus repeated LLM calls with no new outcome.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`. **Tier rationale:** a bounded change to one bash helper, plus extending its existing stubbed tests.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector.sh`
  - Add `readonly VERDICT_CACHE_FILE="${HOME}/.aidevops/cache/fix-the-fixer-verdicts.tsv"`, with columns `slug<TAB>issue<TAB>content_sha256<TAB>verdict<TAB>epoch`.
  - In `cmd_check`, after the title/body extraction (`:519-525`) and before `_classify_via_llm`, compute `_hash_text "${title}"$'\n'"${body}"`. If a cache row matches slug, issue and hash, log `cached verdict=<v>` and return 0.
  - After a `YES` or `NO` verdict, append the row. Write through a temp file plus `mv`, or append atomically, and cap the file at the last 2000 rows. Under `AIDEVOPS_FIX_THE_FIXER_DETECTOR_DRY_RUN=1`, do not write cache rows.
  - In `cmd_run`, read `AIDEVOPS_FIX_THE_FIXER_DETECTOR_BUDGET_SECONDS` (default 45, validated as a positive integer) and record the start time. Before each `cmd_check`, break out of both loops once the elapsed time reaches the budget, then fall through to `_log_run_summary`. Add `budget_exhausted` (true/false) to the summary JSON and the log line.
  - Update the header comment's Tunables list.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector-auth-cooldown.sh` (or the sibling `test-pulse-fix-the-fixer-label.sh`, whichever already stubs `gh` and `PULSE_AI_RESEARCH_HELPER_OVERRIDE`). Add cases:
  - A second `run` over unchanged stubbed issues makes 0 stub LLM invocations (count invocations in a temp file).
  - Changing the stubbed body triggers one new invocation.
  - A stub that exits 2 (SKIP) is not cached, so the next run invokes it again.
  - With `AIDEVOPS_FIX_THE_FIXER_DETECTOR_BUDGET_SECONDS=1` and a stub that sleeps 2s, `run` exits 0 after at most one classification and writes the status file with `budget_exhausted:true`.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh:432` (`_pulse_run_fix_the_fixer_detector_if_stale`, unchanged) and `pulse-check-helper.sh:244` (reads the status file; the new optional `budget_exhausted` field must not break its jq).
- **Writers:** the new cache file under `~/.aidevops/cache/` (already a detector-owned directory, also used for the auth cooldown and status files).
- **Schemas/config:** none. The new env tunable defaults safely.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed via `setup.sh`.
- **Cleanup/rollback:** revert the PR; the cache file is inert without the reader.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- The cache key includes the content hash, so an edited issue is always classified again. `YES` verdicts are cached as well, but the label check (`:501-509`) already skips labelled issues, so a cached YES on an unlabelled issue (label removed by a maintainer) must **not** re-apply the label. That respects the maintainer's removal.
- The budget must stay below `PULSE_FIX_THE_FIXER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (60). Default 45 leaves headroom for the summary write and process exit.
- Keep the explicit `return 0`/`return 1`, `local var="$1"` and named-local argument conventions. The file uses `set -euo pipefail`, so capture return codes explicitly as `cmd_run` already does.

### Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector-auth-cooldown.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-fix-the-fixer-label.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-fix-the-fixer-observability.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-check-helper.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

Post-deploy runtime check: within two hourly cold runs, `pulse-stage-timings.log` shows `fix_the_fixer_detector` rc=0 (not 124), and `~/.aidevops/cache/fix-the-fixer-detector-status.json` exists.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector-auth-cooldown.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-fix-the-fixer-label.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A repeat run over unchanged issues makes zero LLM calls; an edited body is classified again; SKIP and SKIP_AUTH are never cached.


title: Reduce subprocess fan-out in the worktree recovery lifecycle (child of #35359)
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Reduce subprocess fan-out in the worktree recovery lifecycle (retire-plan, retire, migrate, restore)

For #35359. Follows #38659, whose profile is in `todo/research/archive-fixture-timeouts-gh38659.md`.

## What

One `worktree-recovery-lifecycle-helper.sh retire-plan` on a one-file fixture executes about 1,850 processes (strace execve, non-ENOENT): ~680 git, ~320 dirname, ~290 readlink, ~165 python3, ~150 bash, 50-100 jq. `migrate` 5.9 s, `retire-plan` 8.2 s, `retire` 8.7 s, `restore` 2.5 s on that fixture (host load 12.8 of 16 cores). This is why the full 183-test archive suite takes about 23 min and individual cases exceed 60 s on busier hosts.

## Why

#35359 criterion: archive fixture timeouts resolved or tracked. Cheaper passes also let deadline-bounded retention finish instead of returning `classification-deadline-exhausted` with 0 source bytes retired (inferred, not yet measured on a canary).

## How

- Profile per phase with `AIDEVOPS_RECOVERY_TIMING_LOG` (see `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_timing.py`), then remove repeats: `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` / `--git-common-dir` and `config` per path, `worktree list --porcelain` (about 6 per pass), `remote get-url origin`, `branch-has-active-claim` per candidate, and `dirname`/`readlink` re-resolution in shell helpers.
- Likely files (confirm by profile): `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_migrate.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_archive.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-lifecycle-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_git.py`.
- Reference: `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`.

## Constraints

Keep private-ref, process, source-drift and retirement guards and unknown/tracked content protection. Cache only within one invocation; never across a guard re-check. Do not raise timeouts as the fix.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py` finishes in under 300 s; the 3 slowest cases under 10 s each, on the same machine; before/after timing table in the PR.
- `test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py` and `test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` still pass.

title: fix(pulse): partial-continuation reconcile processes one page per pulse visit, so large repos never complete the traversal and merged partials strand for days
body:
## Problem

On a large managed repository (about 180 open `status:in-review` issues), the partial-continuation pass on the stale-blocked cadence has not completed for about 13.7 days (`complete_stamp_age_s=1181714` in the pulse log). Merged worker partials therefore stay in `status:in-review`, still assigned to the finished runner, with no `auto-dispatch`. A read-only survey found more than 50 such issues. In each, the newest ownership event is `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_ready_missing_linkage`, no open PR references the issue, and a merged `For #N` partial exists. The oldest were about 2 days old.

GH#38039 narrowed the listing to label-filtered candidates and kept the stale pass's reserve. It did not change how many pages one call processes.

## Root cause

`_pm_reconcile_partial_continuations` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`) processes **one page** (`PULSE_PARTIAL_RECONCILE_PAGE_SIZE`, default 10) and then `break`s, returning 3. It ignores time left before its deadline. The only exception is the review-to-available phase change. `_pulse_stale_blocked_optional_pass` (`pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`) calls it once per repo visit. With ~19 review pages plus the available pages, a full traversal needs about 20 visits of that repo. With ~80 pulse repos and a shared sweep deadline, the pass reached this repo about 3 times in the retained log window and was deferred the rest of the time (`sweep deadline reached (GH#36041)`). The stamp never completes, so a newly stranded issue waits until the cursor's page comes round, which takes days.

## Evidence

- Cursor file `~/.aidevops/cache/partial-continuation/<owner>__<repo>` was last written 7 hours before inspection and held `3 / phase=review`.
- An operator-run driver ran the same function in a loop until it no longer returned 3, under a 1,500 s deadline. It sourced `shared-constants.sh`, `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` and `pulse-merge.sh`, as `_merge_restore_partial_continuation` in `full-loop-helper-merge.sh` does. Each call returned 3 after one page. Within minutes it logged `returned #N to status:available (auto-dispatch added, released: <runner>) after partial PR #M (GH#34312)` for 28+ issues. Two issues were correctly `kept ... in review` because another open PR referenced them. Every write still went through the existing guards.
- The deployed file matches `main` (blob `a05a3c75ae`).

## Proposed fix

In `_pm_reconcile_partial_continuations`, keep listing and processing pages while `date +%s` is before the deadline, rather than breaking after one page. Keep the existing per-issue cursor persistence, so a deadline between issues still resumes the suffix. Return 0 only when the available phase's last page has been processed, and 3 when the deadline cuts the traversal short. The per-call page cap could become a page budget (for example `PULSE_PARTIAL_RECONCILE_MAX_PAGES`, default unbounded within the deadline) if a hard API bound is wanted.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`

In the script, change `_pm_reconcile_partial_continuations`, at the `break` after a page. In the test file, extend the cursor tests near the `_pm_reconcile_partial_continuations "$SLUG" 2000000060` cases. Add a case where one call processes two full pages when the deadline allows, and one where the deadline stops after the first page and the cursor names page 2.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh`
- ShellCheck clean on both scripts.
- After deployment: on a repo with more than 10 in-review candidates, one pulse visit advances the cursor by more than one page, and the `partial-continuation-complete` stamp age falls below the cadence interval within a day.

title: perf(pulse): stale-blocked sweep still makes at most one visit per pass on large repos after GH#38186; ordinary cursor frozen and one failed read aborts the pass
body:
## Problem

The GH#37965, GH#38112 and GH#38186 fixes are deployed, but on a large managed repository (about 500 open `status:blocked` issues, 13–17 of them ready) the stale-blocked sweep still makes **at most one visit per pulse visit**, and its ordinary cursor never moves. Dependants whose blockers have all closed stay `status:blocked` for days while workers have nothing to claim.

## Evidence (owner pulse, about 80 repos, 15–16 November 2026, after GH#38186 closed on 14 November)

Every `stale sweep repo=<repo>` line in the retained pulse log:

```
candidates=482 resumed_after=19145 pending=359 visited=0 checked=0 prefiltered_open_blocker=0 failed=1 complete=false ready=5  ready_visited=0
candidates=466 resumed_after=19145 pending=343 visited=0 checked=0 prefiltered_open_blocker=0 failed=1 complete=false ready=5  ready_visited=0
candidates=487 resumed_after=19145 pending=364 visited=1 checked=0 prefiltered_open_blocker=0 failed=1 complete=false ready=13 ready_visited=1
candidates=466 resumed_after=19145 pending=342 visited=0 checked=0 prefiltered_open_blocker=0 failed=1 complete=false ready=12 ready_visited=0
candidates=484 resumed_after=19145 pending=360 visited=1 checked=1 prefiltered_open_blocker=0 failed=0 complete=false ready=6  ready_visited=1
```

- `resumed_after` is the same in every pass in the log, so the ordinary lane has made no progress. Even the no-API `prefiltered_open_blocker` count is 0, because the stop-deadline check (`dependency-event-reconciler.sh`, `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues`, the first `if` in the candidate loop) runs before the prefilter.
- 4 of 5 passes logged `failed=1`. The per-candidate `gh api "repos/${repo}/issues/${issue_number}"` read `break`s the whole pass on a single failure, so one transient error ends the pass with nothing visited.
- **The same function given a full deadline** (operator-run, sourcing `shared-constants.sh`, `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` and `dependency-event-reconciler.sh`, with `DER_STALE_BLOCKED_DEADLINE_EPOCH` = `DER_STALE_BLOCKED_STOP_EPOCH` = now + 1500 and `DER_STALE_BLOCKED_READY_MAX=40`) finished in **288 s**: `candidates=517 pending=393 visited=65 checked=65 prefiltered_open_blocker=328 failed=0 complete=true ready=17 ready_visited=17`. Every decision went through `_der_try_unblock`.
- **Budget:** `_pulse_stale_blocked_sweep_deadline` (`pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`) gives the whole sweep `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (60) minus `..._MARGIN_SECONDS` (15), i.e. 45 s across all due repos. A full pass of one large repo needs roughly six times that.

## Proposed fix

1. In the candidate loop, a failed per-issue `gh api` read should count as failed, queue the issue with `_der_retry_append`, and `continue`, instead of `break`ing the pass.
2. Run the no-API prefilter (`.sweep_open`) before the stop-deadline check. It costs no API call and advances the ordinary cursor through issues whose native blocker is still open.
3. Give the ready lane its own bounded budget per pulse cycle, separate from the shared 45 s. For example, `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_READY_SECONDS` (default about 60 s) is spent only on repos whose `.ready` hint (`_der_stale_write_ready_hint`) is non-zero. The ready lane can then visit up to `DER_STALE_BLOCKED_READY_MAX` issues per cycle instead of one. Ordinary-lane fairness across repos stays as it is.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh`

In the reconciler, change the candidate loop in `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues`: move the prefilter, and replace the `break` after a failed read with retry-and-continue. In `pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`, add the ready-lane budget around `_pulse_stale_blocked_run_and_measure`. In the tests, add a case where the stop deadline has passed but prefiltered candidates still advance the cursor. Add another where a failed issue read is queued for retry and the next ready candidate is still visited.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler-partial.sh`
- ShellCheck clean on both scripts.
- After deployment: on a repo with more than 300 blocked issues and ready > 0, `ready_visited` is greater than 1 in a single pass, `resumed_after` changes between passes, and a `failed=1` pass still shows `visited` > 0.

title: Merge gates strand completed worker PRs: silent non_closing_reference_not_open block and prose For #N false positive
body:
## Description

Two merge-gate behaviours strand completed worker PRs in a managed private repository. Both were observed on 2026-11-16 and repaired by hand in an interactive session.

### 1. Silent permanent block for a non-closing reference to a completed issue

`_worker_briefed_link_kind` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process-worker-briefed.sh`, the `issue_state != "open"` branch, GH#33999/GH#38496) marks a PR `non_closing_reference_not_open` and removes it from the backlog count. That is correct when the issue was closed as not planned or superseded. But when the issue closed as `COMPLETED` and the PR records the completion evidence, the PR has no recovery route and nothing surfaces it.

Observed: two data-only PRs (a brief-ledger update recording a passing verification, and a lane-batch work-log record) used `For #N` / `Ref #N`; their issues closed as completed shortly afterwards. Both sat for 1–2 days. One of them held the only record of the passing verification, so the default branch still described a completed issue as blocked. `full-loop-helper.sh merge` refuses them with `Merge blocked by t2449: non-closing reference to issue #N which is not open (GH#33999)`, and the pulse log only ever shows `marked permanently t2449-blocked`.

Interactive repair that worked: confirm `stateReason=COMPLETED` and that the diff only records completion evidence, rewrite the keyword to `Resolves #N` (harmless on an already-closed issue), and rerun `full-loop-helper.sh merge`.

Proposed fix (keep the trust boundary, `#aidevops:trust-boundary`):
- When marking `non_closing_reference_not_open`, post one idempotent PR comment (marker-keyed) and add a discoverable label, so an interactive or maintainer session can find the PR. The comment should state the issue's `stateReason` and the repair options (relink with `Resolves`, or close as superseded).
- Optional: when `stateReason=COMPLETED`, the author is write-authorised, and the PR touches only planning/ledger paths (the same path test as `_worker_briefed_pr_is_planning_checkpoint`), rewrite the keyword and let the normal gates run on the next pass.

### 2. False positive in `_gh_pr_merge_closure_check`

`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh` `_gh_pr_merge_closure_check` scans the body with `(?i)(?:^|[^a-z0-9_])(?:For|Ref):?[[:space:]]+(?:owner/repo)?#N`. Being case-insensitive and unanchored, it treats prose such as `Dates lane batch for #NNN: ...` as a non-closing `For` reference. With a `Resolves #NNN` line further down, the merge fails with `For/Ref contradicts native closing references: #NNN`. GitHub assigns no meaning to `for #N` in prose.

Proposed fix: match only a link-keyword line, for example `^[[:space:]]*(For|Ref):?[[:space:]]+(owner/repo)?#N` (line-anchored; decide whether the keyword stays case-insensitive). Keep the existing fenced-code and inline-code stripping.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process-worker-briefed.sh`: `_worker_briefed_link_kind` and the GH#38496 marker sync.
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`: `_gh_pr_merge_closure_check` regex.
- Matching tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` for both functions; locate them with `rg -l "_gh_pr_merge_closure_check|non_closing_reference_not_open" .agents/scripts/tests`.

## Verification

- Closure check: a body with `batch for #12` plus `Resolves #12` passes; a body with a `For #12` line plus native closure of #12 still fails.
- Link kind: a closed-completed issue with a non-closing PR reference produces exactly one marker comment and label across repeated passes; a closed not-planned issue stays permanently blocked as before.
- `shellcheck` is clean on both scripts.

title: worktree-helper add fails with bare ValueError when a retired worker left a stale lifetime record for the default path
body:
## Problem

`worktree-helper.sh add <existing-branch>` (and `aidevops worktree add`) permanently fails for the default auto-generated path when a retired worker worktree previously used that exact path:

```text
Creating worktree for existing branch '<branch>'...
Worktree ownership transaction unavailable
WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_ERROR_STAGE=lifecycle:begin-create
WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_ERROR_TYPE=ValueError
```

`shared-worktree-create.sh` → `worktree_create_registered` calls `shared-worktree-registry-owner.py begin-create`, which calls `worktree_lifetime_owner.begin_creation()`. That function finds the old row in `worktree_managed_lifetimes` for the path and calls `worktree_lifetime_proof.proof(record, record["identity"]["source_inode"], fresh=True)`. For a retired worktree, this raises `ValueError: no matching sealed generation`. No `git worktree add` runs.

## Observed evidence (read-only inspection, 2026-11-16)

- The default path `<worktree-base>/<repo>-feature-auto-<timestamp>-gh<N>` does **not** exist on disk; the worker worktree was retired days earlier.
- The `worktree_managed_lifetimes` row for that path is still present: `manager: "pulse"`, keys `created_at, created_by, generation, identity, launches, manager, ownership_epoch, schema, state, task`, `identity` keys `admin, admin_inode, common, path, source_inode`.
- `proof(..., fresh=True)` on that row → `ValueError: no matching sealed generation`.
- Workaround that worked: pass an explicit new path under the worktree base directory, `worktree-helper.sh add <branch> <worktree-base>/<repo>-<new-slug> --issue <N>`.

## Impact

An interactive maintainer adopting a dispatched worker's PR branch (the common "continue the worker's draft PR" flow) cannot create the conventional worktree path. The error names only `ValueError`, so the cause isn't discoverable without reading the registry code.

## Expected

When the path is absent and the stale lifetime record belongs to a retired (non-live) generation, either:
1. reconcile or seal the stale record and continue creation, keeping the fence guarantee for live owners; or
2. fail with an actionable message naming the cause (`stale lifetime record for retired path; no sealed generation`) and the supported remediation (registry prune command or explicit alternate path).

Never silently delete a record whose owner may still be live.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_owner.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-registry-owner.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh`

Reference (read, edit only if needed): `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_proof.py` (`proof`) and `.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-create.sh` (`worktree_create_registered`). The existing test already asserts the `lifecycle:begin-create` failure stage; add a case for an absent path with a stale, unsealed `pulse` record.

## Verification

1. Seed a registry with a `worktree_managed_lifetimes` row (manager `pulse`) for a path that doesn't exist and has no sealed generation.
2. `worktree-helper.sh add <existing-branch>` resolving to that path either succeeds after safe reconciliation, or fails with the explicit cause and remediation instead of a bare `ValueError`.
3. Existing live-owner fence tests still pass.

body:
## Problem

`_runtime_path_is_low` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh:75-88`) matches whole paths with bash `case` globs, where `*` also matches `/`. Several test/lint entries therefore classify **runtime source files** as Low when a *directory* name (or any substring) happens to match. Low paths skip the Critical/High `runtime-verified` gate and are dropped from keyword context (`_runtime_paths_keyword_context`, `_runtime_diff_keyword_context`), and `workflows/full-loop.md:147` gives Low changes only direct diff inspection instead of independent review.

## Reproducer

On `main` (`669e0b1`), source `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh` (define a stub `print_error`) and call `_runtime_path_is_low "<path>"` for each path below. Each one returns 0 (Low):

```text
LOW  test_harness/auth.py          # test_* matches a top-level directory
LOW  src/a.test.d/auth.sh          # *.test.* matches a directory segment
LOW  src/auth.spec.d/session.ts    # *.spec.* matches a directory segment

```

title: fix(pulse): GH#38548 enumeration limit halves to 1-2 on fixed-cost timeouts and never recovers, starving a large repo to 0 ranked candidates
body:
## Problem

After GH#38548, a large product repo's candidate enumeration limit halves on every
timeout at the budget cap. On this runner it fell 500 → 250 → 125 → 63 → 32 → 16 →
8 → 4 → 2 → 1 within one day, and scans **still** time out at limit 1–2. Elapsed time
does not depend on the limit, so halving it does not fix the timeouts. Recovery
(`_dispatch_recover_repo_enumeration_limit`) doubles the limit only after 8 consecutive
successful reduced scans. Any timeout resets the counter, so the limit never recovers.

With limit 1–2, the repo's newest issues fill the whole snapshot. Those issues are
interactive, claimed, or held (`interactive_review_hold`, `status:in-progress`,
`status:in-review`), so the repo contributes **zero ranked candidates**. This is the
prefix starvation that GH#38548's recovery path was supposed to avoid.

## Evidence (runner log `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`, 2026-11-16 ~14:30–15:40Z)

- `Candidate repository enumeration limit reduced: repo=<large-product-repo> from=2 to=1 reason=timeout_at_cap (GH#38548)`. Earlier entries the same day show the full halving chain from 500.
- Cache `~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-repo-enumeration-limit/<repo>` contains `2` (successes counter 0).
- First wave: `Candidate repository enumeration unavailable: ... rc=124 budget=15s`, then `Candidate census reused last-good candidates: ... count=1`.
- Refill wave: `enumeration slow: elapsed=16s budget=23s` followed by `Dispatch_max skipped: no ranked candidates (available=21)`.
- `pulse-health.json`: `workers=0/32 dispatched=0`. Supervisor `capacity` printed `26|0|26`.
- At the same time, `pulse-wrapper.sh --command list-candidates <repo> 100` returned 37 issues. About 30 of them are `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` (class `award-enrichment`, tier:standard). None were enumerated for dispatch.
- 393 `enumeration slow|unavailable|budget raised|limit reduced` lines for this repo in the current log.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
  - `_dispatch_reduce_repo_enumeration_limit` (~L630): do not halve below a floor. Suggested: `max(per_repo_limit/8, 25)` or a config key. Also skip the halving when the last reduction did not reduce elapsed time (the cost does not depend on the limit).
  - `_dispatch_recover_repo_enumeration_limit` (~L649): when a reduced scan completes but yields no dispatchable candidates, probe a larger snapshot immediately (prefix exhausted) instead of waiting for 8 successes.
  - `_dispatch_census_enumerate_repo` (~L678): record elapsed time per limit so the reducer can tell limit-proportional cost from fixed cost (this also feeds the bullet above).
- Tests: extend the existing GH#38548 test for this file, if there is one (`git ls-files '.agents/scripts/tests/*enumeration*'`). Otherwise add one focused regression case: a timeout at limit ≤ floor leaves the limit unchanged.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`

title: terminal-blocker-recovery pending: decided human_decision holds starve the queue budget (budget_exhausted every pass)
body:
## Problem

`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` cannot observe a large queue in one supervisor sweep. With the default `BLOCKER_RECOVERY_BUDGET_SECONDS=45`, every pass in a 2026-11-16 sweep ended with `incomplete stage=queue reason=budget_exhausted` and `reason=unobserved_entries`. The seed and holds stages also hit `rc=124` on every pass. One managed repo has 60+ queued entries, mostly `remote_observation` holds that already carry a public maintainer or supervisor decision.

## Evidence (2026-11-16 sweep, one runner)

- Default pass: 3–6 entries checked before the budget ran out. `pending --count` reported 2 entries but printed none.
- `env BLOCKER_RECOVERY_BUDGET_SECONDS=150` pass: about 20 entries per pass, and still `budget_exhausted`.
- About 90% of surfaced entries already had a public decision with no newer maintainer reply. The supervisor's only action was `record ... wake=human_decision`, re-reading each issue by hand. Each one costs roughly 3 GitHub reads in the helper plus supervisor reads.
- `BLOCKER_RECOVERY_DECISION_TTL` defaults to 86400, so the same decided holds resurface daily and crowd out new local circuits (fresh `files_scope_excluded`, `unknown`) that need real work.

## Proposed fix

- Files to modify: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` (queue stage ordering and suppression), possibly `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-holds.sh`.
- Order queue entries so `local` intake and entries without a recorded decision come before `remote_observation` entries whose last recorded `human_decision` is still unanswered.
- For `human_decision` records, suppress re-assessment until a positive wake signal (a new maintainer or OWNER/MEMBER comment, a label change, a revision change, or a policy fingerprint change) instead of the flat 24 h TTL. The policy fingerprint already does this (t19068).
- Reference pattern: the existing `answered_hold` reply detection (GH#38311) and the policy fingerprint suppression in `record`.
- Verification: on a runner with 50+ queued decided holds, one default 45 s `pending` pass reaches every undecided local entry; `pending --count` matches the entries printed.

title: perf(pulse): supervisor-phase active refill never dispatches — inherited cycle budget is spent, pool sits empty for the whole LLM session
body:
## What

Make the Pulse "active refill" work during the LLM supervisor phase. Today it can never launch a worker, so an empty pool stays empty for the whole supervisor session (25-50 min, about every 3-4 h).

## Why (evidence, one 20-slot macOS runner, v3.39.215, 2026-11-16)

- `maybe_refill_underfilled_pool_during_active_pulse` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1874`) runs from the `run_pulse` watchdog loop (`.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh:725`). `run_pulse` runs only from `_pulse_maybe_run_llm_supervisor`, after `_pulse_run_supervisor_phase` has released the instance lock (`.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1761`).
- At that point the cycle has used its wall-clock budget. Cycles take 25-80 min before the supervisor starts (`pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`: 4088s, 4647s, 4832s), and `PULSE_STALE_THRESHOLD` is 1800s. The in-process `dispatch_max` therefore always stops before enumeration:
  - `Active pulse refill: underfilled 0/20 ... runnable=163` → `Dispatch_max skipped before candidate enumeration: cycle wall-clock budget below dispatch reserve (remaining=-3519s ...)`
  - `Active pulse refill: underfilled 4/19 ... runnable=103` → `remaining=-2249s`
  - `Active pulse refill: underfilled 1/19 ... runnable=246` → `remaining=-2853s`, then the minimum-floor refill also logs `remaining=-2856s`
  - That is 3 of 3 active refills in the retained `pulse.log` window, with 0 launched.
- launchd (and systemd timers) run one instance of the Pulse job. While the supervisor session runs, no full cycle can start. The only other refill path is a worker-exit wake, and an empty pool has no worker exits. Slots stay empty until the supervisor ends and the next cycle reaches early dispatch (prefetch alone took 503s in the cycle that started at 14:50Z). On 2026-11-16 the pool sat at 1/19 from about 16:06 to 16:14Z with 246 runnable candidates, and the `daily_sweep` supervisor ran from 15:49 to 16:13Z.
- The in-process call also dispatches without the instance lock and from the supervisor's own runtime bundle. After an activation that bundle may be inactive, which breaks the GH#32546/GH#38627 drain contract.

## Reproducer

1. Let a Pulse cycle run longer than `PULSE_STALE_THRESHOLD` (default 1800s) and then reach a supervisor trigger (`daily_sweep`, `blocker_recovery` or `stall`).
2. While the LLM session runs, leave the pool below the floor-aware target with runnable candidates. No worker exits, so no worker-exit wake fires.
3. `rg -A 6 "Active pulse refill: underfilled" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` shows each attempt followed by `Dispatch_max skipped before candidate enumeration: cycle wall-clock budget below dispatch reserve (remaining=-NNNNs ...)`, and no launch.

## How

Reuse the worker-exit wake path for the active refill instead of an in-process `dispatch_max`:

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh`: `pulse_event_refill_signal` accepts an optional refill source (default `worker-exit`). Add `pulse_event_refill_wake_underfilled` to wake one `--refill-only --refill-source=active-pulse` pass. Reference pattern: `pulse_event_refill_signal` (active-bundle rebase, runtime-transition deferral, wake-lock coalescing). `_pulse_run_refill_only` then takes the instance lock and applies the fresh `_pulse_event_refill_apply_budget`.
- Keep the GH#35349 failed-drain cooldown for the `active-pulse` source. With cron schedulers a full cycle can start during the supervisor phase, and the cooldown (at most 600s) is short compared with a 25-50 minute supervisor session.
- Spawn the wake detached, as the worker-exit observer is spawned (systemd user service, `setsid nohup` or `nohup`). The watchdog then keeps supervising the LLM session, and the refill-only run outlives the supervisor's process group or service cgroup.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` (`maybe_refill_underfilled_pool_during_active_pulse`): keep the underfill and breaker gates and the worker recycler. Replace `dispatch_max` and `_dispatch_min_worker_floor_refill` with the wake, and fall back to the old in-process call only when the event-refill module is not loaded.

## Acceptance

- When the supervisor phase is underfilled with runnable work, an active refill logs `[pulse-event-refill] action=drain_started source=active-pulse` and launches workers. It no longer logs `Dispatch_max skipped ... remaining=-`.
- Worker-exit refill behaviour does not change: same default source, cooldown and pass count. The only addition is a `source=` field at the end of `wake_started` log lines.
- `shellcheck` is clean, and the existing `tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh` passes.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh`
- After deploy: `rg "source=active-pulse|Active pulse refill" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` during the next supervisor phase.
