title: wp-helper.sh --fluent-boards: add an 'add' action to create cards (follow-up to #38593)
body:
## Observed (2026-11-16)

Follow-up to #38593 (merged as #38604). `wp-helper.sh --fluent-boards` can
read, comment on, tick and move cards, but cannot add one. Working a delivered
"Website Setup" board on a WordPress multisite over SSH, two needs came up:

- Checking a card against the live site found follow-up work that belongs on
  the board (here: a listing clean-up found by `wp spd audit` while closing
  "Import the First Listings"). The evidence comment had to say "tracked
  separately", with nowhere to put the new card.
- The board's own cards expect new cards to be added: "Review the Site Before
  Launch" says "Add each fix as a card here", and "Setup Backups, Updates and
  Uptime Alerts" says "Add a card for anything that broke".

The gap is in the helper's scope (#38593 listed only boards, cards, show,
move, comment and check), not in Fluent Boards: owners add cards in the board
UI, and the helper already writes through the plugin's models.

## Proposed

Add an `add` action alongside `move` and `comment`:

```bash
wp-helper.sh --fluent-boards SITE add --board ID --title "Title" \
  [--stage ID|TITLE] [--body-file FILE] --user=ID [--url BLOG_URL]
```

- Create through Fluent Boards' own task model/service with the same hooks the
  board UI fires, so the activity log records it.
- Default stage: the board's first stage. Description only from `--body-file`
  (plain text, same size cap and no-secrets rule as `comment`).
- Read back after the write; exit 1 if the card is not found.
- Document in `.agents/tools/wordpress/fluent-mcp.md` ("Fluent Boards cards
  over SSH" and step 4 of "Work a setup board": follow-up work found while
  checking a card becomes a new card, with the evidence).

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/wp-helper-fluent-boards.sh` (usage, argument parsing)
- `.agents/scripts/wp-fluent-boards-writer.php` (and the entry file's action
  dispatch in `wp-fluent-boards.php`)
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/fluent-mcp.md`

## Verification

- LocalWP site with Fluent Boards: `add` creates a card that shows in the board
  UI in the chosen stage, with the description and an activity entry; `cards`
  then lists it.
- Multisite: `--url` creates it on the right blog's board.
- Hostinger shared hosting (no `proc_open()`): works over SSH, uploads removed.
- ShellCheck clean.

title: hostinger.md: note that website backups are not in the Hostinger API (VPS/DNS only)
body:
## Observed (2026-11-16)

Asked to confirm that a Hostinger Cloud plan website had last night's
automatic backup, I searched `services/hosting/hostinger.md` and
`hostinger-helper.sh` (nothing about website backups), then the published
OpenAPI spec. `services/hosting/hostinger.md` gives the API base
(`https://developers.hostinger.com`); the spec is linked from Hostinger's
endpoint index.

Result: the spec has **no website (shared/Cloud hosting) backup endpoints**.
Matching paths exist only for VPS (`/api/vps/v1/virtual-machines/{id}/backups`,
`.../snapshot`) and DNS (`/api/dns/v1/snapshots/{domain}`). So an agent cannot
list, generate or verify website backups over the API. That has to happen in
hPanel (the website's **Backups** page). Hostinger's own docs page is
`https://docs.hostinger.com/websites/backups`.

Getting to that answer meant fetching the docs home page (about 700 KB of
GitBook HTML) and then the spec.

## Proposed

Add one bullet to `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` near the other
API capability notes (around the "Per-site PHP version over the API" and "SSL
status over the API" bullets):

- **Website backups are not in the API.** Checked against the OpenAPI spec on
  2026-11-16: backup and snapshot endpoints exist only for VPS and DNS. To
  confirm or generate a website backup, the owner uses hPanel → the website's
  Backups page. For an agent-side safety copy before a risky database change,
  use "Database backups without WP-CLI" (or `wp db export` where `proc_open`
  is allowed) into `~/backups/`.
- Optional: document the machine-readable spec for endpoint discovery, so
  agents don't fetch the docs HTML:
  `curl -sS https://developers.hostinger.com/openapi/openapi.json | jq -r '.paths | keys[]'`.

## Files

- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`

## Verification

- `curl -sS https://developers.hostinger.com/openapi/openapi.json | jq -r '.paths | keys[]' | rg -i backup`
  lists only `/api/vps/...` paths.
- markdownlint clean.

title: r914 trust-workflow rollout files auto-dispatch issues on repos it cannot install into
body:
## Observed

`repo-aidevops-health-helper.sh` (r914 trust-workflow rollout) files "chore: install aidevops issue triage gate" on every repo where `issue-triage-gate.yml` is absent, then runs `sync-workflows-helper.sh --apply --install-missing`. On repos where the runner login has WRITE but not ADMIN/MAINTAIN, the sync returns `SKIPPED ... eligibility: insufficient-permission`, but the tracking issue it already created stays open with default `auto-dispatch`. The pulse then dispatches workers that cannot deliver: the change is only a `.github/workflows/` file, which a token without the `workflow` scope (or a repo runbook forbidding `.github/**`) cannot push.

Evidence on one runner (2026-11-15/16): eight such issues across one org and one personal repo; three dispatches each on two of them (two `provider_error` at tier:standard, cascade escalation to tier:thinking, then a thinking-tier run ending `BLOCKED` with `permission_required`; one with GitHub refusing the push for lack of `workflow` scope). The remaining six are `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` + `tier:thinking` and will repeat the same cost.

## Expected

The rollout files no dispatchable issue on a repo it cannot install into.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/repo-aidevops-health-helper.sh`: `_trust_install_one` (calls `_trust_ensure_tracking_issue` before the sync) and `_trust_ensure_tracking_issue`.
- Reference pattern: `sync-workflows-helper.sh` `--install-missing` eligibility filter (archived, inaccessible, non-ADMIN/non-MAINTAIN).

## Proposed fix

1. Before creating the tracking issue, read `viewerPermission` (or reuse the sync helper's eligibility check) and skip with a log line when it is not ADMIN/MAINTAIN, the same way archived repos are skipped.
2. When the sync result is `SKIPPED` with an eligibility or `workflow`-scope reason after the issue exists, apply a durable hold (`no-auto-dispatch` with the reason, and `needs-maintainer-input`) and post one comment naming the human step (`aidevops sync-workflows --repo <slug> --workflow issue-triage-gate --install-missing --apply --issue <N>` from an account with admin/maintain and workflow scope), instead of leaving the issue available.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/repo-aidevops-health-helper.sh`
- Dry run on a WRITE-only repo: no tracking issue is created and the log names the eligibility skip.
- Existing tests for the health helper, if present (`rg -l repo-aidevops-health-helper .agents/scripts/tests`).

title: full-loop merge: prospective TODO guard checks the PR's stale base.sha, so duplicates added to main after the PR opened get through
body:
## Summary

`_merge_guard_prospective_todo` (added for #28639) checks the prospective merge of a PR into its base for duplicate TODO.md task IDs and `ref:GH#` mappings. It merges against the PR's REST `base.sha`. GitHub's `base.sha` is the base-branch commit recorded when the PR was opened or last updated, not the current branch tip. When the default branch gains a conflicting TODO row after that point, the guard merges against the old commit, sees one mapping and passes. The real squash merge lands on the current tip and produces two.

## Observed

Framework v3.39.192 at merge time. The same code is still in deployed v3.39.215 (`_merge_fetch_pr_refs_rest` reads `.base.sha`).

In a private managed repo:

1. An interactive session filed a task issue with `issue-sync-helper.sh push` and opened PR A. PR A's branch adds the task's TODO row (`ref:GH#N`). PR A's `base.sha` is commit B0, which has 0 rows for GH#N.
2. About 6 hours later, issue sync on main committed `chore: sync GitHub issue refs to TODO.md [skip ci]` and seeded an orphan row for GH#N, so main had 1 row.
3. PR A merged about 8 hours after that. The resulting TODO.md had 2 rows for GH#N. The Issue Sync job "Sync Issue Hygiene on PR Merge" failed with `ERROR: closing issue #N has 2 ref:GH#N TODO mappings; expected exactly one`. The task was not marked complete; a completion-bookkeeping PR repaired it by hand.

Reproduction with PR A's own commits:

- `git merge-tree --write-tree <base.sha> <head.sha>`: the merged TODO.md has 1 `ref:GH#N` row, so the guard returns 0.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree <tip just before the merge> <head.sha>`: 2 rows, so `todo_duplicate_report` would return 1 and block.
- After the merge, `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{A} --jq .base.sha` still returns B0.

Caveat: the merge was most likely made with `full-loop-helper.sh merge` (the session read its usage minutes earlier), but I could not confirm the exact path from logs. Pulse's log shows Pulse found the PR already merged. Either way, the guard logic passes this case.

## Second gap (not verified end to end)

Pulse's deterministic merge (`pulse-merge.sh`, log line "Deterministic merge: merged PR") merged two other `origin:interactive` PRs the same day. `rg -n "prospective|todo_duplicate_report" .agents/scripts/pulse-merge*.sh` finds no call to the guard, so Pulse merges appear to skip it entirely.

## Worker guidance

Files:

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-prospective.sh` `_merge_fetch_pr_refs_rest`: keep `.base.ref` from the PR, but resolve the base SHA from the current branch tip, for example `gh api repos/{repo}/git/ref/heads/{base.ref} --jq .object.sha` or the `refs/heads/{base.ref}` fetch already done in `_merge_fetch_pinned_commit_objects`. Keep `.base.sha` for diagnostics only.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` `_merge_guard_prospective_todo`: use the resolved tip for both the merge-tree and the baseline TODO snapshot.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`: run the same guard, or an equivalent, before the deterministic merge write, failing closed.
- Optional, upstream: `_seed_orphan_todo_line` in `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh` could skip an issue that an open same-repo PR already maps in its TODO.md diff. #20484 covered this scenario with a push-time guard only.

Reference pattern: the pinned-evidence fetch and fail-closed handling in `_merge_fetch_pinned_commit_objects`; duplicate detection with `todo_duplicate_report` in `issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh`.

Acceptance:

- A PR whose `base.sha` is behind the tip, where the tip gained a duplicate mapping after the PR opened, is blocked before any merge write.
- A unique stale branch still passes; an unresolvable tip fails closed.
- Pulse's deterministic merge blocks the same case.
- Verification: add the stale-base case to the focused merge tests named in #28639 (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`); ShellCheck the changed helpers.

Related: #28639 (guard added), #20484 (pre-push guard for orphan-seed duplicates), #29454 (orphan-seed deferral for `publication:pending`).

title: aidevops_bounded_operation: say restoration_command also runs after success (abort-only cleanup deleted a good result)
body:
## Observed (2026-11-16)

I ran a one-off remote database copy with `aidevops_bounded_operation`
(`ssh host 'bash ~/copy.sh'`). For `restoration_command` I passed an
**abort-only** script (kill the copy, delete the partial file), because the
tool description reads as if restoration is the remote-cancel path:

> "Cancel ends only the local process group: a remote command started via ssh
> keeps running unless ssh allocates a TTY (-tt) … or the restoration command
> kills it remotely."

The copy succeeded (`process_exit: 0`), and then the restoration ran too
(`restoration_state: succeeded`). It deleted the verified copy. That matches
`reference/context-efficient-output.md` ("An optional restoration argv runs
after every terminal command path"). But the tool description, which is the
text the model sees when choosing arguments, doesn't say restoration also runs
on success. No production harm: the copy was re-run without a restoration
command and verified. It would have been worse if the abort step had been
destructive outside its own scratch files.

## Proposed

1. Tool description (`aidevops_bounded_operation`): state plainly that
   `restoration_command` runs after **every** terminal path, including
   success, so it must be safe to run after a successful command. For
   abort-only cleanup, either omit it and cancel manually, or make the
   restoration command check a success marker first.
2. Optional: add `restoration_on: "always" | "failure_or_cancel"` (default
   `always` for compatibility), so abort-only cleanup can be expressed safely.
3. Mirror the sentence in `reference/context-efficient-output.md` next to the
   existing "runs after every terminal command path" line, with a one-line
   abort-only example.

## Files

- The OpenCode plugin's `aidevops_bounded_operation` tool definition
  (description and schema; path not verified, search the plugin source for
  `restoration_command`)
- `.agents/reference/context-efficient-output.md`

## Verification

- Start `["true"]` with `restoration_command: ["sh","-c","echo ran"]`: the
  receipt shows restoration ran. With the proposed option set to
  `failure_or_cancel`, it is reported `not_required`.
- The tool description shown to the model contains the "including success"
  wording.

title: WordPress multisite domain move: reusable procedure (folder-path and COOKIE_DOMAIN gotchas found on a live move)
body:
## Goal

A reusable, documented procedure (and ideally a helper) for moving a WordPress
multisite network from preview/temporary hostnames to its own domain on
Hostinger shared hosting. Today the framework only has the generic
`wp search-replace 'old.com' 'new.com'` lines in
`tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md` ("Site Cloning") and
`tools/wordpress/wp-cli-reference.md`. A second network on the same account
needs the same move soon, so the steps below were composed by hand once and
should not be reinvented.

## Observed (2026-11-16, one subdomain multisite, 3 sites, 752 tables, ~520 MB data)

Worked well:

1. Pause the per-network cron runner by renaming its `enabled` file (the
   runner prints "paused"); wait with `flock -w 300 runner.lock`.
2. Fresh `mysqldump --single-transaction --quick --no-tablespaces` with a
   temporary 0600 option file built from `wp config get` (works even when
   WordPress cannot boot mid-change), raw then `gzip -1` at low priority, verify the
   `-- Dump completed` trailer and the table count, plus a tar of every file the move changes.
   Copy: 14 s.
3. Read-only pre-checks: a dry run per old host (`--all-tables --dry-run
   --report-changed-only`, ~10-16 s each), and a unique-key clash check (rows
   whose key holds the old host, rewritten key already present).
4. `wp search-replace OLD NEW --all-tables --skip-columns=guid` per host, mapped/template
   hosts first, network host last (~25 s each), then `wp config set
   DOMAIN_CURRENT_SITE`, then read back `wp site list`.
5. Per-blog LiteSpeed purge (never `litespeed-purge all` on multisite).
6. `.htaccess` 301s from each old host (and `www.`) to the new one, excluding
   `/.well-known/` so the old hosts' certificates can still renew.
7. The runner enumerates sites from the DB, so it picked up the new domains
   with no hPanel change; first cycle after resume succeeded.

Gotchas that need to be in the procedure:

- **Folder paths contain the old host.** Hostinger's folder is
  `~/domains/<preview-host>/public_html` and does not move with the domain,
  but a plain host search-replace also rewrites absolute paths stored in the
  DB (here 7 values: `downloaded_font_files` ×3, SEO Pro Stack hardening records, an
  AI Engine settings backup) to a non-existent `~/domains/<new-host>/…`. Fixed by a reverse
  replace of `/domains/<new-host>/` → `/domains/<old-host>/` on
  `wp_options`/`wp_sitemeta`, then a dry run showing 0 for
  `domains/<new-host>` (also check JSON-escaped and URL-encoded forms).
- **`COOKIE_DOMAIN` is computed by core** for subdomain installs
  (`ms_cookie_constants()` → `'.' . network domain`). `wp eval 'echo
  COOKIE_DOMAIN;'` shows a value even when wp-config.php does not define it;
  `wp config set COOKIE_DOMAIN` then *adds* a hard-coded constant (which would
  block per-domain cookies for mapped custom domains). Do not set it; check that
  `wp config get` finds it before changing.
- **`--skip-plugins` leaves rows with plugin classes** ("Skipping an
  uninitialized class FS_Plugin"). After the main pass and wp-config change,
  repeat the dry run *with plugins loaded* at the new `--url` and apply the
  remainder. Some plugins self-heal stored paths on load (AI Engine
  `logs_path`), so a remaining match may be a legitimate folder path.
- Ultimate Multisite domain mappings (`wp_wu_domain_mappings`) and `wp_blogs`
  hold the same host for mapped template sites; both must change together
  (search-replace over all tables does this).
- Local-font CSS files (`wp-content/fonts/*.css`) and per-site analytics
  configs on disk embed the host; grep `public_html` (excluding uploads/cache)
  for each old host before and after.
- An isolation/outbound allow-list constant may need the new hosts so the site's own
  requests to itself (loopbacks) still work.

## Proposed

- New section (or `tools/wordpress/wp-multisite-domain-move.md`) with the
  steps and gotchas above, linked from `wp-admin.md` "Site Cloning" and
  `services/hosting/hostinger.md`.
- Optional helper: `wp-helper.sh --domain-move <site> --map old=new,...
  [--apply]` producing the dry-run report, backup, change, path-repair,
  purge, redirects and verification receipts; with no `--apply` it is read-only.

## Files

- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md` (Site Cloning)
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-cli-reference.md` (search-replace section)
- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` (folder-name-not-domain note)
- New helper path unknown; search `wp-helper.sh` subcommand layout first.

## Verification

- Dry run on a test multisite reports per-host counts and a clash check.
- After apply: each new host 200 over https, old hosts 301 with path and
  query preserved, `.well-known` not redirected, 0 old-host matches outside
  GUIDs, 0 `domains/<new-host>` matches, login cookie domain correct, cron
  runner cycle succeeds, no new PHP errors.

title: worker_lifecycle: typing.TypeGuard import breaks on Python 3.9 (macOS system Python); profile README routine fails every run
body:
## Problem

`agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/pull_requests_graphql.py` line 13 imports `TypeGuard` from `typing`, which only exists in Python 3.10+. On macOS the pulse runs these helpers with the Command Line Tools system Python (3.9), so the import fails:

```
File ".../worker_lifecycle/pull_requests_graphql.py", line 13, in <module>
    from typing import TypeGuard
ImportError: cannot import name 'TypeGuard' from 'typing' (.../Python3.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/typing.py)
[worker-lifecycle] retirement-refused status=unparseable rc=1
Warning: profile publication worktree cleanup failed: <worktree base>/<profile-repo>-profile-readme-<timestamp>
Error: profile publication worktree remains for guarded recovery: ...
[pulse-wrapper] routine <profile README routine>: script exited with code 1
```

## Impact

The profile README routine pushes the stats successfully, then fails at worktree cleanup, so every run is recorded as a failure (65 consecutive on one install) and leaves a detached worktree behind. Any other caller of `worker_lifecycle.cleanup` on Python 3.9 will fail the same way.

Present in v3.39.211 and v3.39.215.

## Fix

Python 3.9-compatible import, e.g.:

```python
try:
    from typing import TypeGuard
except ImportError:  # Python < 3.10
    from typing_extensions import TypeGuard  # or annotate `-> bool`
```

Simplest without a dependency: drop `TypeGuard` and annotate `valid_slug(name: object) -> bool` (line 27).

## Files

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/pull_requests_graphql.py` (lines 13, 27)
- Check the rest of `worker_lifecycle/` for other 3.10+ only syntax (`X | Y` unions in runtime annotations, `match`).

## Verification

`/usr/bin/python3 -c "import worker_lifecycle.cleanup"` (Python 3.9) from `agents/worker-lifecycle/` succeeds; the profile README routine reports `success` and leaves no worktree.

title: stats: idle skipped-creation repos monopolise health-dashboard recovery lane; stale dashboards wait ~44h rotation
body:
## What

The health-dashboard recovery lane is monopolised by idle repositories that the activity guard skips, so genuinely stale dashboards wait a full rotation (~44h on a 70-repository fleet). Any repository whose turn ends in `rc=124` then exceeds the 48h freshness threshold, and `dashboard-freshness-check` files recurring "Supervisor health dashboard stale" alerts. 14 such alerts were open across managed repositories on 2026-11-17, after GH#38631 (PR #38632, released in v3.39.213) was already deployed.

## Root cause (verified on `main`, `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard.sh`)

1. `_update_health_issue_for_repo` (~line 413) calls `_check_health_issue_activity_guard`. For an idle repository whose local issue-number cache file (`~/.aidevops/logs/health-issue-<identity>-<slug>`) is missing, the guard logs `skipping creation for <slug>` (line 181) and returns 1. The caller records stage `skipped-idle` and **returns 0**.
2. `_refresh_health_repo_bounded` (line 630) writes `.attempt` but no `.refresh-state`, because nothing was published.
3. `_health_repo_needs_recovery` (line 576) treats `epoch == 0 && attempted > 0` as "attempted but never refreshed: eligible immediately, oldest candidate" (line 582) and prints epoch `0`.
4. `_apply_health_recovery_lane` therefore picks that same idle repository as the single recovery candidate on **every** pass, ahead of dashboards that are days stale.
5. The idle repository's *existing* open dashboard is never looked up, because the guard only checks the local cache file. It never refreshes either, so the guard also produces its own stale alert.

## Evidence (`~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log`, one operator, 70 eligible repositories)

- One idle private repository logs `Health issue: skipping creation for <idle-repo>` on nearly every hourly pass from 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-17T04:22Z. It always appears directly after the priority repository, which is the recovery-lane slot. Its schedule cache has only `.attempt` and `.stage` files: no issue-number file and no `.refresh-state`. Its open dashboard (labels `supervisor`, `source:health-dashboard`) last refreshed 2026-11-11T08:04Z.
- Other repositories' `.attempt` timestamps span 2026-11-15T09:16Z to 2026-11-17T04:26Z, so a full rotation takes ~44h. Each pass updates only 1–6 repositories before `Health dashboard repository pass deferred: reserved quality/cleanup budget`.
- Repositories that hit `rc=124` on their turn (data-gather, body-publication or maintenance) are not retried for ~44h. Examples still stale on 2026-11-17: last refresh 2026-11-10, 2026-11-12 (x2) and 2026-11-14 (x3).
- GH#38631's escalation does work (`.timeouts` was written after `elapsed=60s timeout=60s` on 2026-11-16T18:44Z). But the escalated budget only applies on the next turn, ~44h later.

## How (suggested)

Files: `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard.sh`; tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stats-wrapper-timeout.sh` (the existing pattern for scheduling and recovery assertions).

1. In the idle-guard path, when the local issue-number cache is missing, resolve an existing open dashboard before deciding to skip. Reuse `_resolve_health_issue_number` lookup semantics without creating a new issue. If one exists, cache it and let the normal idle refresh proceed, so the idle state is published and `.refresh-state` is written.
2. When the guard genuinely skips (no dashboard exists, idle repository), record a distinct schedule state, for example `.refresh-state` = `skipped-idle|<now>`, or exclude `skipped-idle` stages from `_health_repo_needs_recovery`. The repository must not count as "attempted but never refreshed" and must stop occupying the recovery lane.
3. Optional, if it stays within the budget: allow the recovery lane to promote up to `STATS_HEALTH_RECOVERY_SLOTS` (default 2) candidates, ordered by oldest successful refresh. This keeps dashboards that had an `rc=124` turn under 48h.

## Acceptance

- An idle repository with an existing open dashboard but no local cache refreshes that dashboard instead of logging `skipping creation`.
- An idle repository with no dashboard is not selected by `_health_repo_needs_recovery` on consecutive passes.
- The recovery lane selects the oldest genuinely stale dashboard. Verify with a test that has one skipped-idle repository and one 3-day-stale repository: the stale one is promoted.
- `shellcheck` is clean, and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-stats-wrapper-timeout.sh` passes.

## Related

Ref #38631 (escalating per-repository budget, merged in #38632). Ref #37681 and #37676 (earlier rotation and recovery-lane fixes).

title: cloudron-package-monitor: release-parent image gate stalls silently; support cross-repo pinned source images
body:
## What

`cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh upstream` can wait forever, silently, when an upstream release's release-parent image is never built, and it cannot gate on a companion repository's release while the packaged image comes from another repository.

## Evidence (observed 2026-11-17)

- A Cloudron package registered with `upstream_image` (`ghcr.io/<owner>/<relay>`, signer `<owner>/<relay>/.github/workflows/docker.yml`) and tag prefixes `desktop-v`/`v` printed `WAITING <owner>/<relay>: release-parent image ...:sha-bf422ac is not published.` on every run for days.
- Cause: the upstream Docker workflow is path-filtered (`!mobile/**`, `!desktop/**`, ...). The release tag's single parent only touched mobile code, so no image was ever published for it. Later qualified `main` images exist, but `_cloudron_monitor_upstream_image_ready` accepts only `sha-<release-parent>`.
- `WAITING` goes to stderr and the `--apply` routine returns 0, so nothing records that the package fell behind upstream.
- The same upstream moved its desktop app to a separate repository whose releases pin the relay revision in `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`. `upstream_image.signer_workflow` must live under `upstream_slug`, so the image gate cannot be used with the app repository as the release stream; the registration was switched to the app repository without an image gate as a workaround.

## Reproducer

1. Register a package with `cloudron_package.upstream_image` whose upstream Docker workflow is path-filtered.
2. Have the newest stable release tag's single parent touch only filtered paths (no image build for that commit).
3. Run `cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh upstream`: it prints `WAITING <upstream>: release-parent image <image>:sha-<parent> is not published.` and exits 0 on every run, with no issue created, even though later qualified `main` images exist.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-monitor.sh`

## How

File: `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh` (`_cloudron_monitor_upstream_image_ready`, `_cloudron_monitor_upstream_entry`), tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-monitor.sh`, registry docs for `cloudron_package.upstream_image`.

1. When the release-parent image is absent, accept the earliest qualified image (same annotation, provenance and eligibility checks) whose revision descends from the release commit's parent, or emit a durable finding/issue after a bounded wait instead of an indefinite stderr-only `WAITING`.
2. Optional `upstream_image.source_slug` (image repository owner, used for signer validation and attestation `--repo`) plus `upstream_image.source_pin` (`path` + regex capturing a 40-hex revision in the release tag's tree). With these, the gate requires a qualified image whose revision contains the pinned revision.

## Acceptance criteria

- A release whose parent image was path-filtered no longer stalls the monitor indefinitely without a visible signal.
- A release in repository A can be gated on a qualified image built from repository B that contains the revision A pins.
- Existing `upstream_image` configurations keep their current behavior.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-monitor.sh` plus ShellCheck on the helper.

title: fix(headless): escalate repeated model_unavailable backoff instead of re-probing rejected models hourly
body:
## What

A repeated `model_unavailable` rejection for the same model, under the same auth, should back off for progressively longer instead of always restarting at 1 hour. Bursts of rejected launches should collapse to roughly one or two a day, so dispatch slots go to models that can actually run.

## Why (evidence, host logs 2026-11-16T16:27Z → 2026-11-17T04:39Z)

- 58 `model_unavailable` worker outcomes in 36 hours, all on `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` and `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`. Every rejection is a definite pre-generation `400 model_not_found`: "The '<model>' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account." (`isRetryable: false`).
- The rejections arrive in hourly bursts (~16:27, 17:32, 18:37, 19:40, 20:59, 22:00, 23:03, 00:33, 01:35, 02:36, 03:37, 04:38). Each burst is 1–4 concurrent dispatches, and each dispatch tries terra and then sol.
- In `worker-activity-helper.sh summary` (24 hours) the `local-runtime-error` family is the largest failure family: 32 sessions, 27 of them `model_unavailable`.
- The whole attempt is lost. After terra and sol both fail, the attempt ends and the issue waits for a later cycle. Examples: issue-25596 failed at 23:03 and again at 00:33; issue-26433 at 02:36 and again at 03:37. Neither did any work.
- Cause: `record_provider_backoff` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-provider.sh`) always uses `model_unavailable) retry_seconds=3600`, and `backoff_active_for_key` deletes the row once it expires. The next rejection therefore never knows it is a repeat. The entitlement is unchanged: both live rows carry the same auth signature, recorded an hour apart.

## Reproducer

1. Use an OpenAI ChatGPT-OAuth account that cannot use a routed model (here `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` and `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`).
2. Let the pulse dispatch workers on a tier that routes to that model.
3. `headless-runtime-helper.sh backoff status` shows `openai/gpt-6.1-sol|model_unavailable|<T+1h>|<T>|<sig>`.
4. After `T+1h` the row is deleted on the next check, and the next dispatch tries the model again. `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` logs another `model_unavailable`, again with exactly 3600 seconds, and the cycle repeats every hour indefinitely.

## How

EDIT `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-provider.sh`:
- `backoff_active_for_key`: when a `model_unavailable` row expires, keep it as history (return "not active") instead of deleting it. Other reasons, and any auth-signature change, behave exactly as before (delete).
- `record_provider_backoff`, `model_unavailable` with no Retry-After:
  - The previous row has the same reason and the same non-empty auth signature, was updated within 48 hours, and is still active: leave it unchanged. Concurrent launches in one burst do not escalate twice.
  - The same previous row has already expired: double its duration (`retry_after - updated_at`), capped at `AIDEVOPS_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_BACKOFF_MAX_S` (default 86400).
  - Otherwise use the existing 3600-second base.
- New `clear_model_unavailable_history <model>`: deletes `model_unavailable` rows for the model and its `pulse/` key.

EDIT `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-run.sh`: on a successful attempt (`0)` in `_handle_cmd_run_terminal_attempt`), call `clear_model_unavailable_history "$selected_model"` next to `clear_startup_no_model_feedback`. A restored entitlement then returns to the base 1-hour behaviour.

EDIT `.agents/scripts/worker-watchdog-checks.sh` `_backoff_query_db`: exclude `reason = 'model_unavailable'`. The watchdog only checks after 300 seconds, so any running worker's model was already accepted. Today a model-level row such as `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` matches `LIKE 'openai/%'` and can kill healthy workers on a different OpenAI model. Longer backoffs would make that worse.

EDIT `.agents/scripts/orchestration-efficiency-collector.sh`: exclude `model_unavailable` from the "slots lost to rate limits" duration sum. Other models absorb these rejections, so no slots are lost.

EDIT `.agents/tools/context/model-routing.md` (GH#36698 entitlement-failover bullet): describe the escalation, the cap and the success reset.

## Acceptance

- First rejection: 1-hour backoff (unchanged). The first rejection after that backoff expires, same auth: 2 hours, then 4 hours, and so on up to 24 hours.
- A second rejection during an active backoff does not change `retry_after`.
- An auth change still clears the backoff at once (existing test `test_entitlement_backoff_clears_on_auth_change`).
- A successful run with the model removes its `model_unavailable` history.
- The watchdog no longer reports `model_unavailable` rows as provider backoff.
- Existing tests pass: `test-headless-openai-routing.sh`, `test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`, `test-headless-routing-retry.sh`, `test-worker-stall-diagnosis.sh`, and the headless-runtime database and contract suites.

## Verification after deploy

`headless-runtime-helper.sh backoff status` shows growing `retry_after - updated_at` for `openai/gpt-6.1-*`. Over 24 hours, `model_unavailable` outcomes in `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` fall from about 40 a day to about 10 or fewer, and then to one burst a day.
